item.title: The Daily: Red Wings Open Road Trip in Seattle; McKenna Nets Game Winner
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 2026 no. 1 overall draft pick Gavin McKenna squared off with 2024 no. 1 overall draft pick Macklin Celebrini last night as the Toronto Maple Leafs upended the San Jose Sharks 3-1. McKenna scored the game winner for the Maple Leafs, helping the team snap a three game losing streak in the third period of their game against the Sharks. San Jose has now lost two in a row, dropping them to 4-4-1 on the year after losing in the shootout to the in Detroit to Lucas Raymond and the Red Wings over the weekend. The Red Wings begin the first leg of their four game road trip tonight with their second and final matchup of the season with the Seattle Kraken. After managing to rattle off their last two wins at home, Detroit will be looking to even the score with Seattle after losing to the Kraken 6-3 in their first matchup at Little Caesars Arena this year. The Red Wings, still staring down the barrel of Dylan Larkin ‘s looming trade request will be hoping the former captain will start to look more like his old self after having to shuffle their lines around over the last week. Larkin has lost his usual spot as top-line center following a less than productive week from him and his linemates. However, the Red Wings will definitely need depth scoring facing off a Kraken group that managed four goals in less than ten minutes during their last matchup and that has scored 2+ goals in all but one game this year. Having Larkin get back on track would also help incentivize any prospective trade destinations to make a move sooner rather than later for the centerman. In Case You Missed It Eddie Genborg helped a certain former Red Wings captain’s big day go off without a hitch. Former Red Wings defenseman Robert Hagg has found himself suspended in Sweden. The New York Rangers are giving former Red Wings forward Luke Glendening a PTO contract. Red Wings Extra Glendening isn’t the only player from Detroit that New York has signed in the last week. Netminder James Reimer , who spent the 2023-24 season with the Red Wings, has joined the Rangers’ AHL farm club, the Hartford Wolfpack. GOALTENDING HELP COMING TO THE RANGERS ORG 🤝 James Reimer signed a PTO with the @HWPHockey Last season, he posted a 7-4-2 record with the @Senators and appeared in a game with @BellevilleSens , returning to the AHL for the first time since 2010-11 #AHL | 📺 Watch Live on… pic.twitter.com/QmAG5sqbzz — FloHockey (@FloHockey) October 15, 2026 In his sole season with the Red Wings, Reimer played in 25 games, collecting a 11-8-2 record with a 3.94 GAA and .904 sv%. The 38-year-old is on his sixth club in the last five years. Hockey Now Network Pittsburgh Hockey Now: The Pittsburgh Penguins lost to the Utah Mammoth. Former Red Wings top prospect goaltender Sebastian Cossa started in net for the Mammoth, stopping 14 of 18 shots. Chicago Hockey Now: Patrick Kane and the Chicago Blackhawks have a brief hold in their schedule after a bust week. New Jersey Hockey Now: New Jerse

item.title: Mourinho: “Fede and Arda’s best positions? On the pitch”
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - OCTOBER 20: Jose Mourinho, head coach of Real Madrid CF, is seen speaking during the press conference on day ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 at Ciudad Real Madrid on October 20, 2026 in Valdebebas, Spain. (Photo by Alberto Gardin/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of Real Madrid’s Champions League fixture against RV Leipzig on Wednesday, coach José Mourinho spoke to the media and addressed a question on the best positions of Fede Valverde and Arda Güler, saying: “The best position for them is on the pitch. Obviously, they are different players, different ages, different experiences, different qualities, but both have this ability to be versatile, to adapt to different positions. There are players who either play here or don’t play at all. That’s my view, and that’s that. And some are genuine specialists in a particular position. Others aren’t; there are others who can play in different positions. Every match is a match in its own right, every team is a team in its own right, every team is a jigsaw puzzle you’re trying to put together. Often, the combination of right-back and right winger isn’t something you can simply choose. This one and that one, without considering what the two of them can do together. The same goes for the other flank, the same for midfield. For example, the other day we played, as you know, with a different midfield set-up, with one player who is more defensive, more positional, and another who is more creative, with more freedom. There have been matches where we’ve effectively played with two more positional players. In Rome, in the last 20 minutes, we played with two players who were practically free to roam. It depends on the situation. I try to put together the best possible combination to give the team balance and, at the same time, always improve its quality. I still feel that if we’d played in Rome with Bernardo Silva and Arda Güler from the first minute, I reckon they’d have scored five against us because we wouldn’t have had the capacity to hold our own against a very strong, intense side that comes out all guns blazing from the very first minute. There’s a time and place for everything. I try to do things right, at the right time. Sometimes I’ll be right, other times I won’t.” Mourinho on RB Leipzig “Leipzig aren’t the team that suffered a heavy defeat in Munich. They’re the team that beat PSV, who have three points and are determined to qualify. That’s Leipzig. We have, it’s true. We’ve won three matches in quick succession. And in the last one, we won whilst playing very well. They put in a very complete performance. But we must keep going. Just because we’ve won three doesn’t mean we’ll win the fourth. We have to play and win.” Mourinho on referees and VAR “We’ve got a referee tomorrow who won’t take any nonsense. He’s a referee of the highest calibre and with a formidable character. item.content:encoded: MADRID, SPAIN - OCTOBER 20: Jose Mourinho, head coach of Real Madrid CF, is seen speaking during the press conference on day ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 at Ciudad Real Madrid on October 20, 2026 in Valdebebas, Spain. (Photo by Alberto Gardin/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of Real Madrid’s Champions League fixture against RV Leipzig on Wednesday, coach José Mourinho spoke to the media and addressed a question on the best positions of Fede Valverde and Arda Güler, saying: “The best position for them is on the pitch. Obviously, they are different players, different ages, different experiences, different qualities, but both have this ability to be versatile, to adapt to different positions. There are players who either play here or don’t play at all. That’s my view, and that’s that. And some are genuine specialists in a particular position. Others aren’t; there are others who can play in different positions. Every match is a match in its own right, every team is a team in its own right, every team is a jigsaw puzzle you’re trying to put together. Often, the combination of right-back and right winger isn’t something you can simply choose. This one and that one, without considering what the two of them can do together. The same goes for the other flank, the same for midfield. For example, the other day we played, as you know, with a different midfield set-up, with one player who is more defensive, more positional, and another who is more creative, with more freedom. There have been matches where we’ve effectively played with two more positional players. In Rome, in the last 20 minutes, we played with two players who were practically free to roam. It depends on the situation. I try to put together the best possible combination to give the team balance and, at the same time, always improve its quality. I still feel that if we’d played in Rome with Bernardo Silva and Arda Güler from the first minute, I reckon they’d have scored five against us because we wouldn’t have had the capacity to hold our own against a very strong, intense side that comes out all guns blazing from the very first minute. There’s a time and place for everything. I try to do things right, at the right time. Sometimes I’ll be right, other times I won’t.” Mourinho on RB Leipzig “Leipzig aren’t the team that suffered a heavy defeat in Munich. They’re the team that beat PSV, who have three points and are determined to qualify. That’s Leipzig. We have, it’s true. We’ve won three matches in quick succession. And in the last one, we won whilst playing very well. They put in a very complete performance. But we must keep going. Just because we’ve won three doesn’t mean we’ll win the fourth. We have to play and win.” Mourinho on referees and VAR “We’ve got a referee tomorrow who won’t take any nonsense. He’s a referee of the highest calibre and with a formidable character. I can really sense just how good he is and the character he possesses. I don’t think VAR will play a significant role in the match with him in charge. I’m very pleased to have a referee like Kovács for an important match like tomorrow’s.” Mourinho on whether Real Madrid’s aim is to win the Champions League “No. It’s far too early. Real Madrid’s objective right now isn’t to win the Champions League. The objective right now is to qualify. Our objective is to qualify. Then, if we reach the points total that secures our qualification, the second objective comes into play, which is to try and avoid the play-off. The play-off that we had to play last season, two matches that are always tense, full of pressure, and which immediately put you in a knockout situation. You’re either through or out. And these are matches that can be avoided. But, looking at the competition, I get the feeling that we’re going to need a lot of points. A huge number of points to avoid the play-offs. We’ll take it step by step. First, reach the 11 or 12 points needed to qualify. And once we’ve achieved that, because we will achieve it, we’ll go all out to finish in the top eight.” Mourinho on the players spending time at Valdebebas “Look, I’ve stayed here tonight. Yesterday afternoon I slept; I didn’t work. The hours you spend here don’t necessarily mean you’re working. And perhaps you have to bear in mind that a player might sneak off hidden inside a car and you wouldn’t even know he’d left. But, on the positive side, well, I like it. I like that it’s being said, and besides, it’s true. It’s true that this culture of recovery and taking meticulous care of oneself helps; that’s true. It’s also true that Yan always comes in the afternoon with the fitness coach Iván, who looks after him very well, and that he feels great with that personalised care. But for me, the most important thing is that whilst they’re here, there are other people who need to be here too. There’s an overall work dynamic here. The medical department is on hand, and the sports science team is available. No one stays here without one of my assistant coaches being here as well. I really like this overall work dynamic.” Mourinho on untouchable players “Untouchable? I rule that out. I don’t like this concept of an ‘untouchable’ player. What makes a player untouchable isn’t their status, it isn’t the captain’s armband, it isn’t the number of years they’ve been at the club, and it isn’t how much was paid for them. What makes a player untouchable is their performance on the pitch.” Mourinho on the progress so far “We’ve still got a long way to go. We’ve been here for three or four months. It’s impossible to be where we want to be. We must always improve, whether individually or collectively. Obviously, the more I get to know the players and the more they get to know me, the greater the technical and tactical understanding, let’s put it that way, we’ll have, and we’re taking it step by step. I understand that the demands of a club like Real Madrid are the highest possible. The fact that I’ve only been here a short while, though I’ve actually been here for three years, makes me perfectly aware of this, but I cannot lose sight of my direction. We cannot lose sight of the fact that there is a great deal of work to be done at various levels. You’re talking about the tactical aspect. The tactical aspect is an accumulation of experiences, an accumulation of work, and an accumulation of the knowledge a manager can gain about his players. As I said at one of my recent press conferences, I’m not a stubborn manager. I’m not the sort of manager who clings to a single idea and lives or dies by it. And that means I’m always open to analysing, understanding things and seeking what’s best for my team. I’m happy with many things, I’m not happy with others, and we must keep working.” Mourinho on Mbappé and Espí playing together “Difficult. Difficult. From the start of a match, difficult. For both of them to play in a match where we want to play a 4-4-2, well, yes, but a 4-4-2 with the wingers we have isn’t a 4-4-2, it’s a 4-2-4, and with a 4-2-4 I’ve got my doubts we’d win. Timing is another matter. If you’re playing against a team that’s tired, against a team that no longer breaks out of a deep block, against a team that’s no longer capable of stringing together two or three passes, against a team that no longer cares about building play and is simply focused on breaking it down, well, at that point you can do all sorts of crazy things, as we did in Rome. But you have to read the game. The difference between those who comment or write, with all due respect, and the coaches is the same as the difference between me going there to write or comment. I’m sure you’re all much better at it than I am.” Mourinho on Spanish referees “My view is that the president is exactly the same as me. For me, my players are the best in the world, and for him, his referees are the best in the world, and I applaud him for this, because it’s only natural that he defends his

item.title: Duke Slots #2 In Preseason AP Poll
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 8: Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje #30 of the Duke Blue Devils looks on during the game against the Belmont Bruins at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images T he first AP Top 25 Poll came out on Monday, and Duke was ranked #2, behind only Florida. The only three teams to get #1 votes were the Gators (47), Duke (10), and Illinois (2), presumably from some homer reporters. UConn and Arizona round out the Top 5. Also ranked from the ACC: Virginia (#9), Louisville (#11), and Miami (#14). UNC got 20 votes, and Virginia Tech, somewhat surprisingly, at least to us, got 10. Other interesting rankings: Tennessee, in Cameron Tuesday night, is #8, Houston checks in at #10, John Calipari’s Arkansas is #12, defending champ Michigan is #16, Kansas is #17, but that was before the extraordinarily late addition of Trey Kaufman-Renn, and Kentucky is #23. This is also interesting: we think the last preseason #1 team to win the title was UNC in 2008-09. Florida is in a good situation, but Rueben Chiyenlu essentially guaranteed a championship. It’s certainly possible, but it seems a bit premature, if not foolish, to be saying stuff like that. But he could be right. Florida should be really good. item.title: Enes Kanter picks NBA player who called him a ‘drama queen’ as America’s most desirable punching bag
item.description: Photo by Eduardo Munoz Alvarez/Getty Images Controversial former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom is back with another hot take. In the past few months, Enes Kanter has made a name for himself by taking continuous shots at the WNBA. Be it the players or the commissioner, Kanter has refused to back down. As a result, Kanter has made himself an enemy of several outspoken athletes. The list includes Milwaukee Bucks star Kyle Kuzma. After all, Kuzma lashed out at Kanter’s continued disrespect of the WNBA and labelled him as a ‘drama queen.’ Now, Kanter has clapped back at the Bucks star. American sports fans want to ‘punch’ Kyle Kuzma, says Enes Kanter Kanter shared his response during a recent episode of Michael Porter Jr.’s ‘Curious Mike’ podcast, where the former Boston Celtics center passed on a ruthless verdict on Kuz. “If there is one player, if there’s one athlete in America that sports fans would like to punch in the face more than Enes Kanter Freedom, it’s Kyle Kuzma,” Kanter told Porter Jr. He added, “Listen, I look at his tweets, right? I look at some of his takes, and I’m like, ‘Dude, you just got to educate yourself.’ His takes might be worse than his basketball skills.” Kanter did mention that he’s not mad at Kuzma, but he simply wants the Bucks star to educate himself rather than relying on tools to draft his posts on X. Either way, Kanter did take a jab at Kuzma’s basketball skills as well. This will likely result in a response from Kuzma sooner rather than later. item.title: F1’s former fuel flow meter supplier sues its replacement ahead of US GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1’s former fuel flow meter supplier, Sentronics Holdings Ltd, has taken its replacement to court in Texas. The company claims that the sensors now used by every car in the championship infringe its patent. The British company filed the case against German manufacturer Allengra GmbH in the US District Court for the Western District of Texas on 16 October. This comes just days before the United States Grand Prix in Austin. According to the court docket , Sentronics has demanded a jury trial and filed two exhibits alongside its complaint. What are fuel flow meters? Fuel flow meters measure how much fuel reaches each engine, allowing the FIA to police the flow limits set out in the technical regulations. The FIA wants to keep an eye on this, because a change in fuel flow means a change in power produced by the internal combustion engine. According to the complaint, as reported by PlanetF1 , Sentronics was the FIA’s exclusive supplier from 2018 to 2025 before Allengra won the contract for 2026 to 2030 in November 2024. The two companies are now butting heads, as Sentronics claims Allengra’s meters infringe its US patent, 11,391,609 , which was granted to Sentronics in July 2022. The patent, titled "Flow meter", relates to "a method and an associated flow meter for measuring fuel flow rate in a vehicle". It explains that ultrasonic flow meters work on the principle that "the propagation time of ultrasonic signals travelling through a fluid between two fixed points varies depending on whether the signal travels in the direction of flow or against the direction of flow, with signals propagating more quickly when travelling with the flow". Sentronics' method sends pairs of signals in opposite directions and alters their phase to measure the flow. What Sentronics is claiming The complaint says Sentronics’ own laboratory testing in late 2024 confirmed the infringement. It also says Sentronics shared technical details with the FIA under a non-disclosure agreement. As well as direct infringement, Sentronics accuses Allengra of encouraging the FIA and the teams to use the meters in the United States, including at the races in Austin, Miami and Las Vegas. The complaint alleges the infringement was a deliberate choice, adding that Allengra was told about the European version of the patent in August 2025. Sentronics’ lawyers sent a demand letter in April 2026, which Allengra’s US counsel disputed. According to the complaint, the FIA confirmed receiving Sentronics’ earlier notice on 17 September 2025, saying its contents were "duly noted". Sentronics is now asking the court to permanently ban Allengra from making, selling or supplying the meters in the US. Unsurprisingly, it is also seeking damages for lost profits and royalties dating back to as far as 2022. In fact, it wants those damages tripled because it says the infringement was wilful. Sentronics is now asking the court to permanently ban Allengra from making, selling or supplying the meters in the US. Unsurprisingly, it is also seeking damages for lost profits and royalties dating back to as far as 2022. In fact, it wants those damages tripled because it says the infringement was wilful. Will the US Grand Prix be affected? No, the race weekend won't be affected at all as Sentronics hasn't asked for an emergency ban that would stop the usage of these parts as Kimi Antonelli fights for his championship win. The court has been asked to issue a summons, which is a normal step for serving the case. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Chet Holmgren’s bizarre claim about ‘tanking’ teams gets NBA fans riled up
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images Oklahoma City Thunder center Chet Holmgren has been commenting on having to play what he described as ‘tanking’ teams in December. The NBA season is back underway this week and fans are no doubt excited to see their sides in action. However, during a recent interview, Holmgren has suggested he would rather have a night off instead of playing struggling teams midway through the season. Fans unhappy with Chet Holmgren’s ‘tanking’ teams comment As quoted by NBABase on X , when commenting on playing bottom-tier teams in the regular season, he said: “You don’t get extra excited to play a tanking team in December. “A lot of times you’re like, ‘F*** . Why don’t we just get a f****** night off instead of having to play [this team].” A number of fans have since responded to Holmgren’s comments and are not overly happy. One wrote : “Losers mentality,” with a second stating: “Enjoy getting traded to Charlotte.” A third tweeted: “I hate this guy so much,” while another responded: “The dude is begging to be replaced by Mara and be shipped out to the Kings.” “Humble up dude,” responded another NBA fan, with a sixth writing: “This for real? S*** karma about to get you.” Oklahoma are now set to kick off their NBA campaign on Tuesday evening against the San Antonio Spurs and Holmgren is expected to feature. He had a quad issue during preseason but is now thought to be available for the start of the 2026/27 season. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Lisa Blumenfeld/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona are being tipped to launch a new away kit for the 2027-28 season that will “exclusively honor the Los Angeles Lakers, featuring a distinct yellow and purple color scheme.” The latest update comes from Footy Headlines and an “exclusive leak” that claims Barca’s away kit “will pay direct homage to the Los Angeles Lakers.” And here’s a prediction of what the kit may end up looking like: 💣💛💜 𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 – 𝗘𝘅𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝗶𝘃𝗲: FC Barcelona 27-28 Away Kit to Be Pure Lakers Tribute: https://t.co/o0uj2m3DII — Footy Headlines (@Footy_Headlines) October 20, 2026 Barcelona have produced a couple of Nike vs Kobe Bryant Mamba kits, including this season’s black and purple away outfit. The club are now said to be ready to take “basketball inspiration to the forefront” in order to produce an eye-catching kit that will be “pure Lakers.” Barcelona are no strangers to wearing yellow as the club have regularly produced Senyera kits , paying tribute to the club’s Catalan identity, but pairing yellow and purple would be a first. What do you think of the latest Barcelona kit leak? Tell us what you think in the comments below!

item.title: Bayern coach Kompany told to rest: no training and media duties
item.description: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany celebrates while seated on the bench during the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig on matchday six at the Allianz Arena in Munich. (is associated with: «Bayern coach Kompany told to rest: no training and media duties») Karl-Josef Hildenbrand/dpa Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany missed training and will also be absent from the pre-match news conference but plans to be back for Wednesday's Champions League match against Arsenal. Kompany has been plagued by a virus and hip problems and he watched Bayern's 6-1 demolition of RB Leipzig on Saturday sitting in the dug-out, with assistant Aaron Danks giving the instructions. "Vincent Kompany has been advised to take it easy due to a viral infection so will be absent from today's training session and press conference," Bayern said on Tuesday. Danks oversaw training and will conduct the news conference, having also done the latter last season when Kompany was suspended for the first leg semi-final against eventual champions Paris Saint-Germain. Bayern will be without influential winger Michael Olise for the visit of the Gunners and striker Harry Kane urged that others must seize the opportunity. "When one of your key players is missing, you definitely feel the difference. But that's exactly when other players have to step up and make the most of this opportunity," Kane said. "Others can step in and, hopefully, do a really good job." Arsenal last won in Munich in 2013 but beat Bayern 3-1 in their last meeting almost a year ago in London.

item.title: Preview: Dortmund trip next for Eagles
item.description: Preview: Dortmund trip next for Eagles Eintracht are hoping to build on their first home win of the season when they travel to Borussia Dortmund on Saturday – one of the “toughest matches of the season”, but also an “awesome” one. Backdrop Adi Hütter had called on his team to “run until you can’t anymore and fight for every inch” before the home game against 1. FC Köln. The Eagles duly obliged and picked up an important three points with a 1-0 win. Meanwhile, Borussia Dortmund drew 0-0 at Union Berlin and are still without a win since the international break, having also drawn 2-2 against Werder Bremen in the league as well as suffering a 1-0 defeat at FK Bodö Glimt in the UEFA Champions League. BVB are in European action again on Tuesday at Sabah FK before the meeting with Eintracht on Saturday evening (24 October, 18:30 CEST). ‘Throw everything at it again’ “We have to throw everything at it again in Dortmund,” stated captain Robin Koch, who was a tackling titan against Köln, winning 19 of 22 direct duels – on the ground and in the air. “We showed how we need to perform against Köln. Dortmund away will certainly be one of the toughest matches of the season – but it’s always an awesome match, too.” Looking back Eintracht haven’t had much to show for their trips to Dortmund in recent years. In fact, the Black and Yellows have won 14 of their last 15 Bundesliga home matches against Frankfurt. Only in April 2021 did the Eagles emerge victorious after a 2-1 win – coached at that time by Hütter. BVB have kept a clean sheet in four of their six league games in 2026/27 and conceded four goals overall, the fewest in the league. Both goalkeepers, Noah Atubolu and Gregor Kobel, registered shutouts on the last matchday. “We keep going and want to have more clean sheets,” highlighted Eintracht keeper Atubolu ahead of the outing in Dortmund. Another one would do very nicely on Saturday evening at Signal-Iduna-Park.

item.title: PSG vs Barcelona Preview: Can the Champions End Barca’s Perfect Run?
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain's French forward #10 Ousmane Dembele celebrates after scoring his team's second goal during the French L1 football match between RC Strasbourg Alsace and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) at the Stade de la Meinau in Strasbourg, eastern France, on October 17, 2026. (Photo by ROMEO BOETZLE / AFP via Getty Images) Getty Barcelona's German head coach Hansi Flick (C) addresses his players while taking part in a training session at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 19, 2026, on the eve of the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) Getty Two of Europe’s most electric teams collide at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday night in a Champions League league-phase heavyweight. Both PSG and Barcelona sit on six points from two games with identical +7 goal differences. Kick-off is 9:00 p.m. local time (3:00 p.m. ET). PSG are the reigning champions. Barcelona arrive on an 11-match winning streak across all competitions and the most feared attack on the continent, fresh off a 5-2 demolition of Real Betis. Something has to give. PSG vs Barcelona Preview: The Team News Story Nobody’s Telling Here’s the irony buried in PSG’s build-up: Luis Enrique rested a host of key players, including Ousmane Dembélé, Vitinha, Achraf Hakimi, Marquinhos and Désiré Doué, for Saturday’s 3-1 win over Strasbourg , specifically to protect bodies for Barcelona. Nuno Mendes got injured anyway, picking up a thigh problem as a second-half substitute and now facing several weeks out, a cruel twist given he’d also been rested the week before against Le Mans. Lucas Digne, PSG’s summer signing, is expected to deputize at left-back, a tough ask given Mendes had previously had real success one-on-one against Lamine Yamal. Senny Mayulu (thigh) and young goalkeeper Alessandro Longoni also missed the Strasbourg win, though Mayulu is back in full training. There’s a detail that complicates PSG’s “fresher and stronger” narrative, too: they’ve kept just one clean sheet in 10 matches this season and have conceded in each of their last four games. This isn’t a team with nothing to worry about defensively, it’s a team that’s been winning shootouts, not clean sweeps. One player relishing the occasion either way is Ferran Torres, the former Barcelona forward now leading PSG with seven goals in all competitions, including an opening-day Champions League hat-trick against this exact opponent group. Barcelona’s injury list is the headline, and it’s a real one. Eric García is out three to four weeks with a thigh injury, Jules Koundé misses out with an ankle sprain, and Andreas Christensen remains unavailable, leaving Hansi Flick with very thin options at centre-back . On the plus side, both Raphinha and Frenkie de Jong are back and available, Raphinha after recovering from his own muscle issue and featuring off the bench against Betis, de Jong returning from the knee injury

(Photo by ROMEO BOETZLE / AFP via Getty Images) Getty Barcelona's German head coach Hansi Flick (C) addresses his players while taking part in a training session at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 19, 2026, on the eve of the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) Getty Two of Europe’s most electric teams collide at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday night in a Champions League league-phase heavyweight. Both PSG and Barcelona sit on six points from two games with identical +7 goal differences. Kick-off is 9:00 p.m. local time (3:00 p.m. ET). PSG are the reigning champions. PSG vs Barcelona Preview: The Team News Story Nobody’s Telling Here’s the irony buried in PSG’s build-up: Luis Enrique rested a host of key players, including Ousmane Dembélé, Vitinha, Achraf Hakimi, Marquinhos and Désiré Doué, for Saturday’s 3-1 win over Strasbourg , specifically to protect bodies for Barcelona. Nuno Mendes got injured anyway, picking up a thigh problem as a second-half substitute and now facing several weeks out, a cruel twist given he’d also been rested the week before against Le Mans. Lucas Digne, PSG’s summer signing, is expected to deputize at left-back, a tough ask given Mendes had previously had real success one-on-one against Lamine Yamal. Senny Mayulu (thigh) and young goalkeeper Alessandro Longoni also missed the Strasbourg win, though Mayulu is back in full training. There’s a detail that complicates PSG’s “fresher and stronger” narrative, too: they’ve kept just one clean sheet in 10 matches this season and have conceded in each of their last four games. This isn’t a team with nothing to worry about defensively, it’s a team that’s been winning shootouts, not clean sweeps. One player relishing the occasion either way is Ferran Torres, the former Barcelona forward now leading PSG with seven goals in all competitions, including an opening-day Champions League hat-trick against this exact opponent group. Barcelona’s injury list is the headline, and it’s a real one. Eric García is out three to four weeks with a thigh injury, Jules Koundé misses out with an ankle sprain, and Andreas Christensen remains unavailable, leaving Hansi Flick with very thin options at centre-back . On the plus side, both Raphinha and Frenkie de Jong are back and available, Raphinha after recovering from his own muscle issue and featuring off the bench against Betis, de Jong returning from the knee injury that cost him the World Cup. Getty Barcelona’s German head coach Hansi Flick (C) addresses his players while taking part in a training session at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 19, 2026, on the eve of the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) What to Expect This has the ingredients of a classic, and for once the data agrees: Opta’s supercomputer gives PSG just a 39.7% chance of winning against Barcelona’s 37.7%, with a 22.6% chance of a draw, essentially a coin flip. Barcelona’s high line and relentless pressing have torn teams apart all season, but they’ve rarely faced an attack this clinical, and PSG’s own defense has rarely faced an attack this good either. History leans Parisian: PSG’s 2-1 win in this exact fixture last season was Barcelona’s only defeat in the meeting since the famous 2017 “Remontada” comeback. Expect an open, high-tempo match with real chances at both ends rather than a cagey, low-event European night. Prediction: PSG 3-2 Barcelona Barcelona’s incredible streak ends in Paris, but only just. PSG’s attacking talent and extra rest should be enough to edge a genuine thriller, though their own leaky defense means this is far from the safe home banker some will treat it as. Expect an absorbing, high-scoring contest that lives up to the billing, with the home side shading it late. How to Watch Region Channel USA Paramount+ (English); TUDN, UniMás, ViX (Spanish) UK TNT Sports 2 Canada DAZN Australia Stan Sport France Canal+ Foot Spain Movistar+ Liga de Campeones 4 This article was originally published on HEAVY The post PSG vs Barcelona Preview: Can the Champions End Barca’s Perfect Run? appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ESPN, Disney tease bonkers Star Wars-themed Super Bowl alt broadcast
item.description: ESPN, Disney tease bonkers Star Wars-themed Super Bowl alt broadcast appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ahead of the first ESPN Super Bowl broadcast in 2027, another alternate broadcast, which will be inspired by Disney ’s Star Wars, has been announced. ESPN has announced the “ Star Wars Funday Football” alternate broadcast for Super Bowl 61, which airs on Valentine’s Day (Feb. 14) next year. A teaser was released featuring C-3PO and R2-D2 walking through the desert. Once again, C-3PO is displeased with getting into another “mess.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “How did we get into this mess?” he asks R2-D2. “Seems we are made to suffer. It’s our lot in life.” R2-D2 begins chirping, telling his friend that they are Super Bowl-bound. C-3PO is happy with the news, admitting that he is “ready for some football.” The “Funday Football” alternate broadcast will be aired on Disney+, Disney Channel, Disney XD, and the ESPN app. So, viewers will have several different ways of tuning in. According to the press release, the “Funday Football” broadcast will “recreate every play” of the game in real time, “transforming players on the field into animated avatars.” Various Star Wars characters will “sub in during key moments,” and there will be Easter eggs to look out for throughout the game. ESPN and Disney will have another special NFL collaboration before Super Bowl 61 Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The collaborations between ESPN/Disney and the NFL will begin before Super Bowl 61. Starting during the Monday Night Football game on Oct. 26 between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles, Darth Vader will be interviewing a player from the game on SportsCenter+. Additionally, starting on Oct. 20, SportsCenter on Disney+ will feature “Hyperspace Highlights, which are Star Wars-themed highlights from Monday Night Football. ESPN is going all out for its first Super Bowl broadcast. Of course, Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters, and Laura Rutledge will call the traditional broadcast on ESPN, ABC, and Disney+. Peyton and Eli Manning will also host a ManningCast live from Los Angeles, California. Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged Related: Troy Aikman drops wild anti-analytics take during 49er-Commanders MNF tilt

item.title: SEC All-American Xavier Atkins no longer at Auburn, announces transfer plans
item.description: SEC All-American linebacker Xavier Atkins is no longer listed on Auburn’s 2026 roster and has been dismissed from the team, according to reports . It was announced last week, ahead of the Tigers’ game against Georgia, that Atkins would miss the game due to a disciplinary issue. But head coach Alex Golesh declined to share what happened for Atkins to miss one of Auburn’s biggest games of the season. “We’ll keep it in house. That’ll be the only piece of it that I will be addressing. He won’t be available for us this week for the game,” Golesh said before the Georgia game. The Tigers would go on to upset Georgia , 27-24, and on Monday, Golesh said they were still working through whatever happened with Atkins. “We’re still working through it. I don’t have an update right now,” Golesh said. MORE: College football overreactions after Week 7: Texas’ CFP bid is all but over Atkins makes transfer portal plans known Sep 5, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Auburn Tigers linebacker Xavier Atkins (17) reacts after a missed field goal against the Baylor Bears in the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) While we still don’t know what Atkins might’ve done to sit the Georgia game and then get dismissed, the star linebacker did post on his X account to announce he would be entering the transfer portal once the timing was right. “I have nothing but respect Auburn University and will continue to support my teammates this season. My focus is on my health, my family, and on finishing up the academic semester strong, and I’ll be entering the transfer portal at the appropriate time,” Atkins wrote on his X post . Atkins was second on the team this season with 37 tackles. He also had 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks, along with one interception. There is no doubt that Atkins will be a sought-after linebacker target once the transfer portal opens. Last season, Atkins had 84 tackles, 17 tackles for loss, and nine sacks for Auburn. He was in his junior season with the Tigers and will have two more years of eligibility with the new 5-for-5 rule. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Google Cloud outage: Problems reported at banks, Revolut, Rightmove and court video cameras – business live
item.description: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news, as Google suffers a a major Cloud outage in its London region The pound has rallied after Britain’s unemployment rate fell unexpectedly this morning to 4.7%. Sterling has gained half a cent against the US dollar to $1.3352, as the City welcomes the news that employment rose in the last quarter. “This data has caught the market on the hop, with traders scrambling to respond and boost exposure to the pound. Good news has been a touch more prevalent for the UK of late, which is just the kind of framing the government needs heading into the budget, though signs of more resilience in the labour market do of course mean the BoE has more room to respond to higher inflation.” “The labour market remains relatively flat overall. This resilience in the face of headwinds driven by global events is welcome. But underlying problems remain, with around one million young people not in education, employment or training and overall employment more than two million short of the Government’s 80% employment rate target. To fix those challenges we need to change the benefit system so it offers active help to all who need it, but also make it easier for employers to create jobs. “ Continue reading...

item.title: Iowa high school football schedule Week 9: Every IHSAA game
item.description: It is time for Week 9 of high school football in the state of Iowa for the 2026 season. The final week of the regular season involves potentially exciting games featuring teams from the metro. This week is headlined by Class 4A No. 7 Ballard at No. 3 Carlisle and 5A No. 6 Indianola at Urbandale. Ballard's Blakely Carlson and Carlisle's Hayden Schulte are the top two receivers in 2A District 5. Carlisle's rushing attack and potent defense could prove to be the difference, but if it comes down to the wire Ballard features one of the state's best kickers in Sam Hoffman. Indianola heads into Week 9 on a six-game winning streak. The Indians feature an excellent quarterback in Nolan Freeman and a balanced receiving corps. Urbandale has won its last five games. The J-Hawks feature a stout defense that just posted a shutout against Norwalk, and quarterback Landon Rinnan is a dual-threat weapon with 1,266 yards and 13 touchdowns passing and 790 yards and 12 scores on the ground. Other top metro games involving 5A schools include: No. 1 Johnston at Des Moines Roosevelt, Des Moines East at No. 2 Southeast Polk, Marshalltown at No. 3 Dowling Catholic, Council Bluffs Lincoln at No. 4 Ankeny, No. 7 Valley at Des Moines Lincoln, Norwalk at No. 8 Waukee Northwest, No. 9 Waukee at Waterloo West and Cedar Rapids Kennedy at No. 10 Dallas Center-Grimes. In 4A, No. 10 North Polk hosts Gilbert, and in 3A No. 3 Des Moines Christian hosts Winterset. The playoffs for Classes 2A, 1A, A and 8-player football begin on Oct. 23. In the 2A first round, No. 2 Van Meter hosts Albia and Grand View Christian is at Roland-Story. In Class A, Martensdale St. Marys is at ACGC. item.title: Iowa Hawkeyes Halfway Point Report Card
item.description: SEATTLE, WA - OCTOBER 09: Head coach Kirk Ferentz of the Iowa Hawkeyes leads his team out before a game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and Washington Huskies on October 9, 2026 at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Henry Rodenburg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’re officially at the midway point of the 2026 season with the Hawkeyes sitting at 5-1 overall, 2-1 in the Big Ten and ranked 15th in the nation. At the outset of the year, virtually every Iowa fan would have signed up for that through six weeks. Getting to that point has come with some twists and turns, however. Starting the year 3-0 came as little surprise. Struggling at home against an Iowa State team in a full rebuild was, and it was reason for some concern. Then came the trip north to Ann Arbor and a ranked win over Michigan. While that one was picked by some given the coaching change for the Wolverines, it was the way Hank Brown led the offense down the field for a game-winning drive on the road that spurred optimism for this season. It also set the table for upside in what was widely considered the most difficult three game stretch of the season. The Hawkeyes returned home and were blasted by Ohio State, as virtually everyone expected pre-season. That left us with the question of whether this team was simply a solid one that could perform well against inferior competition and would struggle with real opponents. While that question remains largely unanswered, the response from the Hawkeyes in their road trip to Washington raised both the floor and the ceiling on this season’s potential. Iowa dominated as a road dog west of the Rockies in a way we haven’t seen an Iowa offense do in quite some time. The defense dominated in a way we weren’t sure whether we could count on. The result was a whole lot of fun and the end of that difficult three-game gauntlet better than most could have expected. So where do things stand at the midway point in this season? Let’s dive in. The Offense Six games in, Iowa’s offense is averaging 31 points a game, good for 61st nationally. They’re 62nd in total offense at 403.2 yards per game. They’re 93rd in passing offense at 209.2 yards per game and 35th in rushing offense at 194.0 yards per game. Those are winning numbers for the Hawkeyes, but some skepticism remains. item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WA - OCTOBER 09: Head coach Kirk Ferentz of the Iowa Hawkeyes leads his team out before a game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and Washington Huskies on October 9, 2026 at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Henry Rodenburg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’re officially at the midway point of the 2026 season with the Hawkeyes sitting at 5-1 overall, 2-1 in the Big Ten and ranked 15th in the nation. At the outset of the year, virtually every Iowa fan would have signed up for that through six weeks. Getting to that point has come with some twists and turns, however. Starting the year 3-0 came as little surprise. Struggling at home against an Iowa State team in a full rebuild was, and it was reason for some concern. Then came the trip north to Ann Arbor and a ranked win over Michigan. While that one was picked by some given the coaching change for the Wolverines, it was the way Hank Brown led the offense down the field for a game-winning drive on the road that spurred optimism for this season. It also set the table for upside in what was widely considered the most difficult three game stretch of the season. The Hawkeyes returned home and were blasted by Ohio State, as virtually everyone expected pre-season. That left us with the question of whether this team was simply a solid one that could perform well against inferior competition and would struggle with real opponents. While that question remains largely unanswered, the response from the Hawkeyes in their road trip to Washington raised both the floor and the ceiling on this season’s potential. Iowa dominated as a road dog west of the Rockies in a way we haven’t seen an Iowa offense do in quite some time. The defense dominated in a way we weren’t sure whether we could count on. The result was a whole lot of fun and the end of that difficult three-game gauntlet better than most could have expected. So where do things stand at the midway point in this season? Let’s dive in. The Offense Six games in, Iowa’s offense is averaging 31 points a game, good for 61st nationally. They’re 62nd in total offense at 403.2 yards per game. They’re 93rd in passing offense at 209.2 yards per game and 35th in rushing offense at 194.0 yards per game. Those are winning numbers for the Hawkeyes, but some skepticism remains. A lot of work has been done against the softer competition on the schedule. Against NIU and UNI, the offense averaged 573.5 yards and 47.5 points – both would be top-15 marks. Against the likes of Iowa State, Michigan and Ohio State, the numbers were an abysmal 269.0 yards and 16.7 points – both would be bottom-10 marks nationally. Washington was the first power-conference opponent Iowa cracked 300 yards or 21 points against all season. That one game dragged the P4 averages up to 318.0 yards and 22.75 points. Still not glamorous, but the trend line finally points the right direction and it bent on the road with Jeremy Hecklinski making his first career start behind an offensive line that didn’t allow a sack. A reason for optimism for Hawkeye fans is the efficiency underlying the numbers. Iowa has allowed 5 sacks all season, tied for 10th fewest in the country and has given the ball away just 3 times in 6 games. The Hawkeyes are completing 62.6% of their passes collectively, 81st nationally while the passing attack is averaging 7.0 yards per attempt. Midseason Grade: C+ The Defense Through six games, Iowa is 8th nationally in scoring defense at 14.5 points per game and 22nd in total defense at 293.3 yards per game allowed. Up front is where it gets really loud: the run defense sits 7th nationally at 84.7 yards a game, 2.51 a carry and exactly one rushing touchdown allowed all season. In their last outing, Iowa gave up -3 rushing yards on 25 carries, marking just the second time in the Ferentz era the Hawkeyes have held an opponent to negative rushing for a full game (Kent State 2004). Opponents are converting a third of their third downs (38th nationally), the turnover margin sits at a modest +2 and the red zone defense ranks 29th. Meanwhile, the pass rush has quietly stacked 19 sacks, tied for 6th in the country. The quiet part is driven by the variety of guys working together to make that happen. Iowa’s leader in sacks is Joseph Anderson at 3.0. Preston Ries and Bryce Hawthorne each have 2.5 while Jayden Montgomery and Cam Buffington both have 2.0. Pressure comes from everywhere, which means offenses can’t slide protection toward any one problem. While Iowa has shown the ability to get to the QB, the pass defense looks worse on paper than it has been. They come in at 68th nationally allowing 208 yards per game. That will happen when you face Ohio State and the best receiver in the country. It’s the one number on the sheet which points the wrong way, and we’ll get more into it momentarily. Like the offense, the defense has certainly made a lot of its hay against weaker competition. Every single point Iowa has allowed this season came from a power-conference opponent. Both tune-up games ended in shutouts – 137.5 yards a game allowed, zero points, with NIU held to 7 rushing yards in the opener. Against the four P4 opponents, the numbers are mortal: 21.75 points and 371.25 a game, with Michigan (429 yards) and Ohio State (484) both moving it more than anyone in black and gold enjoyed watching. But last week mattered, because Washington was the first P4 game where the front seven flatly dominated. And the schedule’s remaining offenses look a lot more like Washington’s than Ohio State’s. Now, about that number pointing the wrong way: Iowa is 68th in passing yards allowed at and the last three opponents threw for 276, 324 and 320. Some of that is structural – teams abandon the run against Iowa because the run stops working and Washington’s 320 came largely after the game was 27-0. But Michigan’s and Ohio State’s totals came in competitive football and nine passing touchdowns allowed in six games isn’t the Parker standard. Again, thankfully most of the rest of the schedule looks little like the Buckeyes, but there is some cause for concern in the secondary if you’re picking nits. So, where does 14.5 a game sit in the Phil Parker catalog? Right in the penthouse. The 2023 defense, the one that dragged a 15-points-a-game offense to 10 wins, finished the year 4th nationally at 14.8. The 2021 West champs allowed 19.2 (13th), and the 2015 group entered the Rose Bowl ranked 15th at 18.5. This unit is currently tracking ahead of all of them, with the cupcake caveat fully acknowledged. Midseason Grade: A- Second-Half To-Do List So we have a middling offense that is trending the right way, elite ball security and a defense allowing 14.5 points a game. That’s a formula this program knows by heart. Now, what does a strong second half look like from here? The honest answer is something boring. Iowa doesn’t need 41 a week like they got at Washington. It needs the P4 average to live in the mid-20s instead of the mid-teens, the run game to stay ahead of schedule as they did last week and the quarterback (whichever one trots out at Minnesota) to keep the giveaway count microscopic. The defense handles the rest. That’s how 5-1 becomes 11-1, and 11-1 teams don’t sweat Selection Sunday. The fanbase is a skeptical they’ll be able to stick to the script. We asked for updated projects on the full season during the bye and 74% of you think the Hawkeyes will drop one somewhere down the stretch. The most common response was 10-2, indicating they’ll drop just one. That leaves 27% of the fanbase that thinks Iowa will fall at least two more times this season. History tells us that’s probably true and the math points that direction as well. But it’s hard not to daydream about running the table, and there too the statistics say it’s certainly plausible. The 2009 Orange Bowl team averaged 23.2 points per game. The 2021 Big Ten West champs averaged 23.4 on 303.7 yar

item.title: Iowa high school football schedule Week 9. Every Ames-area IHSAA game
item.description: It's Week 9 of the 2026 Iowa high school football season , and five of the seven teams from the Ames area will be in action. Ames gets to play a day early when the Little Cyclones travel to Sioux City on Oct. 22 to face the Class 5A No. 5 Sioux City East Black Raiders. On Oct. 23 Ballard, the No. 7 team in 4A, goes on the road to face No. 3 Carlisle and Gilbert is at No. 10 North Polk in a pair of 4A District 5 showdowns. Nevada ends its season on Oct. 23 with a home game against Knoxville. Roland-Story beings 2A playoff competition on Oct. 23 by hosting Grand View Christian in a first round game at Story City. The Ames area's two 8-player programs, Collins-Maxwell and Colo-NESCO, both concluded their seasons last week. Here is what is in store for Week 9 of high school football games in the Ames area. Ames-area Iowa high school football schedule, Week 9 Thursday, Oct. 22 Class 5A No. 5 Sioux City East vs. Ames, 7 p.m. at Elwood Olsen Stadium in Sioux City Friday, Oct. 23 Class 2A football playoff first round: Roland-Story vs. Grand View Christian, 7 p.m. at Kerry Van Winkel Field in Story City Class 4A No. 3 Carlisle vs. No. 7 Ballard, 7 p.m. at the Carlisle High School Stadium in Carlisle Class 4A No. 10 North Polk vs. Gilbert, 7 p.m. at Comet Field in Alleman Nevada vs. Knoxville, 7 p.m. at Cub Stadium in Nevada Joe Randleman covers high school sports for the Ames Tribune. item.title: How should the Detroit Lions handle Cade Mays’ return?
item.description: Jun 17, 2026; Detroit, MI, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) gets ready to take a snap from center Cade Mays (64) during the Detroit Lions veteran’s minicamp at the Allen Park Training Facility. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Monday, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell announced the impending return of two key players. Barring some unforeseen setback, starting center Cade Mays and safety Brian Branch will make their 2026 debuts on Sunday afternoon against the Green Bay Packers. For Branch, his return is pretty simple. While it sounds like the Lions will limit his reps a bit, Campbell seemed confident the Pro Bowl safety can take on a significant role, and his presence will be welcomed in a secondary that has struggled through five games. Mays’ situations is far more complicated. For one, unlike safety, it’s hard to just give a center a situational role to ease him back in. A team wants to keep their center the same throughout the game for a ton of reasons, but none more important that keeping that exchange between center and quarterback consistent. “We’re still back-and-forth on what do we do with him,” Campbell said of Mays. “Do we work him and Juice (Scruggs) in and out? Do we—the center position, it’s a little different than a guard. That’s somebody that’s constantly touching the football.” Making the transition even tougher is the fact that current Lions starting center Juice Scruggs is playing very good football in Mays’ absence. It’s unlikely that Scruggs takes the starting job from Mays, but I’m sure it does bring up thoughts of, “Why mess with something that’s working?” So today’s Question of the Day is: How should the Lions handle Cade Mays’ return? My answer: Let’s establish what the Lions should do once they believe Mays is fully healthy and ready for a full share of snaps. At that point, I don’t think there should be any question that Mays should be the starting center. Scruggs may be playing well, but Mays is better. There’s a reason Mays was a costly free agent and Scruggs was part of a trade for a starting running back. I don’t think the perception of these players should change based on a five-game sample size that includes a very rough game from Scruggs vs. the Bills. But what’s a good way to ease Mays in this week? Do you actually give him a few drives at center? Do you have him simulate make protection calls from the sideline? Do you get him out there as an extra lineman in some formations? Or do you just relegate him to some special teams snaps to get him on the field, get used to contact, and re-evaluate next week? I’m leaning toward that last option. I really don’t like the idea of rotating Mays in at center for a drive or two or three. It just seems like too much of a risk. item.content:encoded: Jun 17, 2026; Detroit, MI, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) gets ready to take a snap from center Cade Mays (64) during the Detroit Lions veteran’s minicamp at the Allen Park Training Facility. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Monday, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell announced the impending return of two key players. Barring some unforeseen setback, starting center Cade Mays and safety Brian Branch will make their 2026 debuts on Sunday afternoon against the Green Bay Packers. For Branch, his return is pretty simple. While it sounds like the Lions will limit his reps a bit, Campbell seemed confident the Pro Bowl safety can take on a significant role, and his presence will be welcomed in a secondary that has struggled through five games. Mays’ situations is far more complicated. For one, unlike safety, it’s hard to just give a center a situational role to ease him back in. A team wants to keep their center the same throughout the game for a ton of reasons, but none more important that keeping that exchange between center and quarterback consistent. “We’re still back-and-forth on what do we do with him,” Campbell said of Mays. “Do we work him and Juice (Scruggs) in and out? Do we—the center position, it’s a little different than a guard. That’s somebody that’s constantly touching the football.” Making the transition even tougher is the fact that current Lions starting center Juice Scruggs is playing very good football in Mays’ absence. It’s unlikely that Scruggs takes the starting job from Mays, but I’m sure it does bring up thoughts of, “Why mess with something that’s working?” So today’s Question of the Day is: How should the Lions handle Cade Mays’ return? My answer: Let’s establish what the Lions should do once they believe Mays is fully healthy and ready for a full share of snaps. At that point, I don’t think there should be any question that Mays should be the starting center. Scruggs may be playing well, but Mays is better. There’s a reason Mays was a costly free agent and Scruggs was part of a trade for a starting running back. I don’t think the perception of these players should change based on a five-game sample size that includes a very rough game from Scruggs vs. the Bills. But what’s a good way to ease Mays in this week? Do you actually give him a few drives at center? Do you have him simulate make protection calls from the sideline? Do you get him out there as an extra lineman in some formations? Or do you just relegate him to some special teams snaps to get him on the field, get used to contact, and re-evaluate next week? I’m leaning toward that last option. I really don’t like the idea of rotating Mays in at center for a drive or two or three. It just seems like too much of a risk. Either make him your starting center or find another way to get him out there. The best way to do that is give him some special teams reps or jumbo package responsibilities, and then make him the starting center in Week 8 against the Vikings’ tough defense. It’s not an ideal spot to throw him in, but I don’t think there is an ideal option out there. What do you think? How would you handle Cade Mays’ return? Share your ideas in the comment section below. item.content:encoded: Mar 2, 2026; Indian Wells, CA, USA; Novak Djokovic (SRB) during a practice session for the BNP Paribas Open at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith As you already know, this is not the ATP rankings list; rather, these are ATP power rankings that combine 2026 results, recent form, performance against elite opposition, current fitness, and the level each player is realistically capable of producing during the final stretch of the season. The picture has changed considerably since our pre-Wimbledon rankings . Alexander Zverev has won two Grand Slams, Ben Shelton has reached his first major final, Carlos Alcaraz has returned from injury, and Alejandro Davidovich Fokina has suddenly become one of the most dangerous players on Tour. Meanwhile, Jannik Sinner, who topped the previous list, has ended his season because of a knee injury and is therefore excluded. Other players unavailable through injury are also left out. With the European indoor swing and ATP Finals approaching, here is the updated order. Post-Shanghai ATP Power Rankings 1. Alexander Zverev ATP Rank: No. 2 Previous Power Ranking: 3 There is very little room for argument at the top of the ATP power rankings. Zverev has won Roland Garros and the US Open, reached the Wimbledon final, and established himself as the strongest performer of 2026. He leads the ATP Race with 8,760 points, more than 4,000 ahead of Carlos Alcaraz, and he won’t lose it as he’s guaranteed to finish the year as number one. His Shanghai semi-final defeat to Davidovich Fokina was disappointing, particularly after winning the opening set, but hardly enough to undermine an extraordinary season. Zverev’s serve and backhand have provided a level of consistency that few opponents can match. The forehand remains exploitable, as Shanghai demonstrated, but his ability to control matches over several hours has improved considerably. With Sinner unavailable, he is the obvious ATP Finals favourite. 2. Carlos Alcaraz ATP Rank: No. 3 Previous Power Ranking: NR Alcaraz’s season has been interrupted by injury, yet he has still managed to win the Australian Open, Doha and Tokyo. His 33-5 record is particularly impressive considering how much tennis he missed because of his wrist problem. The concern is consistency. Alcaraz lost to Shelton in the US Open quarter-finals and suffered another disappointing defeat against Zizou Bergs in Shanghai. At his best, his movement, forehand and extraordinary variety make him almost impossible to contain. But he can still complicate matches through questionable shot selection and occasional lapses in concentration. His decision to accept a Vienna wild card suggests he wants more competitive matches before Turin. If healthy, his ceiling remains as high as anyone’s. 3. Alejandro Davidovich Fokina ATP Rank: No. 13 Previous Power Ranking: NR Nobody has improved their standing more dramatically over the past month . Davidovich Fokina returned from a lengthy injury absence to win Chengdu and followed that breakthrough with the biggest title of his career in Shanghai. He defeated Zverev in the semi-finals before recovering from a set down against Rafael Jodar to claim his first Masters 1000 trophy. That makes three titles in 2026 for a player who had previously lost his first five ATP finals. His aggressive returning, outstanding movement and ability to redirect pace have always made him dangerous. The difference is that he is finally converting strong performances into championships. Right now, very few players would welcome drawing him, which means his first entry into the ATP power rankings. 4. Ben Shelton ATP Rank: No. 4 Previous Power Ranking: 5 Shelton’s US Open campaign was arguably the most important development of his career. He defeated Alcaraz in a remarkable five-set quarter-final, overcame Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals and reached his first Grand Slam final before losing to Zverev. Add his Montreal Masters title into the mix and the American has made a convincing case that he belongs among the game’s elite. His serve remains one of the most destructive weapons on Tour, while his improving return game has made him significantly more competitive against the very best. However, his recent form has cooled. He withdrew from Tokyo and suffered an unexpected third-round defeat against Arthur Gea in Shanghai. Shelton remains a dangerous indoor opponent, but needs to rediscover the sharpness he showed in New York. 5. Arthur Fils ATP Rank: No. 10 Previous Power Ranking: NR Fils might be the most interesting player heading into the indoor season. His Cincinnati Masters triumph was a breakthrough. The Frenchman defeated Flavio Cobolli in the semi-finals before overcoming Tiafoe 6-3 1-6 6-0 to claim the biggest title of his career. His explosive forehand, improved movement and willingness to attack second serves make him particularly dangerous on hard courts. There have been setbacks since, including a first-round US Open defeat to Stefanos Tsitsipas and a third-round exit in Shanghai. But Fils also reached the Tokyo quarter-finals after coming through qualifying, showing his Cincinnati success wasn’t by chance. The biggest question is whether he can produce that level consistently. His upside is enormous while his week-to-week reliability remains less convincing. 6. Rafael Jodar ATP Rank: No. 11 Previous Power Ranking: NR Jodar began 2026 as an emerging prospect and has somehow reached the Shanghai Masters final while putting himself firmly in contention for the ATP Finals. His run in China was particularly impressive: he defeated Jiri Lehecka, Casper Ruud, and Daniil Medvedev, repeatedly recovering from difficult positions before eventually losing to Davidovich Fokina in three sets. Jodar’s aggressive baseline game and willingness to take the ball early have translated remarkably well to the ATP Tour; however, there is an important qualification. He has not yet shown that he can sustain this level over multiple seasons, or even across several consecutive elite tournaments. That uncertainty prevents him from climbing higher in the ATP power rankings, but based on current form alone, he absolutely belongs here. 7. Daniil Medvedev ATP Rank: No. 5 Previous Power Ranking: 8 Medvedev has quietly re-established himself as a serious contender. His Shanghai semi-final reinforced the improvement, with the Russian producing some excellent tennis before Jodar defeated him 6-3 6-4. The numbers suggest he is rediscovering some of the qualities that once made him world No. 1: his first serve remains effective, his return positioning continues to frustrate opponents, and his ability to extend rallies gives him a useful advantage against aggressive players. However, Medvedev still struggles when opponents successfully combine power with variety. Jodar exposed that problem in Shanghai. Indoor hard courts should suit the Russian, and his experience makes him a credible ATP Finals contender. Whether he can consistently beat the very best remains the larger question. 8. Flavio Cobolli ATP Rank: No. 6 Previous Power Ranking: NR Cobolli’s 2026 season has been extraordinary, even if his recent results have become considerably less impressive. He reached the Roland Garros final, made the Wimbledon quarter-finals, and established himself inside the world’s Top 10. We can’t ignore any of that. But the ATP power rankings are not simply a reward for accomplishments earlier in the season. Cobolli lost in the third round of the US Open, suffered an opening-round defeat in Beijing, and was eliminated by Adrian Mannarino in his first Shanghai match. His attacking baseline game remains dangerous, particularly when his forehand is working; however, he has struggled to maintain the consistency that carried him through the spring. The upcoming indoor tournaments will reveal whether this is simply a temporary di

item.title: These NBA teams have the most expensive tickets — and it's not close
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers' game at the New York Knicks , one of three games opening the NBA season on Oct. 20, is the league's most expensive regular-season ticket for 2026-27, with a get-in price of $1,474. Based on ticketing data for 1,194 regular season and NBA Cup games USA TODAY obtained from TicketData on Oct. 19, the premium for that game is far from shocking. As the defending champions, Jalen Brunson and the Knicks are the priciest home team in the league, with a median get-in price of $226 at Madison Square Garden. That’s double the next highest median, held by the Los Angeles Lakers . Meanwhile, LeBron James and the 76ers command the biggest road premium. Games featuring the 76ers carry a median ticket-price premium of 242% compared to the typical price for the rest of a team’s home slate. As such, when you put the Knicks and the 76ers together, it produces a pricey match-up (plus, New York will be raising its first NBA championship banner in more than 50 years). It’s about three times as expensive as the next priciest ticket — New York’s Christmas Day NBA Finals rematch against the San Antonio Spurs has a get-in price of $487. The median get-in price league-wide is $43. The NBA’s most expensive home tickets As mentioned above, the Knicks have the priciest home ticket, with a median get-in price of $226. The Lakers are the only other team in triple digits — and are still only half the cost of the Knicks’ get-in price at $113. The Boston Celtics are third, edging out the Minnesota Timberwolves , with a $93 median. On the opposite side, the cheapest median ticket falls to the Memphis Grizzlies and the Charlotte Hornets with their $19.50 get-in prices. The get-in price in New York is more than 11 times as expensive. Also around $20 are the New Orleans Pelicans ($21 get-in price) and the Utah Jazz ($21.50). The NBA’s hottest traveling tickets On the road, James and the 76ers are priced well above most host teams’ other games. Philadelphia’s road games cost a median premium of 242% compared to the typical get-in price for other games at that arena. In fact, the 76ers are the most expensive (or tied for the most expensive) visiting ticket in 25 out of the 29 NBA arenas they'll visit. The matchups that beat Philadelphia are New York at Brooklyn ($192 get-in price), Los Angeles Lakers at Chicago ($159), Miami at Milwaukee ($110), and Boston at Minnesota ($302). Two of those games have unique circumstances: the Heat’s game at the Bucks will be Giannis Antetokounmpo’s first return to Milwaukee since being traded this past summer, while the Timberwolves will be retiring Kevin Garnett’s jersey on Feb. 28 following its game against Boston. The Spurs, who lost to the Knicks in last season's NBA Finals, are the 76ers' priciest visiting opponent, with a $223 get-in price for their March 21 game. That's just $1 more than the $222 get-in price for New York's Feb. 11 visit to Philadelphia. San Antonio itself has a tie between the 76ers and the Knicks — both

item.title: NBA top 100 defenders rankings (1-10): Who is No. 2 after Victor Wembanyama in the top 10 for 2026-27?
item.description: NBA top 100 defenders rankings (1-10): Who is No. 2 after Victor Wembanyama in the top 10 for 2026-27? originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The league is full of brilliant defenders that never truly get their due. I've ranked them up to 100 every year in order to bring more attention to the defensive side of the ball. In Part 1 of this series, I covered some of the more underrated players that ranked from No. 11 to 100 . In Part 2, we're getting to the well-established names in the top 10. All of the players in the top 10 have the ability to swing games due to their defensive ability. Watch them closely inside of the last two minutes and you will see something special, as they take away huge portions of the floor or find ways to create game-changing turnovers. Spoiler alert: Victor Wembanyama is at No. 1 on this list and will probably hold that top spot for the next decade. The battle for No. 2 is a much more interesting question, and I have two players who have skyrocketed from last year's list that were in top consideration for that spot. Here's who I have at No. 2, along with the stalwarts that make up the rest of the top 10. Top 100 defenders of 2023-24 | Top 100 defenders of 2024-25 | Top 100 defenders of 2025-26 The best defenders in the NBA: 1-10 Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images 1. Victor Wembanyama, Spurs Wembanyama won his first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year award last season, and he should win a flurry more over the coming years. He's the most game-changing defender of his generation, and he's only getting better as a 22-year-old. Wembanyama's eight-foot wingspan allows him to do things that nobody else can. He's a blocks machine, leading the league during every season of his career thus far. He should retire as the best shot-blocker of all time. He also uses those long arms to swipe for crazy steals and pick off passes. Wemby has become synonymous with players U-turning any time they see him lurking in the paint. "You literally don't even want to go to the hole when he's on the floor," LeBron James said recently on his Mind the Game podcast. Wemby is also a capable defender on the perimeter, although the one minor area of improvement for him is to stop being so jumpy out there. He's willing to run step-for-step with Steph Curry as he wiggles through screens, and his length allows him to recover when he does get temporarily beat. Wemby's impact shows up all across the numbers. He's No. 1 in blocks per game. He's No. 1 in defensive estimated plus-minus. The Spurs defend a massive 8.7 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor versus off. And he inherited a team that was last in the league in defense and brought them up to No. 3 last year. Any list of the best defenders has to have Wemby at No. 1.
