item.content:encoded: By Haroon-Ishola Balogun The facts are now clearer than the fiction that went viral. The two Bangladeshi migrant workers, Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar, were not newlyweds on honeymoon. They were not executed for a kiss on the forehead. According to the Saudi Ministry of Interior and the official dispatch to the Bangladeshi Foreign Ministry, they were convicted of committing an explicit sexual act inside a mosque in the Makkah region – an act of desecration of a holy place, tried as adultery and immoral conduct, and sentenced under Ta’zir after judicial review. Correcting the false narrative is necessary. But correcting the narrative does not end the conversation – it should begin a deeper one. We call on the League of Muftis, the International Islamic Fiqh Academy, Al-Azhar, and Islamic scholars and jurists worldwide to reflect openly on this painful incident through the full lens of Shariah: justice, mercy, repentance and proportionality. Three principles demand reflection: On Justice and the Sanctity of Place To intentionally violate a mosque with fahisha is a grave sin and a crime against the sanctity that all Muslims revere. No school of thought trivializes it. The need for deterrence is real. But Shariah also places immense sanctity on process. Justice in Islam is not only about the verdict, but about how we arrive at it. Was there adequate consular access? Were alternatives of proof, confession, privacy and rehabilitation weighed? The Bangladeshi government’s query about lack of prior notification raises a legitimate procedural question that scholars of siyasa shar’iyya must address. On Repentance – The Door That Must Never Be Closed Our greatest concern is the place of Tawbah in Ta’zir punishments. In Hudud, the Prophet, peace be upon him, turned away from those who confessed, giving them room to withdraw. He said to Ma’iz: “Woe to you, go back and seek forgiveness.” Islamic jurisprudence has a rich tradition of Satr – covering sins – and encouraging private repentance for sins committed in private. While this offence, because it was committed in a public sacred place, moved beyond private sin to public violation, the question remains: In cases of Ta’zir where the judge has discretion, how central should repentance, remorse, and the possibility of reform be? Did the sinners show remorse? Were they given opportunity for Istighfar and Tawbah Nasuha before the ultimate penalty? The Quran balances justice with mercy: “But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness.” [5:39]. If Ta’zir means discretion, discretion must include the Prophetic mercy that sought to avert the harshest punishment where possible. On Ta’zir and Proportionality This was not a Hadd punishment for Zina, which requires four eyewitnesses to the actual act. It was Ta’zir – discretionary punishment for a grave act that the court deemed deserving of death for violating the holiness of Makkah. And that is precisely where the global scholarly debate is needed. Ta’zir, by its classical definition, is meant to be corrective, deterrent, and proportionate to the offence and offender – lashes, imprisonment, exile, fines, according to many jurists, with death as Ta’zir being the most disputed and restricted application. The majority of classical scholars, including the Hanafis and Shafi’is, permit death as Ta’zir only for incorrigible offenders whose continued existence poses a direct danger to public order, and even then with extreme caution. Can a single, albeit deeply offensive and immoral act inside a mosque, by two migrant workers, fall into that category of incorrigibility that necessitates execution? Or would a severe but non-lethal Ta’zir – long imprisonment, deportation after punishment, public repentance – have served both justice for the sanctity of the Haram and mercy for flawed humans? These are not questions to be answered by social media outrage or by state press releases. They are questions for qualified fuqaha. We do not call for condoning fahisha in the House of Allah. We call for scholarly ijtihad that shows the world that Islamic law is not bloodthirsty, but profound – that it defends sanctity while preserving life, that it punishes desecration while leaving the door of Tawbah open. The viral lies about a “kiss” insulted our intelligence. But a routine acceptance of death for every grave Ta’zir without scholarly debate insults our fiqh. Let the League of Muftis convene. Let them issue a contemporary, reasoned guidance on Ta’zir death penalties, on repentance in public morality offences, and on the ethics of desecration cases – so that justice is done, is seen to be done, and is seen to be merciful. Because in Islam, justice without mercy is incomplete, and mercy without justice is hollow. The post The Makkah Mosque Incident – A moment for scholars to reflect on justice, repentance and Ta’zir appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NFL Boilers: Week 6
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Tyrone Tracy Jr. #29 of the New York Giants scores a touchdown against Jaylan Ford #53 of the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hard to believe that the NFL season is already 1/3 of the way over. Also hard to believe is the fact that my beloved Tampa Bay Bucs are still looking for their second week of the season. Ugh. In more local NFL news the Indianapolis Colts fired their GM so maybe that will fix things? Word is they are talking to Peyton Manning either for him to take the job or for him to provide a recommendation for the job. It’s an interesting way to go but if I’m Manning there’s no chance I’m taking that job. Right now he does the Manningcast for a bunch more money and far less hassle than he would have in his life if he became Colts GM. Plus, he’s a Colts legend so taking the chance that the owners of the Colts would eventually have to fire him doesn’t seem worth the risk to me. Week 6 Derrick Barnes – Detroit Lions – The Lions were on a bye. George Karlaftis – Karlaftis was credited with 6 tackles (3 solo), 1 sack, and 2 TFLs, he also had 2 passes defended and 3 QB hits. The Chiefs bet the Chargers 22-6. Tyrone Tracy Jr. – NY Football Giants – Tracy had 6 rushes for 18 yards and a TD. He also had 2 receptions for 27 yards and a TD. He returned 2 kickoffs for a combined 45 yards. A combined total of 86 yards. The Giants lost to the Saints 34-27. Marcus Mbow – NY Football Giants – Mbow started at right tackle for the Giants. This was his 4th career start. He did commit a costly false start penalty. The Giants lost to the Saints 34-27. Tracy and Mbow both being on the Giants also gave us this picture which is glorious. What. A. Photo. Pair of Pro Boilers @TyroneTracy and @MarcusMbow showing out in front of the New York crowd. 📸 @Giants pic.twitter.com/vD36DFcyGK — Purdue Football (@BoilerFootball) October 18, 2026 Payne Durham – Tampa Bay Bucs – Durham had no receptions again in this game keeping guys like me incredibly frustrated that he’s not being utilized. The Bucs lost 26-19 to the Steelers in overtime. Reese Taylor – Miami Dolphins – Inactive. Aidan O’Connell – Las Vegas Raiders – DNP. Raiders lost to the Bills 33-30. item.title: Dan Quinn replacements: Ranking 7 best candidates if Commanders move on from coach
item.description: Dan Quinn replacements: Ranking 7 best candidates if Commanders move on from coach originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders went 12-5 in the first season under head coach Dan Quinn in 2024. Since then, ahead of Week 6 of the 2026 NFL regular season, his team has posted a 6-15-1 record, putting his job security in serious jeopardy in Year 3. Beyond the lack of success in the past two seasons, the Commanders' botching of a potential overtime victory over the Giants in Week 5 has made his seat hotter. Quinn will need Washington to show improved results soon to extend his term to four years. Should owner Josh Harris want to make another change and hire the 32nd head coach in franchise history, here would be his options, starting with one in-house. David Blough, Commanders offensive coordinator (age: 31) Would the Commanders follow the Bills ' example and remove an older defensive-minded coach in Quinn (56) and promote his offensive coordinator? Don't rule it out, despite Blough, a former journeyman backup, being so young. Bold offensive-minded hires have worked well for several teams. It's a good bet Washington pivots from old-school defense to new-school offense with its new leader. Blough should get a chance because of good early work getting Jayden Daniels back on track. 2. Nate Scheelhaase, Rams offensive coordinator (age: 35) Like Blough (Purdue), Scheelhaase is another former Big Ten quarterback (Illinois) to consider. Going back to before Sean McVay, five former Rams OCs (Mike LaFleur, Liam Coen, Matt LaFleur, Kevin O'Connell, Brian Schottenheimer) are current NFL head coaches, making the position the ultimate springboard. Scheelhaase also would get the best out of Daniels. 3. Declan Doyle, Ravens offensive coordinator (age: 30) The Commanders also should be paying attention to what's happening with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley around the Beltway in Baltimore. Doyle left Ben Johnson and the Bears to take play-calling duties. The results have been pretty good with the Ravens as Todd Monken's replacement. Consider Quinn's original OC was Kliff Kingsbury, who did well with the Daniels because of early good experience with another running QB, Kyler Murray. Doyle would be a great fit in Washington. Even wunderkinds Brady and Kellen Moore had to wait a little for teams to be comfortable. 5. item.title: Abduction of corps members: DSS arraigns three suspects, two others
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Department of State Services has arraigned three suspects, namely Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu and Mohammed Ali, over the kidnapping of 20 NYSC corps members along the Owerri-Onitsha road. The three suspects pleaded not guilty to the three-count charge of abduction and hostage taking, collection of ransom of N48 million and dollars, as well as illegal possession of firearms. The other two suspects, Aminu Haliru and Jiji Ibrahim, were charged with conspiracy and hostage-taking, and illegal possession of firearms. They were accused of abducting Winner Ogidi, Opara Timothy, Ogechi Henrietta and one other on October 4, 2026, but they also pleaded not guilty to the charges. Counsel for the state, Ekezie Nwauzo, filed a motion for the suspects to remain in the DSS custody, which the court presided over by Hon. Justice Emeka Orafu granted. Nnaemeka Adipuo stood for the first and second defendants in the case of abduction of corps members, while Paschal Ofoma represented the third defendant. The cases were adjourned to Thursday, October 22; Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, October 27, 28, 29, for hearing. Recall that about 20 corps members had been reportedly abducted on October 1, along Owerri-Onitsha Road, while heading to the NYSC orientation camps in Akwa Ibom and Abia States. They were later released after about six days in captivity and subsequently reunited with their families. Speaking to journalists after the court session, counsels for the defendants, Adipuo and Ofoma, noted that the suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty. The post Abduction of corps members: DSS arraigns three suspects, two others appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: SpaceX launches its 'Starfall' return capsule for 2nd time ever (video)
item.description: null SpaceX just launched its mysterious "Starfall" return capsule for the second time ever. Starfall was one of 32 payloads on the company's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission, which launched atop a Falcon 9 rocket at 7:04 a.m. EDT (1104 GMT) today (Oct. 20) from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. SpaceX has been relatively quiet about Starfall, which debuted this past June on a Falcon 9 launch from the Cape. The payloads of SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission, seen in a prelaunch photo. The company's Starfall capsule sits at the very top of the stack. (Image credit: SpaceX) That June 23 flight was a dedicated demonstration mission for Starfall, designed to show that the capsule can fly in a controlled fashion and survive the harrowing downward trip through Earth's atmosphere . And those will be Starfall's main jobs. The vehicle "will enable affordable, routine access to the microgravity environment for scientific research and in-space manufacturing," SpaceX in a June 23 X post , one of the few public statements the company has made about Starfall. Indeed, most of the details that we have about the capsule come from an environmental assessment that was published by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration in May. According to that document, the disk-shaped Starfall is roughly 2.5 feet (0.75 meters) tall and 10.2 feet (3.1 m) wide. It weighs about 4,600 pounds (2,100 kilograms) and can bring 2,200 pounds (1,000 kg) of payload back down to Earth. Artist's illustration of a SpaceX Starfall capsule reentering Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: SpaceX) Starfall wasn't the only return capsule that went up on Bandwagon-5. Among the other 31 payloads on the flight was W-Series 7, the latest orbital "mini-factory" built and operated by the California company Varda Space Industries . The W-Series capsules are designed to both host the production of valuable goods such as pharmaceuticals and bring them safely down to Earth, Varda has said. The other payloads on Bandwagon-5 are a mix of " cubesats and microsats," according to SpaceX's mission description . Among the latter is Pelican-12 , a sharp-eyed Earth-observation satellite built by the San Francisco company Planet. If all goes according to plan today, the 32 payloads will be deployed over a nearly two-hour span beginning about 57 minutes after launch. Starfall will be the last to separate, releasing from the Falcon 9's upper stage two hours and 48 minutes post-liftoff. The Falcon 9's first stage, meanwhile, came back to Earth as planned on Bandwagon-5. It touched down about nine minutes after launch, coming down in the Atlantic Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "A Shortfall of Gravitas." It was the 19th mission for this particular booster, according to the company. (Image credit: SpaceX) Bandwagon is one of two SpaceX rideshare programs. The other, known as Transporter, has been busier, flying 18 missions to date . The first Transporter mission, which lifted off in January 2021, delivered 143

item.title: EndSARS: ‘Who gave the order?’ — Atiku says APC owes Nigerians answers six years on
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Atiku Abubakar, former vice-president and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has renewed calls for accountability over the October 2020 Lekki shooting, asking who ordered the violence against protesters six years since the incident. Atiku, in a post on his X account on Tuesday, accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of failing to provide answers over the shooting and give young Nigerians a better future. “Six years after the Lekki shooting, Nigeria is still waiting for a clear answer to one devastating question: Who gave the order?” Atiku asked. Atiku also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s response to the incident, recalling remarks the president made in October 2020 when he questioned the presence and conduct of protesters who suffered casualties. “At a moment when Nigerians were demanding accountability for the violence against peaceful protesters, his response appeared more concerned with questioning the victims than demanding answers from those responsible,” he wrote. According to Atiku, the country’s failure to provide satisfactory answers has deepened public distrust, leaving families seeking justice and young Nigerians frustrated over how the incident was handled. He said, “The anger trending across the country today is not a social media performance. It is grief that has been left to harden into distrust. It is the pain of families still demanding answers, and of young people who watched their calls for dignity meet violence and then watched the country move on without the truth they deserve. “The APC has governed Nigeria through these six years. It cannot keep asking Nigerians to remember the dead while refusing to confront the unanswered questions. A government that cannot give citizens confidence that their lives matter has failed one of its most basic duties.” Atiku cited the rising cost of petrol, which he put at N1,405 per litre, saying the increase had made it more difficult for households to afford food, rent, education and transportation. To illustrate the pressure on workers, Atiku recounted an account from one of his aides about a young woman who reportedly resigned from her job because her salary could no longer cover her transport costs. Quoting the woman, he said: “The pay no longer covers transport. Everything in Nigeria just dey increase in price. Feels like I’m working for Bolt guys.” Atiku described the situation as evidence of an economy in which even some employed Nigerians were struggling to afford the cost of getting to work. He said his Economic Recovery Plan was designed to address the hardship through measures including support linked to fuel refined in Nigeria, increased local production, protection for minimum-wage earners, student support and reductions in government waste. “This is precisely the hardship my Economic Recovery Plan is designed to address, with one overriding objective: to Make Nigeria Affordable Again. Nigerians are entitled to ask why the answers and the opportunities are still missing,” he said. item.title: France pledges new curfews as PM seeks to regain control after unrest
item.description: France will impose new curfews where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, as authorities sought to restore order after weekend demonstrations degenerated into riots. The eurozone’s second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst street violence in recent years, just six months before the election to replace President Emmanuel Macron. Images of clashes, mobs looting stores and public buildings set ablaze circulated around the world, prompting several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France. Accused of failing to anticipate and contain the street violence, the government has pledged to restore order, and had announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities on Monday. During the night, a helicopter flew over the French capital’s Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square to monitor compliance with the curfew. “The sound of a helicopter at one in the morning is a bit oppressive,” said Sylvain Courant, a resident of the Les Halles neighbourhood, another hotspot of the street violence. “It’s that thing you see on TV, in all the good war films.” Macron, currently on a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, has acknowledged shortcomings in the handling of the protests. France is wrestling with a multitude of crises including high public debt, anger over soaring prices and the rise of the far right. The unrest on Saturday broke out after around half a million people turned out across France to denounce the cost of living, following four weeks of school protests. – Targeted curfews- The government scheduled another series of emergency meetings on Tuesday, including talks involving representatives of major social media platforms. Talks with trade unions are scheduled for Wednesday. Lecornu said new curfews would be decided “where the situation requires it,” adding the measures had contributed to calm overnight. Several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews on Monday in response to urban unrest that followed weeks of student demonstrations over poor learning conditions in high schools. A targeted curfew for minors was to be introduced in several districts of the southern port city of Marseille from Tuesday evening and at least through Friday, a source close to the matter told AFP. On Tuesday, security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to the ultra-left over the burning down of a historic town hall in the central city of Limoges, whose destruction has become a symbol of the violence. Anti-terror police have been called in to investigate the suspected arson. Talks with trade unions are scheduled for Wednesday. Lecornu said new curfews would be decided “where the situation requires it,” adding the measures had contributed to calm overnight. Several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews on Monday in response to urban unrest that followed weeks of student demonstrations over poor learning conditions in high schools. A targeted curfew for minors was to be introduced in several districts of the southern port city of Marseille from Tuesday evening and at least through Friday, a source close to the matter told AFP. On Tuesday, security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to the ultra-left over the burning down of a historic town hall in the central city of Limoges, whose destruction has become a symbol of the violence. Anti-terror police have been called in to investigate the suspected arson. Authorities have come under criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a “wake-up call” that exposed a “profound crisis” of authority. Investors have sold off French debt in recent weeks amid rising doubts about the government’s ability to rein in spending. – ‘Close up your borders’ – Nationwide, more than 2,500 people have been taken into police custody since the weekend, and 67 people had been jailed. Some demonstrators were seriously injured. In the eastern city of Mulhouse, a 17-year-old girl lost an eye. In Saint-Etienne, a 17-year-old boy had his hand blown off by a grenade. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday, saying police “had lost control” during the unrest. Macron rejected his resignation. Finance Minister Roland Lescure has pledged support measures for shopkeepers and craftspeople. Patrick Martin, the head of France’s Medef business lobby group, accused the state of having “failed” during the urban unrest that hit at least 3,000 businesses, according to preliminary estimates. Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, as the upcoming midterm elections force his Republican party to face strong headwinds. “What’s happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything,” Trump told reporters in Washington. “It’s immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders.” The post France pledges new curfews as PM seeks to regain control after unrest appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Visiting Slate’s first showroom as its $25,000 electric truck nears production
item.description: As I sat in the cab of the pickup truck and manually rolled down the windows, I closed my eyes and flashed back to opening the windows on a cold, winter day in my dad’s 1975 Ford Ranger to let more cigarette smoke escape. The memory faded as I opened my eyes and looked through the windshield at a wall in the Slate Customer Experience Center studded with bright color chips. Last week, in a former Tesla store staffed by some former Tesla employees, Slate opened its first showroom. Located in the Fulton Market District just northwest of the Chicago Loop, the Slate Experience Center is a place for would-be buyers to poke around a prototype, check out customization options, buy some Slate merch, and even pre-order a new Slate Truck with a $300 deposit. Designed for the American obsession with pickup trucks, the Slate Truck is a bare-bones electric pickup truck retailing for $24,950 . It sports plastic panels, a minimalist interior design sensibility, actual window winders, and a projected range of 205 miles. Ars got to go for a ride in a Slate Truck over the summer , but we haven't had a chance to shop for one. So I stopped by the Slate Experience Center so I could, er, experience the Slate. Read full article Comments

item.title: SDP to scrap bulletproof SUVs, charter jets for officials – Adebayo
item.description: By John Alechenu Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has vowed to scrap bulletproof SUVs, charter flights and other luxury perks for public officials if elected, describing the current system as Nigerians subsidising political opulence. In a statement by the Chief Media and Communications Adviser of the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign, Comrade Mark Adebayo, in Abuja, on Tuesday. The SDP candidate said an SDP administration will redirect trillions of Naira wasted on executive comforts into education, healthcare and infrastructure. “We will stop Nigerians from subsidizing the lavish lifestyles of politicians,” Adebayo declared, noting that hardship in the country is not due to lack of resources but a ruling class that “prioritizes institutionalized waste over human capital development.” Adebayo explained that successive budgets have funnelled enormous public capital into luxury vehicles, presidential fleet upgrades, State House renovations and loosely defined empowerment schemes while families grapple with inflation, fuel duty increases and crumbling social services. According to fiscal estimates cited from civil society tracking reports and budget analyses, the cost of political opulence runs into multiple trillions annually, with nearly N1 trillion regularly earmarked across cycles for luxury utility vehicles, presidential fleet upgrades and executive renovations. Mid-2026 budget implementation updates, he added, show that 33 state governments expended over $300 million, about N410 billion, on governors’ offices, Government Houses and executive travel within six months, indicating an annual drain exceeding N1 trillion across all 36 states. Adebayo also condemned multi-billion Naira deviations for luxury armoured vehicles, including single-agency procurements exceeding N10 billion for management fleets and state purchases outside appropriation bills, which he described as “criminal wastes in the midst of mass suffering induced by the anti-people policies of the current APC administration.” He assured that an SDP government will plug the leakages, eliminate unconstitutional vehicle allowances and restructure public finances, insisting four years is sufficient for a determined leader to fix infrastructure in line with Nigeria’s history of focused governance. The party urged Nigerians to reject leaders who treat public resources as personal accounts and embrace an economic model centred on welfare, production and transparent service delivery. The post SDP to scrap bulletproof SUVs, charter jets for officials – Adebayo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Erik ten Hag accuses Cristiano Ronaldo of ‘letting down’ Manchester United
item.description: Ten Hag says Ronaldo did not complete post-match run Former manager claims club broke promises made to him Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo “let the team down” during their time together at Manchester United. Ten Hag has also alleged that promises made by United’s owners went unfulfilled, leading to his sacking by the club in October 2024 . Ronaldo returned for a second spell at United in August 2021 and was already at the club when Ten Hag was appointed in April 2022 as Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s successor . The relationship between the pair quickly broke down, however, with Ronaldo refusing to come on as a substitute in a win against Tottenham in October 2022 before he then publicly criticised the club in a TV interview . The forward’s contract was mutually terminated the following month. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He let Manchester United down’ – Ten Hag recounts fallout with Ronaldo
item.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting both the club and him down during their time together at Old Trafford, alleging that the Portuguese forward failed to meet the team’s fitness and training standards. Ten Hag made the remarks in an exclusive interview with The Athletic on Tuesday, reflecting on his difficult relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner during his tenure as United manager. “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said. “I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.” Despite his criticism, the Dutchman acknowledged Ronaldo’s place in football history, describing him as one of the game’s greatest players. “Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision,” he added. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo struggled to meet the club’s fitness requirements, claiming that the forward sometimes withdrew from training sessions and failed to achieve the required heart rate levels. He also recalled an incident after United’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford in August 2022, when players had to run laps as punishment. According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo completed only two of the three laps. The former manager said he confronted Ronaldo over his fitness and positioning, insisting that the forward needed to work harder to put himself in scoring positions. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Ten Hag also claimed that Ronaldo did not contribute sufficiently to the team’s pressing and defensive work, alleging that the forward encouraged teammates to conserve their energy during training. “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training,” he said. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” The Dutchman maintained that while managers must accommodate their best players, star footballers must also accept their responsibilities to the team. “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said. Ronaldo’s relationship with Ten Hag deteriorated during the 2022/23 season, culminating in the forward’s departure from Manchester United in November 2022 following a controversial interview in which he criticised the club and its management. The post ‘He let Manchester United down’ – Ten Hag recounts fallout with Ronaldo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek
item.description: Beijing opposed on Tuesday a US government ban on its agencies using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, saying the move “overstretched” the concept of national security. China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector, trading accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security in recent months. The US Department of Homeland Security on Monday banned products developed by DeepSeek — and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties — saying they risked sharing sensitive data with China. Beijing’s foreign ministry opposed the ban on Tuesday, vowing to protect Chinese businesses. “China has consistently opposed the overstretching of the concept of national security and the politicisation of issues related to science, technology, and trade,” ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a news conference. The Department of Homeland Security can issue directions to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services. Its statement on Monday said that “DeepSeek’s models multiple threat vectors” and must be removed from IT devices. Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors,” the department warned. Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said. AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment. DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance. The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4. The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals. Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents. The topic is expected to arise again when the countries’ leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. AFP The post China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Troops rescue 27 kidnapped victims in Katsina, recover motorcycles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have recorded another operational success with the rescue of 27 kidnapped victims and recovery of a motorcycle in Katsina State. Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja, Media Information Officer, made this known on Tuesday, noting that the successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma. He said, “On 16 October 2026, troops of Sector 1 received a distress call on terrorist activities in Gamji community, Sabuwa Local Government Area. “It was reported that terrorists had abducted 27 residents, comprising 15 males and 12 females. “Troops responded swiftly, pursuing the terrorists along the Gangare–Kamba axis. “On contact, troops engaged with superior firepower, forcing the terrorists to abandon their victims and flee in disarray. “All 27 victims were rescued unharmed during exploitation of the area. “They have been profiled and handed over to community leaders for reunification with their families. “In a separate operation on the same day, troops conducting fighting patrol around Kurba village in Kankara Local Government Area encountered terrorists on 3 motorcycles. “The terrorists fled on sighting troops, abandoning one motorcycle. “The successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma in denying terrorists freedom of action and safeguarding vulnerable communities across the Joint Operations Area. “The Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, commends troops for their gallantry and swift response. “He assures residents of Katsina, Zamfara and adjoining states of the Task Force’s unwavering commitment to restoring lasting peace and security.” The post Troops rescue 27 kidnapped victims in Katsina, recover motorcycles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 'Avatar: Seven Havens' Creators Officially Reveal What Inspired the Devastated New World
item.description: One of the clearest artistic touchstones is French comic artist Jean Giraud, better known as Moebius, whom Avatar creator Bryan Konietzko mentioned as inspiration for the new series on stage at New York Comic Con 2026. Arzach and other works, particularly his contributions to the sci-fi anthology magazine Métal Hurlant , helped establish a visual language for alien worlds that feel simultaneously desolate and brimming with fascinating cultures. Moebius frequently anchored his frames with solitary figures set against colossal landscapes, letting strange architecture and alien terrain tell the story without leaning on heavy exposition. This same philosophy feels central to Seven Havens , where the wilderness is much more than a mere obstacle for Pavi and Nisha to overcome; it’s a standing monument to a deep and lost history that predates them entirely.

item.title: NASA closes the book on epic OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission: 'I am immensely proud of what we did'
item.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth. The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu , an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks , the kind that may have seeded life on Earth. "I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn . "I feel enormous pride in what we accomplished together, and real sadness that this journey has come to an end." For the mission team, the farewell capped a decade of high-stakes engineering, on-the-fly troubleshooting and nail-biting close calls that ultimately delivered to Earth the largest asteroid sample ever collected in space, one that held secrets from the early solar system . Long before launch, the team faced obstacles that nearly thwarted the endeavor — chiefly, two rejections from NASA — before finally securing the green light for the $1 billion project under the New Frontiers Program in 2011. When OSIRIS-REx launched on Sept. 8, 2016, on a two-year journey across the inner solar system, Bennu was little more than a point of light in telescopes. Scientists expected the asteroid’s surface to be a smooth, sandy sphere where OSIRIS-REx could seamlessly touch down. Much to their surprise, however, when the probe arrived at the asteroid in late 2018, it revealed Bennu to be a treacherous, loosely bound amalgamation of jagged boulders. "Our expectations about the asteroid's surface were completely wrong," Lauretta said in an Oct. 7 statement from the University of Arizona. "There was no obvious place to collect a sample anywhere." When OSIRIS-REx touched down on a small crater named Nightingale , Bennu offered so little structural resistance that scientists said its surface reacted more like fluid than a hard, rocky shell. The spacecraft's sampling head sank directly into the asteroid, stopping after burrowing 20 inches (51 centimeters) deep by firing its thrusters at the right time to pull away, with the precious sample in hand. NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft captured this series of images of asteroid Bennu on April 14, 2020, during the first rehearsal of the mission's sample collection event. The actual sample retrieval was extremely close to the way this looks. (Image credit: NASA/Goddard/Universit
item.dc:creator: Sharmila Kuthunur
item.content:encoded:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth. The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu , an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks , the kind that may have seeded life on Earth. "I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn . "I feel enormous pride in what we accomplished together, and real sadness that this journey has come to an end." For the mission team, the farewell capped a decade of high-stakes engineering, on-the-fly troubleshooting and nail-biting close calls that ultimately delivered to Earth the largest asteroid sample ever collected in space, one that held secrets from the early solar system . Long before launch, the team faced obstacles that nearly thwarted the endeavor — chiefly, two rejections from NASA — before finally securing the green light for the $1 billion project under the New Frontiers Program in 2011. When OSIRIS-REx launched on Sept. 8, 2016, on a two-year journey across the inner solar system, Bennu was little more than a point of light in telescopes. Scientists expected the asteroid’s surface to be a smooth, sandy sphere where OSIRIS-REx could seamlessly touch down. Much to their surprise, however, when the probe arrived at the asteroid in late 2018, it revealed Bennu to be a treacherous, loosely bound amalgamation of jagged boulders. "Our expectations about the asteroid's surface were completely wrong," Lauretta said in an Oct. 7 statement from the University of Arizona. "There was no obvious place to collect a sample anywhere." When OSIRIS-REx touched down on a small crater named Nightingale , Bennu offered so little structural resistance that scientists said its surface reacted more like fluid than a hard, rocky shell. The spacecraft's sampling head sank directly into the asteroid, stopping after burrowing 20 inches (51 centimeters) deep by firing its thrusters at the right time to pull away, with the precious sample in hand. NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft captured this series of images of asteroid Bennu on April 14, 2020, during the first rehearsal of the mission's sample collection event. The actual sample retrieval was extremely close to the way this looks. (Image credit: NASA/Goddard/University of Arizona) Then came another nail-biting moment: The sample collector lid got jammed in a partially open position because so much material was scooped up, allowing fragments of the precious cargo to escape. In a race against time to prevent further loss, the mission team quickly stowed the sampler head directly inside the return capsule, securing the cosmic treasure for its journey back to Earth. Even the final return to Earth , on Sept. 24, 2023, kept the team on edge: A parachute failed to deploy properly during reentry, forcing a tense but ultimately safe landing in the Utah desert. "Successful exploration missions are not those that avoid surprises; they are those that are deliberately designed to adapt to them," Lauretta said in the statement, quoting a line from the mission's final report to NASA. "That certainly describes OSIRIS-REx," he said. "Again and again, the mission presented us with circumstances we had not expected, and again and again, this team found a way forward." The mission's triumphs began long before the samples reached Earth. For example, the probe set a Guinness World Record when it slid into orbit around the 1,610-foot-wide (490 meters) Bennu, which became the smallest object ever circled by a spacecraft. The scientific payoff that followed included remote-sensing work that confirmed Bennu's surface is coated in carbon-bearing compounds . Those observations also revealed that Bennu was once part of a much larger, water-rich parent asteroid that shattered in a catastrophic collision in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The returned sample — which weighs 4.29 ounces (121.6 grams) here on Earth, more than twice the mission's requirement — continues to thrill and occupy scientists. A wave of research papers, now topping 200, continues to piece together the composition and history of the ancient space rock. Among other findings, Bennu's pristine material has revealed amino acids and sugars that, on Earth, are essential for life , alongside a history of exposure to liquid water that could have served as the "broth" for these compounds to interact. More discoveries are likely to come. Most of the returned Bennu sample is being preserved for future generations of scientists, who will study it "with questions and instruments we cannot yet anticipate," Lauretta said in the statement. Though its OSIRIS-REx chapter is closed, the spacecraft itself is far from retired. Renamed OSIRIS-APEX (OSIRIS-APophis EXplorer), the probe is using its remaining propellant to head toward Apophis , another near-Earth asteroid and a different type of space rock from Bennu. It is scheduled to arrive in 2029.

item.title: ‘Suarez killed Africa’s hope’ — Ghana’s Ayew revisits 2010 handball incident
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Ghana forward Andre Ayew has recalled the heartbreak of the 2010 FIFA World Cup quarter-final against Uruguay, saying Luis Suarez’s handball denied not only Ghana but the entire African continent a chance to reach the semi-finals then. Ayew spoke on the Obi One Podcast released on Monday, reflecting on Ghana’s dramatic elimination at the tournament in South Africa. “And Luis Suarez handling that ball killed a lot of hopes, not just from Ghana, but the whole continent,” he said. Ayew recalled that Ghana’s players had been confident of beating Uruguay and reaching the final. “How are we not going to beat Uruguay? It was not in our heads, to be honest. We were like, As soon as we beat Uruguay, we’re going to face Holland,” he said. “If we get to the semi-finals, we’re going to the finals. There was this belief that having the whole of South Africa behind us.” Ayew, who was in the stands during the match, said the handball initially left him furious, particularly as he was still a teenager at the time. “Then Suarez catches this ball. I was in the stands, and I was like, ‘I’m young, 19 or 20; everything is just flying up.’ What’s going on? He’s an idiot; he’s this, he’s that,” he recalled. He said the players were devastated when Gyan missed the penalty but did not blame the striker, whom they regarded as a key reason Ghana had reached that stage of the competition. “The players were not angry at the situation of Baby Jet or whatever. We were more like, If you were not there, we wouldn’t get here,” Ayew said, referring to Gyan by his nickname. He described Gyan as Ghana’s designated penalty taker and said the striker had enjoyed an outstanding tournament before the decisive moment. Ayew added that he still sometimes watches the match but avoids watching the penalty shootout because of Ghana’s record in such contests, including the AFCON. Ghana faced Uruguay in Johannesburg on July 2, 2010. The match ended 1-1 after extra time, with Ghana coming close to winning it in the final moments. Uruguay striker Suarez deliberately handled the ball on the goal line to prevent Dominic Adiyiah’s goal-bound header from going in, earning a red card and giving Ghana a penalty. However, Gyan struck the crossbar with the resulting spot-kick, forcing the match into a penalty shootout, which Uruguay won 4-2. In a rematch that happened at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, speaking before the game on December 2, Suarez refused to apologise, saying, “I don’t apologise for it. I apologise if I injure a player, but I took a red card for the handball. “It wasn’t my fault because I didn’t miss the penalty.” The post ‘Suarez killed Africa’s hope’ — Ghana’s Ayew revisits 2010 handball incident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Australian MP Loses Leg In Deliberate Car Attack
item.description: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has lost a leg after being struck by a car in a deliberate attack, local media said Tuesday. Political violence is rare in Australia, but law enforcement have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards the nation’s elected officials in recent years. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the attack was a “test of our character” and led an outpouring of support for Haines, widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption. She was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres (124 miles) northeast of Melbourne, at around 3:35 pm (0435 GMT) on Monday. Witnesses told national broadcaster ABC they heard a bang and saw a woman pinned between two cars. She was getting things from the trunk of her car when the attack happened, Albanese said. The driver did a U-turn to get back to her after passing, he added. “It’s clear this was a deliberate act,” he said. ‘Hero’ Barber The 65-year-old was critically injured. She underwent surgery overnight at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne. National broadcaster ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported she had lost a leg. “Helen remains in hospital in a critical condition. I spoke with her husband Phil last night, and she underwent surgery last night,” Albanese told Australian breakfast show Sunrise. “All Australians’ thoughts are with the family, with her many friends, with her community,” he added. The 43-year-old male driver of the vehicle was restrained by local barber Ricky Jefferies — now widely hailed as a “hero”. Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: “my wife would be disappointed if I’m injured”. “My family, they’re everything, and my community is second to that,” a visibly shaken Jefferies told journalists. “The other people here were just, they did so much more than me… they deserve the credit.” People lay flowers outside the office of Australian politician Helen Haines in the northern regional city of Wangaratta, some 250 kilometres north-east of Melbourne on October 20, 2026. Photo by WILLIAM WEST / AFP ‘Devastating’ The driver was then arrested and police found a knife in his car. Australian media reported that he was known to police and that his name is Brendan Nugent. A statement released by his parents said Haines had been “our friend for more than 20 years and what happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable”, The Age newspaper reported. “We would like to sincerely thank members of the local community and police who came to Helen’s aid yesterday after the shocking and horrific crime,” the statement added. An investigation by federal police, the counter-terrorism squad and Victoria state law enforcement is ongoing and he remained in custody on Tuesday. She underwent surgery overnight at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne. National broadcaster ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported she had lost a leg. “Helen remains in hospital in a critical condition. I spoke with her husband Phil last night, and she underwent surgery last night,” Albanese told Australian breakfast show Sunrise. “All Australians’ thoughts are with the family, with her many friends, with her community,” he added. The 43-year-old male driver of the vehicle was restrained by local barber Ricky Jefferies — now widely hailed as a “hero”. Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: “my wife would be disappointed if I’m injured”. “My family, they’re everything, and my community is second to that,” a visibly shaken Jefferies told journalists. “The other people here were just, they did so much more than me… they deserve the credit.” People lay flowers outside the office of Australian politician Helen Haines in the northern regional city of Wangaratta, some 250 kilometres north-east of Melbourne on October 20, 2026. Photo by WILLIAM WEST / AFP ‘Devastating’ The driver was then arrested and police found a knife in his car. Australian media reported that he was known to police and that his name is Brendan Nugent. An investigation by federal police, the counter-terrorism squad and Victoria state law enforcement is ongoing and he remained in custody on Tuesday. Federal police said they were working with local law enforcement on possible charges, including the offence of causing harm to a government official which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years’ imprisonment. The alleged attacker’s motive remains unknown and Albanese has refused to speculate while the investigation takes place. But he has bemoaned the fact that political debate in Australia had grown too heated and personal over the past few years. “It’s important in a democracy that people are allowed to have disagreements,” he said. “But that doesn’t mean that you have to draw into question people’s motivations or their patriotism or who they are.” “We’ve seen, I think, political discourse go in the wrong direction in recent times,” he said. Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action. “This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care,” her family said. “We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response.” Tributes to the independent lawmaker have poured in from across the political spectrum. Conservative opposition leader Angus Taylor described it as a “shocking day for our nation”. And far-right Senator Pauline Hanson said “violence against any elected representative, whoever they are and whatever they stand for, is never acceptable in Australia”. item.title: New Fortnite Season Might Not Be One Piece After All, New Official Ads Reveal
item.description: With the end of Chapter 7 Season 4 on the horizon, rumors had begun spreading regarding the theme of the upcoming Fortnite mini-season. Beloved manga and anime series One Piece was the most popular contender, especially after a mysterious pirate chest appeared on the island. Epic Games has begun putting up promotional posters, and the design suggests that the mini-season might just have a generic anime theme rather than being an exclusive One Piece crossover.

item.title: UPDATED: DSS Arraigns Five Suspects Over Kidnap Of 20 Corps Members, Others In Imo
item.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has arraigned five suspects allegedly linked to the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and a civilian along the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State. The suspects were brought before the Justice Oputa State High Court in Owerri, the state capital, following their arrest during intelligence-led operations in Rivers and Abia states. ﻿ The victims were abducted by gunmen near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area on October 1, 2026, while travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The abduction sparked a security operation to locate the victims and apprehend those responsible. On October 7, the 20 prospective corps members and the civilian were rescued from the Amakohia-Ubi forest in Owerri West Local Government Area. They subsequently received medical attention at the DSS hospital in Owerri. The DSS later arrested five suspects in intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Aba, Abia State. The operations involved a joint security team led by the DSS, working with the military, police and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for them and other fleeing members of the suspected kidnapping syndicate. The arraignment marks a further step in the investigation into the abduction, as the prosecution of the five arrested suspects gets underway. The post UPDATED: DSS Arraigns Five Suspects Over Kidnap Of 20 Corps Members, Others In Imo appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: INEC chairman warns staff against partisan politics
item.description: …promises new salary structure By Chinedu Adonu The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has warned staff of the commission against partisan politics, urging them to maintain neutrality and professionalism in the discharge of their electoral duties. Amupitan gave the warning on Monday during an interactive session with INEC staff from the South-East region shortly after arriving in Enugu on a working visit to engage traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders in the zone. He said the commission would not tolerate unethical conduct or actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. “You should not pick interest in any political party. Be neutral and firm. I am hearing that some of you are showing interest in some political parties. This is absolutely wrong. “The commission wants you to be neutral and professional, both in your words and actions. The commission will not tolerate unprofessional or unethical electoral conduct from any staff,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had introduced a reward and sanction mechanism covering its local government, state and national offices to promote discipline and accountability among personnel. He also announced plans to move INEC staff from the conventional civil service salary structure to a special salary structure, which he said would take effect from January 1, 2027. According to him, the initiative is aimed at improving staff welfare and reducing the likelihood of electoral officials being induced before, during and after elections. “We want the new salary structure so that you will not easily be induced before, during and after election. We are working with other relevant governmental agencies and commissions to make the cash backing for the new salary structure possible,” he said. Amupitan urged staff to work diligently to restore and strengthen public confidence in the commission, stressing that their conduct was critical to the credibility of elections. “As an unbiased umpire, we need to improve the confidence and trust the people repose in us by being disciplined and diligent in the discharge of our duties at all times,” he said. In preparations for the forthcoming general election, the INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had provided its Enugu office with 10 new pickup vans, adding that more logistics would be made available. He said non-sensitive election materials were ready, while contracts for other required materials, including sensitive materials, were being processed. “Massive training and retraining will commence soon. The retraining is imperative, given the new guidelines and regulations introduced into the amended Electoral Act,” he added. The post INEC chairman warns staff against partisan politics appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sophie Okonedo Is Serving Major Fashion Moments on the Clarissa Press Tour | See Photos
item.description: @nellkalonji From feather-trimmed Dior to fringe, the British-Nigerian actress is making a case for fashion that feels as good as it looks. Sophie Okonedo has always been one to watch on the red carpet and the Academy Award nominee has a knack for choosing looks that feel quietly dramatic. Her latest press tour for Clarissa is no exception. From sweeping feathers and playful fringe to intricate embellishments, Okonedo has been embracing pieces that bring movement and dimension to streamlined silhouettes. Ahead, we’re taking a closer look at some standout moments from her Clarissa press tour thus far. @nellkalonji Feathered Drama at Cannes For the film’s Cannes Film Festival premiere, Okonedo wore a custom black Dior gown. The dress featured an asymmetric neckline framed by delicate black feathers, which continued around the skirt and into the sweeping train. The feather detailing is part of the gown’s architecture, adding softness and movement to its otherwise structured shape. Okonedo also switched up her cornrows for a new hair color and style, giving the look an unexpected beauty twist. @nellkalonji Old Hollywood Glamour With a Modern Twist At the Magnum Cannes After Party she made a compelling case for this wonderful buttery champagne hue, stepping out in a figure-skimming satin gown paired with a lush faux-fur stole. There’s something wonderfully old Hollywood about this look, but Okonedo gives it a distinctly modern sensibility. The softly structured neckline and fluid silhouette lend the dress an understated elegance, while the plush stole introduces an unexpected contrast that makes the entire ensemble feel considerably more interesting. Her sculptural curls are another highlight, bringing an almost playful quality to an otherwise sophisticated look. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde Fringe Benefits at the BAFTA Tea Party At Sunday’s BAFTA Tea Party Q&A as part of the New York Film Festival celebrations, Okonedo returned to her signature cornrows and leaned into another texture-heavy moment, this time in a halter-neck dress from Luar’s Fall 2026 collection. The elongated silhouette was deceptively simple, allowing the details to take center stage. Slashed embellishments and cascading fringe created plenty of movement without overwhelming the look. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde Paired with Jimmy Choo Ixia pumps, the silhouette remained sleek, but the interplay of cutouts and fringe gave the ensemble a slightly rebellious edge. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde A Lesson in Tactile Dressing From Chanel For a press junket in Midtown Manhattan, Okonedo stepped out in a textured white look from Chanel ’s Fall 2026 collection, and it might be her most daring outfit of the tour so far. At first glance, the silhouette was relatively straightforward. Look closer, though, and the intricate surface detailing completely grabs you, gradually intensifying toward the hem. Okonedo finished the look with a crocodile-effect Chanel clutch and oversized sunglas

Slashed embellishments and cascading fringe created plenty of movement without overwhelming the look. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde Paired with Jimmy Choo Ixia pumps, the silhouette remained sleek, but the interplay of cutouts and fringe gave the ensemble a slightly rebellious edge. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde A Lesson in Tactile Dressing From Chanel For a press junket in Midtown Manhattan, Okonedo stepped out in a textured white look from Chanel ’s Fall 2026 collection, and it might be her most daring outfit of the tour so far. At first glance, the silhouette was relatively straightforward. Look closer, though, and the intricate surface detailing completely grabs you, gradually intensifying toward the hem. Okonedo finished the look with a crocodile-effect Chanel clutch and oversized sunglasses, giving an otherwise polished ensemble a playful, almost eccentric finish. The NYFF Beauty Look View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nick Barose (@nickbarose) For Okonedo’s New York Film Festival appearance, makeup artist Nick Barose leaned into a beauty look he described as “flirty fringes with joyous red lips.” For the complexion, Barose used Lisa Eldridge’s Seamless Skin Foundation in shade 22 and the new Luminist Concealer in shade 21 to create an even, natural-looking base. He added warmth and a fresh flush with the Velatura Balm Dewy Lip and Cheek Stick in Pomegranate Glace, while Elevated Glow Balm Concentrate in High-key Light brought a subtle radiance to the skin. Barose used the Seamless Glide Eye Pencil in Black Treacle alongside shades from the Eyeshadow Palette in Vega, adding a touch of Liquid Lurex Eyeshadow in Selene for dimension. Kitten Lash Mascara gave the lashes a fluttery finish and the new Kitten Brow Fluffy Hold and Flyaway Gel kept the brows polished. Barose paired Enhance and Define Lip Pencil in Duchess with Rouge Experience lipstick in Ribbon for a rich, vibrant red that brought instant energy to the look. It’s a beauty combination that feels especially right for Okonedo. The complexion is fresh, the eyes have just enough definition and the lipstick delivers the drama. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nell Kalonji (@nellkalonji) A Golden Moment Courtesy of Prada at the BFI London Film Festival Sophie Okonedo attended the Clarissa premiere at Vue West End during the BFI London Film Festival , wearing a yellow satin Prada gown that had all the makings of a standout red carpet moment. Okonedo naturally gravitates towards unexpected details and pieces that might overwhelm someone else but somehow feel entirely natural on her. The colour is stunning against her skin, while the twisted neckline and open back, finished with a delicate bow, offer exactly the kind of thoughtful design details we love to see. From behind, it’s practically a different dress. Another stunning look from the British-Nigerian star. item.title: Out of control? France stunned by October 17 rioting
item.description: France didn't just erupt on Saturday – it exploded. Police were doubly overwhelmed by the turnout of the October 17 cost-of-living demonstrations, which saw two and-a-half times the crowds they expected. Officers were also overwhelmed by determined flashmobs: some radical militants hellbent on a fight, others who came for the looting. The whole world watched the assault on symbols of the Republic like the 19th-century city hall in Limoges, the usually quiet porcelain capital of France.

item.title: Why Gov Otu deserves second term- Obono-Obla
item.description: A former presidential aide and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Okoi Obono-Obla is confident that Governor Bassey Otu of Cross River State will win his second term election by a landslide. Obono-Obla who was speaking on Arise News programme NewsNight, hinged his confidence on what he described as the Governor’s performance and management of the state’s finances. While stating that opposition in the state has been weakened by internal strife, he said Otu inherited a state facing significant financial challenges, including substantial debt and difficulties paying workers’ salaries. According to him, Otu has managed to address these challenges creditably well without resort to borrowing. He also highlighted an increase in the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), stating that it rose from approximately ₦21 billion in 2022 to nearly ₦76 billion in 2026. Obono-Obla maintained that Governor Otu’s handling of the state’s financial challenges, efforts to improve internally generated revenue, and overall performance makes his re-election a foregone conclusion. On efforts by opposition parties to present a single presidential candidate against President Bola Tinubu, he dismissed the idea as a mere comic relief. The post Why Gov Otu deserves second term- Obono-Obla appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Political Elite Don’t Believe In Free, Fair Elections, They Just Want To Buy Votes – Okoye
item.description: A former National Commissioner for Information and Voter Education at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Festus Okoye, has accused Nigeria’s political elite of seeking to undermine voters’ power through vote-buying. Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Tuesday, Okoye said the political elite appeared unwilling to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders, lamenting that they wanted to take away the people’s power to determine election outcomes. “I think that political elite in this country really do not believe in free, fair, and transparent election. They just want to buy the votes of the people. They want to replace the people as the sovereign, and it is very unfortunate,” Okoye said. ﻿ He said a credible election should allow voters to cast their ballots without intimidation, coercion or duress. Okoye lamented that political parties lacked clear ideologies and were not campaigning on issues, accusing them of seeking ways to ensure that votes did not count on election day. “The mark of a free, fair and transparent election is the ability of the people to go to the polling units to cast their votes without any form of intimidation, without any form of coercion, and without any form of duress. “But in this country, what we are now having is a situation where political parties have no ideologies, political parties are not campaigning on any issue, all they know is that on election day they will find a way of making sure that the votes of the people really do not count.” On the use of technology in elections, Okoye called for continued improvements in the electoral process and the deployment of technology when appropriate. He also urged the media, civil society organisations and Nigerians to pay close attention to the activities of the political elite before, during and after elections. “I think that what is important is for the country to keep on improving and also keep on deploying technology as at when due in our electoral process. “But more importantly, I think the media, civil society groups and organisations, and the Nigerian people generally must focus attention on the activities of the political elite before, during and after election.” Okoye noted that ad hoc staff, including members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and other Nigerians recruited for elections, play a more prominent role in conducting elections at polling units than INEC’s regular staff. The post Political Elite Don’t Believe In Free, Fair Elections, They Just Want To Buy Votes – Okoye appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Amnesty on Turkish media crackdown: 'Disinformation flourishes when media landscape's narrowed down'
item.description: The state takeover of Halk TV, one of Turkey’s most widely watched news channels, represents far more than an isolated confrontation between the authorities and an independent broadcaster. For Milena Buyum, Amnesty International’s Turkey campaigner, it is part of a broader erosion of media pluralism, characterized by the appointment of state trustees, the detention of journalists and mounting restrictions on independent digital platforms. Buyum describes the intervention as a "brutal attack on media freedom in Turkey,” framing it within a sustained crackdown on independent journalism that has intensified since March 2025.

item.title: Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa
item.description: ‎‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested six suspected members of an armed robbery gang responsible for attacks on residents of Jahun Local Government Area, during which cash, mobile phones and other valuables worth millions of naira were stolen. The command’s public relations officer, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday. ‎He said the arrests followed investigations into two armed robbery incidents reported in Jahun on September 24, 2026. ‎According to him, the gang invaded the residence of a 35-year-old man in Kofar Daru Quarters at about 2:00 a.m., making away with ₦20.18 million in cash, iTel mobile phones valued at ₦13.13 million, recharge cards worth ₦1 million, Android phones and other valuables. ‎He explained that the suspects also attacked the residence of a 37-year-old man in Shagari Quarters, where they stole ₦45,000, two blankets, rice and a woman’s wrapper. ‎Shiisu said detectives from Jahun Police Division immediately launched an investigation, which led to the arrest of five suspects. ‎He identified them as Sale Ibrahim, 25; Abubakar Abdullahi, 28; Babangida Ya’u, 35; Babannan Hassan, 27; and Isah Isibu, 35. ‎The police spokesperson said another breakthrough was recorded on October 15, 2026, when operatives of Maigatari Police Division, in collaboration with the Border Patrol Team, arrested a sixth suspect during a routine patrol at Maigatari Market. ‎The suspect identified as Isa Yusuf, 35, from Hantsu village in Miga Local Government Area, was found in possession of 13 new iTel mobile phones, 13 chargers, 13 batteries and ₦102,500 in cash. ‎He said the suspect was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse for further investigation. ‎According to Shiisu, the suspect confessed during interrogation to being a member of the gang involved in the Jahun robbery incidents. ‎He added that further investigation linked the recovered mobile phones and other items to the property stolen during the attacks. ‎The police spokesperson said all six suspects had been charged to court, while efforts were ongoing to track down other fleeing members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen property. ‎ The post Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US midterms – The races to watch
item.description: Americans vote on November 3 in midterm elections that will decide whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans retain control of Congress or spend the final two years of his term confronting Democratic majorities. High living costs, the war with Iran and Trump’s poor approval ratings have helped Democrats expand the electoral map, with unusually tight contests even in Republican strongholds. But polling errors, redrawn districts and record campaign spending make the outcome uncertain. – The arithmetic – Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take the upper chamber of Congress. A 50-50 tie would leave Republicans in charge through Vice President JD Vance’s tie-breaking vote. All 435 House seats are contested. With 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one Republican-aligned independent and two vacancies, Democrats need at least 218 seats in the new lower chamber for a majority. Unlike the Senate, the House battle is spread across dozens of districts rather than a handful of statewide contests. – Senate: eight battlegrounds – North Carolina: Former Democratic governor Roy Cooper faces Republican operative Michael Whatley in a bid to flip the seat vacated by the retirement of Thom Tillis, a vocal Republican Trump critic. Strong polling for Cooper has prompted both parties to shift some spending elsewhere, but the contest remains key for Democrats. Texas: Democrat James Talarico, a Christian progressive, faces Trump-backed Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose controversies have helped turn a longtime Republican stronghold into a closely watched contest. Paxton retains a loyal conservative following and enormous outside financial support. Ohio: Former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown seeks a comeback against Republican Jon Husted, who was appointed to replace Vance. Among the country’s most expensive races, it’s also a test of whether economic discontent can shift a state that has moved sharply rightward. Maine: Republican Susan Collins faces former state Senate leader Troy Jackson. She has repeatedly survived difficult elections in a state that votes Democratic for president. Alaska: Former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola challenges Republican Daniel Sullivan. Her strong standing among voters has made another Trump-voting state unexpectedly competitive. Iowa: Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek compete for retiring Republican senator Joni Ernst’s seat, while soaring agricultural and energy costs are prominent issues. Kansas: Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton is challenging Republican Roger Marshall in a state that has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Tight polling has prompted Trump to campaign for Marshall.
