item.content:encoded: Americans vote on November 3 in midterm elections that will decide whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans retain control of Congress or spend the final two years of his term confronting Democratic majorities. High living costs, the war with Iran and Trump’s poor approval ratings have helped Democrats expand the electoral map, with unusually tight contests even in Republican strongholds. But polling errors, redrawn districts and record campaign spending make the outcome uncertain. – The arithmetic – Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take the upper chamber of Congress. A 50-50 tie would leave Republicans in charge through Vice President JD Vance’s tie-breaking vote. All 435 House seats are contested. With 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one Republican-aligned independent and two vacancies, Democrats need at least 218 seats in the new lower chamber for a majority. Unlike the Senate, the House battle is spread across dozens of districts rather than a handful of statewide contests. – Senate: eight battlegrounds – North Carolina: Former Democratic governor Roy Cooper faces Republican operative Michael Whatley in a bid to flip the seat vacated by the retirement of Thom Tillis, a vocal Republican Trump critic. Strong polling for Cooper has prompted both parties to shift some spending elsewhere, but the contest remains key for Democrats. Texas: Democrat James Talarico, a Christian progressive, faces Trump-backed Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose controversies have helped turn a longtime Republican stronghold into a closely watched contest. Paxton retains a loyal conservative following and enormous outside financial support. Ohio: Former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown seeks a comeback against Republican Jon Husted, who was appointed to replace Vance. Among the country’s most expensive races, it’s also a test of whether economic discontent can shift a state that has moved sharply rightward. Maine: Republican Susan Collins faces former state Senate leader Troy Jackson. She has repeatedly survived difficult elections in a state that votes Democratic for president. Alaska: Former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola challenges Republican Daniel Sullivan. Her strong standing among voters has made another Trump-voting state unexpectedly competitive. Iowa: Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek compete for retiring Republican senator Joni Ernst’s seat, while soaring agricultural and energy costs are prominent issues. Kansas: Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton is challenging Republican Roger Marshall in a state that has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Tight polling has prompted Trump to campaign for Marshall. Michigan: An important Republican pickup opportunity pits former congressman Mike Rogers against progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, to fill retiring Democratic senator Gary Peters’ seat. – The House: watch the suburbs – New York’s 17th district: Republican Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in a Hudson Valley seat won by Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. Nebraska’s 2nd: Republican Don Bacon’s retirement leaves a competitive Omaha-area seat contested by Republican Brinker Harding and Democrat Denise Powell. Pennsylvania: Republican incumbents Ryan Mackenzie, Rob Bresnahan and Scott Perry face closely watched Democratic challenges. Nearby New Jersey’s 7th district, where Rebecca Bennett challenges Republican Tom Kean Jr., is also in play. Virginia’s 2nd: Democrat Elaine Luria is seeking to reclaim the coastal seat she lost to Republican Jennifer Kiggans in 2022. Iowa: Three Republican-held districts in the east and center of the state could provide an early indication of whether Democrats are making broad gains. – Governors: another test of Republican strength – Governors do not determine control of Congress, but 36 states are electing them, with several unusually competitive contests. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa is challenging three-term Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, while Iowa pits Democrat Rob Sand against Republican Zach Lahn. In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, while Nevada’s Republican governor Joe Lombardo is defending his office against Democratic attorney general Aaron Ford. – Under the radar: signs of a wave? – For an indication of the scale of any Democratic advance, watch two Republican-held Virginia house districts: the 1st, where Shannon Taylor challenges Robert Wittman, and the 5th, where former congressman Tom Perriello wants to unseat John McGuire. A Democratic gain in Kentucky’s Republican-leaning 6th district, or unexpected defeats for Republicans in Florida’s 13th and Wisconsin’s 1st, would likewise signal a particularly broad electoral swing. Conversely, Democrats face dangers of their own in redrawn districts, including Alabama’s 2nd, where Shomari Figures is defending his seat, and Texas’s 34th, where Vicente Gonzalez faces Republican Eric Flores. item.title: ENDSARS at Six: The Echoes, The Anger, The unfinished Justice
item.description: STILL BLEEDING: THE UNFINISHED STORY OF AN ENDSARS VICTIM For Gabriel, 20-10-20 did not end at the Lekki Toll Gate. He visited Nigeria from Turkey on the 14th of October, 2020, and arrived at his hotel in Ajah where he lodged in one of the suites. Bright, a close friend of his, visited him from Irrua in Edo state. During this period, the End SARS protest was ongoing, and was peaceful and coordinated. At about 4pm on the 20th of October 2020, Gabriel and his friend, Bright, decided to join the protest at the Lekki Toll Gate, and that turned out to be lifelong nightmare. According to Gabriel, “around 7pm on Tuesday, 20th of October, 2020, soldiers arrived at the toll gate in armoured vehicles, military SUV’s and guns. Upon seeing them, the protesters at the frontline went down on their knees and began singing the national anthem, but himself and his friend, sensing the tension, moved away from the frontline of the protest. Shortly after the soldiers arrived, all the lights at the toll gate suddenly went off, throwing the entire road into total darkness, and not long after, the soldiers opened fire, shooting straight into the crowd. The burnt family house of late Prince Eluojierio – The victims father “ 20-10-20 didn’t end at the Lekki toll gate’” I and Bright immediately started running, there was chaos as the crowd ran in different directions, the shooting did not stop. Along the line, Bright was hit, and I watched him fall. I couldn’t stop because all that mattered was my safety. As far as I remember, Bright never got up, and I was too frightened to stop, I just kept running as fast as I could until someone bumped hard into me, I stumbled and fell, and my head got trampled multiple times till I lost consciousness. That was all I remember from that horrific night. I woke up at the general hospital in Marina, Lagos Island the next morning with no idea how I got there. I had been cleaned up, although my whole body was sore, there was a bandage wrapped around my head, and bruises on my legs. The hospital was crowded with a lot of wounded people being attended to, the sight was so sad and unbearable. Once I felt slight better, I stood up and went outside the ward. I walked around the hospital in search of Bright, but he wasn’t there. I also couldn’t find my phone anymore, but since I was conscious enough to walk, staying at the hospital wasn’t helping as my mind was no longer at ease, so I decided to go back to my hotel. I got a new phone and retrieved some contacts. I tried calling Bright’s number severally, but it was switched off. I immediately went to make a police report that same day. The police took my statement and demanded that I stay around for a while incase they would need me during their investigations. item.dc:creator: akintayo eribake
item.content:encoded: STILL BLEEDING: THE UNFINISHED STORY OF AN ENDSARS VICTIM For Gabriel, 20-10-20 did not end at the Lekki Toll Gate. He visited Nigeria from Turkey on the 14th of October, 2020, and arrived at his hotel in Ajah where he lodged in one of the suites. Bright, a close friend of his, visited him from Irrua in Edo state. During this period, the End SARS protest was ongoing, and was peaceful and coordinated. At about 4pm on the 20th of October 2020, Gabriel and his friend, Bright, decided to join the protest at the Lekki Toll Gate, and that turned out to be lifelong nightmare. According to Gabriel, “around 7pm on Tuesday, 20th of October, 2020, soldiers arrived at the toll gate in armoured vehicles, military SUV’s and guns. Upon seeing them, the protesters at the frontline went down on their knees and began singing the national anthem, but himself and his friend, sensing the tension, moved away from the frontline of the protest. Shortly after the soldiers arrived, all the lights at the toll gate suddenly went off, throwing the entire road into total darkness, and not long after, the soldiers opened fire, shooting straight into the crowd. The burnt family house of late Prince Eluojierio – The victims father “ 20-10-20 didn’t end at the Lekki toll gate’” I and Bright immediately started running, there was chaos as the crowd ran in different directions, the shooting did not stop. Along the line, Bright was hit, and I watched him fall. I couldn’t stop because all that mattered was my safety. As far as I remember, Bright never got up, and I was too frightened to stop, I just kept running as fast as I could until someone bumped hard into me, I stumbled and fell, and my head got trampled multiple times till I lost consciousness. That was all I remember from that horrific night. I woke up at the general hospital in Marina, Lagos Island the next morning with no idea how I got there. I had been cleaned up, although my whole body was sore, there was a bandage wrapped around my head, and bruises on my legs. The hospital was crowded with a lot of wounded people being attended to, the sight was so sad and unbearable. Once I felt slight better, I stood up and went outside the ward. I walked around the hospital in search of Bright, but he wasn’t there. I also couldn’t find my phone anymore, but since I was conscious enough to walk, staying at the hospital wasn’t helping as my mind was no longer at ease, so I decided to go back to my hotel. I got a new phone and retrieved some contacts. I tried calling Bright’s number severally, but it was switched off. I immediately went to make a police report that same day. The police took my statement and demanded that I stay around for a while incase they would need me during their investigations. GABRIEL ELUOJIERIO, 46 – The victim “I understand the pain of loosing a loved one, but not seeing their remains for over six years is unimaginable.” Back in Irrua, Edo state, my brother informed Brights family of the incident, but according to him, they were agitated and terribly infuriated. I decided to speak to them myself, so I called his brother that same day and tried to explain the incident, but he was not willing to listen to me, instead he gave me an ultimatum of three days to send Bright back home to them, threatening that I should be ready for whatever happens if they don’t see Bright. I became scared and confused. On the 26th of October 2020, I got a call from my brother, my father had been killed. His house in Irrua was attacked by a mob led by Brights Brothers, they destroyed everything in sight and set the house ablaze with my father in it. My father was 95 years old and did not survive the flame. The police in Irrua was informed and some arrests were made, after which I was invited to Irrua. Gabriels Fathers House In Irrua, Destroyed and Burnt on October 26th, 2020 I arrived Irrua on the 27th of October 2020 and was at the police station with my brother to give a first account of the incident as it happened in Lagos. After taking my statement, the IPO suggested that I remain in touch during the investigation process, but also advised that I stay away from the community for the time being until they had the situation fully under control. Since October, 2020, my family and properties around Edo state have been attacked several times, this has forced me to relocate my family multiple times for their safety, as the threats did not stop. I have been living in fear of the unknown for since the incident, and all the investigations have yielded no good. My life and the lives of my loved ones have been under serious threats and I have not been able to live in the very place I once called home, because until today, no one has taken responsibility for the shooting, the lives that were lost, and the missing bodies. I understand the pain of loosing a loved one, but not seeing their remains for over six years is unimaginable.” The post ENDSARS at Six: The Echoes, The Anger, The unfinished Justice appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 5 Best Halloween 'Peanuts' Comics That Don't Involve the Great Pumpkin
item.description: Halloween in Charles Schulz's Peanuts frequently meant it was time for another run at the Great Pumpkin . This running gag, introduced in 1959, was sort of like Schulz's answer to Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot . Linus van Pelt spent every Halloween for almost 40 years waiting for the Great Pumpkin to arrive, and he never did.

item.title: Anambra confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response
item.description: The Anambra Government has confirmed a Lassa fever case involving a patient linked to Omasi in Ayamelum Local Government Area (LGA), who is currently receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (FETHA), Ebonyi. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Obidike, disclosed this on Monday at an emergency stakeholders’ meeting in Awka. Obidike said the state had activated an emergency response to prevent further transmission. “The state has intensified disease surveillance and public awareness. “The meeting, attended by health partners, including the World Health Organisation and Médecins Sans Frontières, led to the activation of the Incident Management System. “Health officials will follow up on the affected household in Omasi, identify people who had contact with the patient and classify them according to their level of exposure for appropriate monitoring,” he said. The commissioner urged residents experiencing persistent fever or malaria-like symptoms that do not improve with appropriate treatment to seek medical attention promptly. He warned against relying solely on self-medication, stressing that early diagnosis and proper medical care were essential to managing the disease. Also speaking, the State Epidemiologist, Dr Chuma Emembolu, advised residents to keep food covered and store it in rodent-proof containers to prevent contamination by rats. Emembolu also urged residents to maintain clean surroundings and prevent rodents from contaminating food and household items with their urine and droppings. He further warned against direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or confirmed Lassa fever patients. The epidemiologist called for strict compliance with infection prevention measures and the guidance of health professionals. “We urge residents of Omasi and other communities in Ayamelum and the state at large to remain vigilant, cooperate with public health officials and avoid spreading unverified information. “These measures are aimed at strengthening preparedness, monitoring potential contacts and reducing the risk of further transmission,” he said. (NAN) The post Anambra confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Champions League: Bayern set for Arsenal test without red-hot Olise
item.description: Champions League hopefuls Bayern Munich are set for an early test of their title credentials when they host English champions Arsenal on Wednesday without in-form winger Michael Olise. The London-born Olise, who started in Arsenal’s junior system, is suspended after picking up two yellow cards inside a minute in Bayern’s 3-3 draw with Viking last week. After seeing a first yellow for a foul, a clearly frustrated Olise responded to some verbal provocation from Viking captain Zlatko Tripic by throwing the ball at his head to be sent off for the first time in his career. After being thrust into Ballon d’Or contention due to last season’s stellar showing, the former Crystal Palace winger has continued his excellent form this campaign. Olise has nine goals and five assists from 10 games in all competitions for Bayern. With Jamal Musiala struggling with injury and illness and both Serge Gnabry and Lennart Karl well off their best form, Olise and the ever-reliable Harry Kane have shouldered Bayern’s attacking burden so far this season. The England captain has nine goals and six assists in 10 games. With Bayern 2-0 down away at Viking last week, Kane almost single-handedly engineered a comeback, scoring twice and setting up another. Speaking after Bayern’s ruthless 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, Kane said Bayern would miss Olise but called on the rest of their star-studded squad to step up. “Missing one of your biggest players, you’re going to feel it for sure, but that’s where other people have to step up and show they can take their opportunity,” Kane said. “We talk about the squad a lot, we talk about being ready for your moment and whoever plays will have to be ready.” One of the many positives to come out of Saturday’s thumping win over Leipzig was the performance of Luis Diaz. The 29-year-old had cut a frustrated figure after a poor start to the season but scored three goals and set up another in one of his best performances since moving from Liverpool in 2025. – ‘One of the best’ – Despite swapping north London for the Bavarian capital back in 2023, former Tottenham captain Kane has seen plenty of Arsenal since joining Bayern. Bayern faced the Gunners in two quarter-final legs in 2023-24, progressing by just a goal, but were outclassed in a 3-1 defeat in the league phase of last year’s competition. With domestic and international matches coming thick and fast, Kane has not had time to exchange pleasantries with any of his Gunners rivals. “I spoke to them a bit in the international break previously and we knew the game was coming up, but I think we’re all too busy right now to text each other, with a game every three days,” he explained. Saturday’s thrashing of Leipzig once again showed the perennial German champions are a cut above their domestic rivals and Kane said Bayern were relishing a chance to take on Mikel Arteta’s side. item.title: Tinubu’s reforms spare Nigeria deeper economic crisis – Shettima
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima says President Bola Tinubu’s economic decisions have spared Nigeria a deeper crisis that further delays in implementing critical reforms would have caused. Shettima said this on Monday while addressing leaders and members of the City Boy Movement at the State House Conference Hall in Abuja. He acknowledged the economic pressures Nigerians have endured, stressing that their sacrifices must translate into better livelihoods, more opportunities and improved living conditions. The vice president said the administration had demonstrated the courage to address structural weaknesses rather than postpone difficult decisions. “What distinguishes this administration from its predecessors is our refusal to pay lip service to the structural reforms Nigeria needs. “We owe that resolve to the visionary, audacious, tenacious, sagacious architect of our renewal, His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu. “His courage has drawn Nigeria back from the edge of an economic calamity that continued delay would have made inevitable,” he said. Shettima maintained that Tinubu understood the consequences of postponing necessary reforms. The vice president, however, acknowledged the hardship associated with the implementation of those reforms. “We recognise the pressures Nigerians have endured, and our obligation is to ensure that their sacrifices yield better livelihoods. “We must earn that patience by listening attentively, correcting what fails and measuring progress against the daily experience of households,” he added. The vice president also credited Tinubu’s inclusive leadership with strengthening political cooperation and accommodating diverse interests. “Beyond the science of developing solutions, governance is also the art of managing people. “The All Progressives Congress (APC) has become a template for unifying diverse groups, because Mr President understands the calculus of inclusion. “He listens to those who disagree with him, recognises talent beyond familiar circles, and gives competing interests a stake in shared success,” he also said. On the City Boy Movement, Shettima said its members had helped explain government policies, counter misinformation and encourage issue-based political engagement. “Thanks to you, we lead in issue-based politics; policies find interpreters in communities far beyond the reach of official statements; falsehood encounters resistance; difficult decisions receive a patient hearing, and the distance between government and the governed continues to narrow,” he said. He further described Tinubu as a leader whose development vision extended beyond electoral cycles. Shettima cited his support for the development of reclaimed land along the Atlantic coastline as an example of long-term planning. “He thinks beyond the calendar of an administration. Shettima maintained that Tinubu understood the consequences of postponing necessary reforms. The vice president, however, acknowledged the hardship associated with the implementation of those reforms. “We recognise the pressures Nigerians have endured, and our obligation is to ensure that their sacrifices yield better livelihoods. “We must earn that patience by listening attentively, correcting what fails and measuring progress against the daily experience of households,” he added. The vice president also credited Tinubu’s inclusive leadership with strengthening political cooperation and accommodating diverse interests. “Beyond the science of developing solutions, governance is also the art of managing people. “The All Progressives Congress (APC) has become a template for unifying diverse groups, because Mr President understands the calculus of inclusion. “He listens to those who disagree with him, recognises talent beyond familiar circles, and gives competing interests a stake in shared success,” he also said. On the City Boy Movement, Shettima said its members had helped explain government policies, counter misinformation and encourage issue-based political engagement. “Thanks to you, we lead in issue-based politics; policies find interpreters in communities far beyond the reach of official statements; falsehood encounters resistance; difficult decisions receive a patient hearing, and the distance between government and the governed continues to narrow,” he said. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Villarreal’s Iñigo Pérez ready to meet Iraola again in test of old bond
item.description: Refused a work permit at Bournemouth, Pérez comes face to face with Liverpool’s head coach in Champions League On Iñigo Pérez’s first day as a head coach he took a call from Andoni Iraola, just as he had every day for months. They had known each other for 22 years, lived in the same residency, come through the same academy and played in the same team; they had worked side by side, manager and assistant, and embarked on an adventure together. Now, though, Pérez was having to go it alone. At 36, he had become what his friend thought he would be from the moment they met, just not so soon. “He wished me luck and said he was there for me,” Pérez said, “said that if I ever needed anything …” Well, maybe not anything . Continue reading...

item.title: Googlebook review: Google’s new laptops are woefully underbaked
item.description: Great hardware let down by software flaws on these pricey machines that combine ChromeOS with Android Google’s attempt to create a new type of laptop to compete with Windows and macOS machines is finally here, combining the best of ChromeOS and Android into the new Googlebook. With advanced links to Android phones and the best of Google built in, can these Googlebooks really compete with a MacBook Air or Surface Laptop? I took two for a spin to find out. For years, Chromebooks have been the boss of budget laptops, but Googlebooks take a different, far more premium approach. Made by a range of traditional PC makers, including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo, they start at £999 (€1,099/ $899 / A$2,299 ) – a far cry from the £160 Chromebooks. Continue reading...

item.title: Hollywood AI-listers: is the technology ready to rival flesh-and-blood film stars?
item.description: As a freaky Val Kilmer doppelganger stars in a new western and faux starlet Tilly Norwood is set for her feature debut, experts are split on whether mainstream adoption is a long way down the line – or just around the corner ‘Don’t fear the dead – and don’t fear me.” An exact facsimile of a young Val Kilmer, not quite dead and not quite alive, utters that baiting line in the trailer for the new western As Deep as the Grave. Director Coerte Voorhees knows exactly what he is doing – this is an AI-created version of the late actor, approved by his family but bringing with it a heap of controversy about whether such technology could make flesh-and-blood thespians redundant. Not just yet, judging by the extended glimpse of the film released earlier this year : it looks like a thirtysomething Kilmer, if a robot version had been sent back to the 1920s American wilderness by Skynet and, as well as being strangely rigid, had forgotten to download his voice, let alone his signature air of spacey shrewdness. Kilmer’s estate signed off on it, citing his enthusiasm for new technology that expands storytelling, but surely he would have been dismayed by this freaky doppelganger. Continue reading...

item.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
item.description: Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System. The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan. The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan's flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan's heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date. Read full article Comments

In the recent changes at INEC, Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi, formerly the Administrative Secretary of the commission’s Lagos State office, was redeployed as the Director of Electoral Operations at the commission. She is the wife of Segun Showunmi, a spokesman for the Tinubu/Shettima 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. item.content:encoded: F resh controversies have resurfaced over the redeployment of key personnel of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. In the recent changes at INEC, Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi, formerly the Administrative Secretary of the commission’s Lagos State office, was redeployed as the Director of Electoral Operations at the commission. She is the wife of Segun Showunmi, a spokesman for the Tinubu/Shettima 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. Prof. Mustapha Aliu, identified as an elder brother of Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu, who is seeking a second term on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has also been nominated as an INEC commissioner. According to reports, Isah Magaji Gummi, who previously headed the Electoral Operations Department, was redeployed to the Voter Registry Department. Fubara, Wike reconciliation: Rivers Assembly recalls 3 lawmakers 27 kidnap victims rescued in Katsina The Electoral Operations Department plays a key role in election planning and implementation, including the coordination of polling arrangements, deployment of election materials and management of personnel involved in electoral operations. Although the director of the department does not independently determine election results, the responsibilities attached to the office have drawn attention to the redeployment and calls for INEC to explain the considerations behind the decision. Adeyemi-Showunmi’s redeployment has sparked debate among civil society organisations and on social media over transparency, political neutrality and public confidence in the electoral body. Former director of voter education at INEC, Mr Nick Dazang, when contacted said, it would be wrong for the Commission to pretend that appointing someone that close to a sitting governor who is contesting elections has no implications. “The person may be eminently qualified but I have profound misgivings if he can discharge or execute his office as Resident Electoral Commissioner with the professionalism, neutrality and impartiality that the office demands. On the redeployment of Sowunmi wife, he said in the time past, and oblivious of the closeness/proximity of INEC officials to certain politically exposed persons, INEC officials on their merit, had been inadvertently assigned to roles/tasks that put them in difficult positions which complicated the Commission’s core values of impartiality and neutrality. He said In such circumstances, and in deference to its core values, INEC has demonstrated sensitivity by not posting such deserving officials to these positions. “It is likely that the Commission may not be aware or cognizant of the said officer’s relationship with a prominent politician. “But once this is established, and its attention is called to this reality, it should promptly do the needful, namely: not to put the officer in a position that compromises the Commission’s principles of neutrality and provision of a level playing field to all contestants. In the prevailing circumstance, the officer should be directed to recuse herself. This will allay fears, rightly or wrongly, that she has been procured to deliberately confer an advantage to any candidate(s) in the election. Either the tenure of the subsisting Director is specially extended for the period of the election, or his Deputy is directed to act in the position of Director, subject to consideration(s) of merit, federal character and the core values aforementioned,” he added. Director-General of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo, warned that the electoral body must ensure public confidence in the electoral process and should not take the people for granted in its appointment. On the appointment of Adeyemi-Showunmi as INEC Director of Electoral Operations, Itodo said elections are fundamentally about operations, adding that by this token, it is one of the most sensitive and consequential departments within INEC. He said, “In fact, the Electoral Operations Department is at the heart of election administration. From the recruitment and deployment of polling officials to the planning, production and distribution of election materials, as well as the operational arrangements for voting and results collation, the department plays a central role in determining how elections are conducted. “Mrs. Showunmi’s competence and professional capacity are not in doubt. However, competence alone is not sufficient for appointments to sensitive positions in election management. The independence, impartiality and perceived neutrality of those entrusted with managing elections are equally important. “Appointing individuals with strong ties to politicians in such strategic positions inevitably raises legitimate questions about impartiality and INEC independence. These concerns become even more pronounced in a climate of deep public distrust, growing fears of political capture of INEC, and politicians boldly declaring the number of votes they expect to secure before a single ballot has been cast. “At a time when public confidence in the electoral process is already fragile, appointments to critical positions within INEC should inspire confidence, not deepen suspicion. INEC must recognize that its credibility rests not only on the technical competence of its personnel but also on public confidence in INEC’s independence from partisan interests. Public confidence in the electoral process must never be taken for granted. In this instance, it is being taken for granted,” he said. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar was among those who first raised the alarm over the issue, demanding immediate and full transparency from INEC. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reported changes in the Electoral Operations Department raised serious questions that INEC must answer without delay. “Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gummi was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode has also been identified as the head of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). “These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference. Nigerians will not accept vague assurances on matters this serious.” Atiku said no official should be presumed compromised because of their ethnicity, background or associations. But when reported political connections or a concentration of appointments raises public concern, INEC must provide verifiable assurances that its impartiality is protected. “A government that has driven millions of Nigerians into hardship must not be allowed to turn the electoral umpire into an instrument of political survival. When sensitive election departments are reshaped and major contracts are surrounded by unanswered questions, the suspicion that a failing administration is seeking every possible advantage to cling to power will only grow. INEC must dispel that suspicion through full, immediate and verifiable disclosure,” he said. A political analyst, Professor Saleh Dauda, maintained that political undertones cannot be ruled out in the redeployment of Adeyemi-Showunmi ahead of the general elections. Dauda, however, said the move could also be a routine civil service transfer, noting that there was no conclusive evidence to establish that it was politically motivated. Speaking on the development, Prof Dauda said the circumstances had raised questions about the possibility of political influence in key institutions. “In the Nigerian political scene, anything can happen. You cannot rule out the possibility of political undertones in her redeployment to the INEC headquarters. And from another angle,

item.title: Don’t be fooled. The AI that was supposed to save us time is doing just the opposite | Gaby Hinsliff
item.description: The government says it can transform the state with AI, but it is no match for the resulting stream of machine-generated slop. And we all pay the cost Another morning, another avalanche of emails. Even after a guilty cull, my inbox is sitting at well over 7,000, but lately I’ve started subscribing to the Quentin Crisp theory of housework: why bother, when after four years or so you stop noticing the accumulating dust? Empty inboxes just fill up again anyway. In theory, email was supposed to save hours of meetings, phone calls and standing over photocopiers. Instead, we just spend hours deleting stuff people wouldn’t have bothered telling us if it had meant picking up the phone, but which they can now spam to their entire database at the click of a button. The glorious ease and convenience of being able to reach the world in seconds came, we now know, with the inconvenience of them being able to reach you right back. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

item.title: APOD: 2026 October 20 – An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 20 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. What is most unusual is the fake location of the Sun . The Sun appears to be toward the front, just below those hills — but it is not. That is not how rainbows work . Rainbows involve a backward reflection from falling rain , so that the Sun must really be behind you . In this case, gaps between clouds near the setting Sun allowed rays to cross the entire sky and appear to converge in front , an unusual phenomenon called anticrepuscular rays . The photo was taken with a phone last week at sunset in Presenzano , Italy . The seemingly reverse rainbow was noticed when hanging up laundry . item.title: The Human Fingerprint on Earth’s Water Cycle
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Human Fingerprint on… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Measurements from NASA’s GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) and GRACE-FO (GRACE Follow-On) missions reveal trends in terrestrial water storage from April 2002 to November 2025. Areas outlined in black indicate where trends showed strong associations with human activities. Trends are depicted in terms of average annual change in equivalent water depth. NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison, based on data from O’Neill, M.M., et al . Humans are exerting increasing influence over how water moves through lakes, rivers, soil, and the subsurface, and a new NASA study shows where those effects are greatest. Using more than two decades of satellite measurements of subtle changes in Earth’s gravity, the researchers sharpened the picture of how—and why—terrestrial water storage has changed. This map encapsulates their findings, depicting changes in terrestrial water storage from April 2002 to November 2025. Beyond the influence of climate variability, the scientists identified 40 regions where the changes also aligned with human activities such as irrigation, reservoir impoundment, and land-use change. These activities were significantly related to terrestrial water storage trends on every nonpolar continent except Australia. In some areas, the effects of human activities were especially strong. “In four continental regions, an anthropogenic variable showed a stronger relationship with the storage trends than any climate variable did,” said Mary Michael O’Neill, a hydrologist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and lead author of the study. They include well-known spots such as California’s Central Valley and northern India, where farmers’ heavy reliance on groundwater has drawn down storage—in India’s case, faster than earlier estimates suggested. Elsewhere, some types of farming and water management appear to have done the opposite. Areas outlined in black indicate where trends showed strong associations with human activities. Trends are depicted in terms of average annual change in equivalent water depth. NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison, based on data from O’Neill, M.M., et al . Humans are exerting increasing influence over how water moves through lakes, rivers, soil, and the subsurface, and a new NASA study shows where those effects are greatest. Using more than two decades of satellite measurements of subtle changes in Earth’s gravity, the researchers sharpened the picture of how—and why—terrestrial water storage has changed. This map encapsulates their findings, depicting changes in terrestrial water storage from April 2002 to November 2025. Beyond the influence of climate variability, the scientists identified 40 regions where the changes also aligned with human activities such as irrigation, reservoir impoundment, and land-use change. These activities were significantly related to terrestrial water storage trends on every nonpolar continent except Australia. In some areas, the effects of human activities were especially strong. “In four continental regions, an anthropogenic variable showed a stronger relationship with the storage trends than any climate variable did,” said Mary Michael O’Neill, a hydrologist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and lead author of the study. They include well-known spots such as California’s Central Valley and northern India, where farmers’ heavy reliance on groundwater has drawn down storage—in India’s case, faster than earlier estimates suggested. Elsewhere, some types of farming and water management appear to have done the opposite. Gravity as a Water Gauge The data behind the map come from the GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) and GRACE-FO (GRACE Follow-On) missions, each of which consists of two satellites that fly in tandem. As the lead satellite passes over an area with greater mass, the slight change in gravity tugs at it, and instruments aboard the satellites measure the change in distance between them. Since water and ice are heavy and shift around regularly, scientists can use GRACE data to infer gains and losses. The satellites’ data are typically processed into monthly maps that show broad patterns of water storage. But over more than 20 years, the satellites have passed over most of the planet many times. By combining all of those passes, the researchers could map long-term water trends with five to 10 times more spatial detail than previous analyses. The tradeoff was a loss of temporal detail. They then applied statistical techniques to weigh the importance of various anthropogenic and climatic factors in the storage trends and to pinpoint where human activities may have contributed. The improved spatial resolution uncovered some human impacts that had not been previously detected, said Matthew Rodell, deputy director of Earth Sciences for Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics at Goddard and one of the study’s authors. The analysis also showed that some known trends were stronger than previously realized. Where the Water Went Across several continents, groundwater-irrigated farmland was strongly associated with declines in terrestrial water storage. In North America, these declines appeared in California’s Central Valley, the southern High Plains of the U.S., and Chihuahua, Mexico, where long-term droughts have increased farmers’ reliance on groundwater. Groundwater pumping also drove declines in northern India, where the refined analysis showed a steeper downward trend than previously realized. Consistent with previous findings, retreating Himalayan glaciers accounted for only 15 percent of the decline there. Other types of agriculture had a different relationship with water storage trends. In parts of sub-Saharan Africa, for example, some increases occurred where rainfed cropland has expanded. There, swaths of native savanna were replaced by millet cultivation throughout the study period, and water tables rose despite below-average precipitation. A similar pattern emerged in northern Brazil’s Maranhão state, where soybean fields have replaced forests and shrublands. The resulting water storage trend might be explained in part by the efficient water use of cereal and legume plants and by Indigenous practices that help direct water into shallow aquifers, the researchers said. Water storage and diversion projects also came into focus on the new map. Hundreds of large reservoirs were filled during the study period, the authors note, but the coarse spatial resolution of gravity measurements previously made them difficult to track. In the new analysis, the Boguchany Reservoir on Russia’s Angara River, the second-largest reservoir filled in the 21st century, produced the strongest water storage trend in nonpolar northern Asia. A segment of the Karakum Canal, which diverts river water to irrigate cropland in the desert, is visible as a linear, vegetated feature in this photo, taken by an astronaut aboard the International Space Station on June 13, 2021. The map also resolves smaller reservoirs and other hydrologic engineering projects. The Karakum Desert in Turkmenistan registered water storage gains stemming from the long, largely unlined Karakum Canal running through it. The canal diverts river water to support desert agriculture, but enough seeps into the ground during its journey to alter the water picture in the desert. The map’s finer resolution allows for better monitoring of such hydrologic changes in remote areas where other measurement options may be limited. Moving forward, O’Neill wants to capture how dams, diversions, irrigation, and other controls on Earth’s water affect storage downstream, and to disentangle the influence of local and non-local activities. “I’d also like to recover more of the temporal picture,” she said. One way to do that is by combining the higher-resolution data with standard monthly products or by applying the recent technique over shorter timeframes. “This could help track how localized trends evolve in response to specific events like droughts or policy changes.” NASA Earth Observatory map by Michala Garrison, using data from O’Neill, M.M., et al. (2026) . Astronaut photograph ISS065-E-111045 was acquired on June 13, 2021, with a Nikon D5 digital camera using a focal length of 1,150 millimeters . It is provided by the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility and the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit at NASA Johnson Space Center. The image was taken by a member of the Expedition 65 crew . The image has been cropped and enhanced to improve contrast, and lens artifacts have been removed. The International Space Station Program supports the laboratory as part of the ISS National Lab to help astronauts take pictures of Earth that will be of the greatest value to scientists and the public, and to make those images freely available on the internet. Additional images taken by astronauts and cosmonauts can be viewed at the NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth . Story by Lindsey Doermann. item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5036-5042: Watching the Clouds Go By
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 3 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5036-5042: Watching the Clouds Go By NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this image, a frame from one of this week’s zenith movies, looking directly overhead shortly before sunset on Oct. 7, 2026 — Sol 5037, or Martian day 5,037 of the Mars Science Laboratory mission — at 19:44:19 UTC. Curiosity used its Right Navigation Camera, and you can see the high, wispy clouds that are characteristic of the sky above Gale Crater at this time of year. NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Alex Innanen, Atmospheric Scientist at York University Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 9, 2026 Happy New Mars Year! We mark the start of a new year on Mars at the beginning of the northern hemisphere spring, or the vernal equinox. We then keep track of the seasons by counting degrees of solar longitude — each season is 90 degrees as Mars completes the whole 360 degrees of its orbit. The start of Mars year 39 at a solar longitude of 0 degrees (or L s =0°, pronounced “ell-sub-ess-zero” if you want to sound like a Martian) came at the end of September on Earth. The new year also means it’s now autumn in Gale Crater, just south of the equator. As Michelle talked about last week , we rang in the Martian new year with our drill campaign at “Basque Lakes.” This week was dedicated to wrapping up drill activities before we drive away on the weekend. After the team got a chance to see the results of last week’s lab activities, the SAM team decided on an additional GCMS (Gas Chromatograph/Mass Spectrometry) experiment . While GCMS tends to be an energy-intensive activity, we had four whole sols in Monday’s plan to play with, so we still had room for a slew of remote-sensing activities from Mastcam and ChemCam and contact science of the drill tailings — the bits of rock and minerals that are left over from our drill sample. This weekend’s plan gives us a couple more sols to wrap up drill activities at Basque Lakes and collect any last contact- or remote-science targets we want here before we begin a drive back toward the neat crystal forms we saw in the “Chiu Chiu” region . While all this is happening, the atmosphere around us continues to go through its seasonal changes. Autumn means the return of high-altitude twilight clouds , which the low sun angle at sunset illuminates beautifully. While twilight cloud activity will pick up as the autumn progresses, our late afternoon cloud movies on Wednesday of this week already caught our first high-altitude clouds of the season, as you can see at the top of this post. Most of the clouds we tend to see at Gale Crater are suboptical, or too thin to be seen

I’m looking forward to another Martian autumn of watching all these different clouds go by. Want to read more posts from the Curiosity team? item.title: 3 Video Games Where Your Choices Actually Make a Difference
item.description: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when you have hundreds of endings. Just look at how so much attention on Baldur's Gate 3 focused on its endings or, years before, how everyone tended to ignore the smaller ways the Mass Effect trilogy changed across three games in favor of looking at the restrictive outcomes in Mass Effect 3 .

item.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Adventure Games that are Barely Playable Today
item.description: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

item.title: Pennsylvania issues alert on congenital measles—something US hasn't seen for decades
item.description: Pennsylvania's health department issued a health alert Monday as cases of measles in pregnancy and, in turn, cases of congenital measles have continued to increase. Before the current outbreak—which continues to rage across the state—congenital measles cases hadn't been seen in decades, the department noted in its advisory. The alert included detailed clinical guidance for managing measles exposures and cases during pregnancy as well as cases in newborns. Many doctors have never seen such cases in their careers given the decades of successful use of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. But now, with vaccination rates slipping nationwide, the highly infectious virus is better able to get footholds in communities and spread rapidly through under-vaccinated pockets, as is happening in Pennsylvania. As of October 19, Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 measles cases this year across 42 counties. Of those, 247 have been hospitalized, and six people have reportedly died (though the latest reported death is still pending an investigation by the state health department before it is added to the state tally). Read full article Comments

Before the current outbreak—which continues to rage across the state—congenital measles cases hadn't been seen in decades, the department noted in its advisory. The alert included detailed clinical guidance for managing measles exposures and cases during pregnancy as well as cases in newborns. Many doctors have never seen such cases in their careers given the decades of successful use of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. But now, with vaccination rates slipping nationwide, the highly infectious virus is better able to get footholds in communities and spread rapidly through under-vaccinated pockets, as is happening in Pennsylvania. As of October 19, Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 measles cases this year across 42 counties. Of those, 247 have been hospitalized, and six people have reportedly died (though the latest reported death is still pending an investigation by the state health department before it is added to the state tally). item.title: Stupid Never Dies Is Easily the Worst Game of 2026
item.description: Dated doesn’t begin to describe the debut action RPG from GPTRACK50, a new studio founded by former Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi. Style points only count for so much in a downright regressive action game that’s saddled with a supremely uncomfortable story, a repetitive faux-roguelike hook, and unresponsive combat that wastes some good RPG depth. It’s the kind of game I might have loved as a kid with a low bar for quality, and one that I’d have to make a lot of excuses for loving as an adult who knows better.

item.title: New 'Blade Runner 2099' trailer is a space fan's dream with sinister starships and strange exoplanets (video)
item.description: null Cue the depressing rain, dark trench coats, and a dire dystopian dirge because the Blade Runner 2099 trailer is here! Cyberpunk is charging back in confident fashion with Prime Video's latest detour into the neon-drenched dystopia of humans and rogue replicants first introduced in director Sir Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner" from 1982, then revisited in Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049." Arriving Nov. 25, 2026, " Blade Runner 2099" 's plot turns the tables as resentful artificial beings are now the ones running the show and hunting down Earth’s humans after a successful uprising against their original makers. This newest atmospheric trailer was unveiled at last week’s New York Comic-Con and has us totally jacked to re-immerse ourselves in that noirish futuristic realm. Check it out below: It’s executive produced by showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls”) and stars Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh ("Everything Everywhere All at Once") as Olwen, playing a fading replicant Blade Runner who joins forces with Hunter Schafer’s ("Euphoria") Cora, a pure human on the run attempting to evade a squad of exterminating Blade Runners while examining their existential natures. But aside from the dazzling visuals of the City of Angels at the gates of the 22nd century, fans will also be strapping in for some cool outer space action, as evidenced by fresh footage delivering some arresting scenes of space travel, off-world planets, and Yeoh in a bizarre helmet. "Blade Runner 2099" hits Prime Video starting on Nov. 25, 2026 (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099" 's cast includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) alongside Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Launching with an 8-episode debut season and executive produced by Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" and its new world order lands on Prime Video on Nov. 25, 2026.

item.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
item.description: A Russian military satellite maneuvered in "extreme proximity" of a commercial Earth-imaging satellite in recent days in the first known example an unsanctioned rendezvous in low-Earth orbit, according to the orbital intelligence company LeoLabs. The Russian spacecraft, Kosmos 2612, "conducted a deliberate series of maneuvers toward ICEYE-X36, a US-operated commercial imaging satellite," LeoLabs said. "Kosmos 2612 closed from hundreds of kilometers away to extreme proximity to ICEYE-X36. It then maneuvered around ICEYE-X36, remained nearby for an extended period, and then began moving away." US military officials and independent analysts have tracked Kosmos 2612 since its April launch on a Soyuz rocket from a spaceport in northern Russia. Within weeks, it became apparent that at least four of the six satellites from that launch were stalking ICEYE-X36 after they adjusted orbits to line up with the orbit of the ICEYE spacecraft. Read full article Comments

item.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
item.description: On Monday, a court granted the US government's request to deny release of a former OpenAI engineer accused of bugging a top-secret conference room to steal the frontier lab’s secrets. In a court filing Sunday, US attorney Craig Missakian argued that Abdulrahman Alfozan must continue to be detained while the US makes its case that Alfozan brazenly spied on OpenAI, either for his own personal business gain or to benefit the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Evidence showed that Alfozan had been chatting with a member of the KSA royal family on WhatsApp, while pursuing opportunities to permanently move back to Saudi Arabia during the country's biggest AI push yet, the government argued. Shortly before his arrest, the FBI found he accessed a folder called "Saudi Gov Docs" on his iPhone, where he also allegedly stored photos of a second bug he planted in the offices. Read full article Comments

item.title: Art crime detective Arthur Brand warns: 'All museums have been, and will be, victims of theft'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome art crime detective Arthur Brand. "In the old days they stole a painting, but a painting is unique; you cannot cut it in two," explains Brand, "In the last 10 years they have been targeting more and more objects made of gold, silver". He examines the transformation of international art theft, warning that increasingly sophisticated criminal opportunism is shifting attention from irreplaceable paintings towards precious metals and gemstones that can be dismantled, melted down or dispersed.

item.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
item.description: The first order of business for the energy transition is electrifying applications like vehicles and heating and making sure that the electricity that powers them is made using renewables. But once the dominant slices of the emissions pie have shrunk, other categories with less potential to reduce emissions become important. A new study led by Haiwei Zhou at the University of Melbourne focused on the emissions associated with making lithium-ion batteries, which many parts of the energy transition rely on. Those emissions aren’t zero, so as we use more and more batteries, that number will grow. Right now, the researchers estimate that these emissions only account for 0.18 percent of annual greenhouse gas releases, but they could increase by a factor of 10 or more by 2050. Avoiding production There are a number of ways to reduce the emissions required to make a battery. Some elements used in various lithium-ion battery chemistries are more energy-intensive to mine and refine than others. The battery manufacturing process involves many steps that could be made more energy-efficient. And then there’s recycling, which can put battery materials back into the loop while requiring much less energy than mining. Read full article Comments

item.title: The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia
item.description: null Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set. This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. The top of the model depicts a spinning UFO floating above one of those iconic coniferous forests that dominated 90s sci-fi. Why? Because — thanks to some generous tax credits — it was cheaper to shoot in Vancouver, so that's where they all flocked. Disney Plus / Hulu bundle: was $12.99 now $11.99 Catch Mulder and Scully in every season of The X-Files on Hulu, which is available bundled with Disney+ for only $11.99/month for the first six months, then increasing to $12.99/month. View Deal Mulder and Scully closing in on our "Grey" alien friend in the woods. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies). Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to " The Lone Gunmen ". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon. The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160 Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with. The iconic "I Want To Believe" poster. Future (Ian Stokes) Newspaper clippings were a staple of the X-Files office. Future (Ian Stokes) The show's legendary tagline is proudly displayed on the front. Future (Ian Stokes) X(Files) marks the spot. Future (Ian Stokes) It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set. This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies). Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to " The Lone Gunmen ". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon. The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160 Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with. The iconic "I Want To Believe" poster. Future (Ian Stokes) Newspaper clippings were a staple of the X-Files office. Future (Ian Stokes) The show's legendary tagline is proudly displayed on the front. Future (Ian Stokes) X(Files) marks the spot. Future (Ian Stokes) It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. I love the little touches, like the display cabinets filled with artifacts, the VHS tapes scattered around the office and the black oil spillage on the floor. As with most Lego sets, the minifigures are half the joy. You get Mulder and Scully, obviously, with the dynamic duo of FBI agents both rocking flashlights (no smartphones with built-in lights back in the 90s). Mulder is wearing dark blue, while Scully is rocking an orangey brown suit, with both of them sporting an FBI badge. Outside of the principal pair, you also get Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man. Mulder's partner-turned-nemesis Alex Krycek also gets a suitably devious-looking minifig. It's the gloves, they just make him look like a bad man (which, to be fair, he is). Finally, to ramp up the paranormal scale, we also get a pair of monster minifigs: a grey alien and Flukeman minifigures. The grey alien was a must-have, especially given the UFO floating atop this display piece, but the one-off monster of the week, Flukeman, felt like a weird choice. Agents Mulder and Scully, FBI. Future (Ian Stokes) Assistant Director Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man in Mulder's Office. Future (Ian Stokes) Also, this John Doggett erasure will not stand. Sure, he could never replace Mulder, but Robert Patrick's seasons eight and nine run was excellent and he deserved a spot here. And while I'm voicing minor gripes, the usual Lego FOMO tricks were in force with this set; if you pre-ordered, you got an exclusive gift set — Scully's Lab — free of charge. This extra little diorama isn't necessary, but it does feel like the collection is incomplete without it and it's not for sale separately, so you'll have to try your luck with eBay scalpers if you want it. Speaking of Scully, Gillian Anderson has stated that after season 11 wrapped in 2018, she was done with the role. That wasn't entirely accurate, though, as she donned the lab gloves one more time for the Lego X-Files set advert . It's a short bit of fan service, but a nice touch, and, once again, it sparks those 90s neurons. All these delicious Member Berries come at a price, though, and that's the price. This blast from the past will set you back $199 (£179 in the UK). That's no small chunk of change. But then again, anyone who wants this set is in their thirties or forties and can probably afford that outlay for the nostalgia trip. And look at it this way: when The X-Files debuted back in 1993, the price would only have been about $86. I had a great time building the Lego X-Files set and if you're a fan of the series, you will too. Nostalgia often feels like a cheat code to our hearts, but there's nothing wrong with that. We deserve to remember the good times and the truth is that The X-Files was about as good as it ever got for sci-fi fans. You can buy the Lego X-Files set now, available for $199/£179 from the Lego store.

item.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
item.description: null Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. If everything goes according to plan, MMX will become the first spacecraft to land on and return samples from Phobos for study back on Earth, which scientists think could shed light on a decades-old mystery about the moons' origins and reveal clues about the formation of the early solar system . a rocket launches into a night sky from a seaside pad (Image credit: JAXA) It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket, which was jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. After clearing its launch pad today, the 207-foot-tall (63 meters) launch vehicle flew a nominal trajectory through its ascent corridor over the Pacific Ocean, jettisoning its four solid boosters in pairs just before the flight clock reached two minutes. The rocket shed its payload fairings about one minute and 20 seconds later, exposing MMX to the vacuum of space for the first time. H3's first stage, powered by two LE-9 rocket engines, channels a mixture of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen to produce a combined thrust of 331,000 pounds (1,471 kN), according to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. As the mission clock approached T+5 minutes, H3 executed its main engine cutoff procedure and separated from the second stage, which ignited its engines for a 5.5-minute burn about 10 seconds later. All continued to go to plan after that. The H3's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time for a trans-Mars injection burn about one hour and four minutes after liftoff, a maneuver that lasted roughly six minutes and 25 seconds and took MMX to a maximum velocity of about 24,145 mph (38,858 kph). MMX was released from the rocket's upper stage right on schedule, about one minute after the completion of that burn and roughly 71 minutes after liftoff. The success elicited loud cheers in mission control, which viewers saw and heard on JAXA's launch webcast. MMX is now under its own power, and on course for Mars. The interplanetary transit will last about 10 months, with the spacecraft scheduled to arrive at the Red Planet in August 2027. When it does, MMX's propulsion module will execute an orbital insertion burn to place itself in a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos, which places MMX within the space around the moon as both circle Mars.
