item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets. "They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement . "Unlike exoplanets , free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are." Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light. "We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said. A forest (of brown dwarfs) Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory. To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius). Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold. Brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/NASA/JPL-Caltech) The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane. "We’re seeing the signatures of these molecules and how they change from object to object across the entire temperature regime," said team member J. Davy Kirkpatrick, also of Caltech. "Our paper concentrated on just three dozen, but we have thousands more that we are in the process of analyzing. "I really want to see what bounds the universe places on the variety of brown dwarfs." All my colors Brown dwarfs have been routinely observed by other telescopes, including NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and the agency's now-retired Spitzer Space Telescope , but the wide wavelength coverage of SPHEREx has made it particularly useful in observing these failed stars. That's good news for astronomers waiting for change in the atmospheres of brown dwarfs as they age and grow cold. The researchers found that some brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx are at a stage of extreme change in which their clouds are clearing, creating atmospheres rich in methane. The team may have discovered significant new details about brown dwarfs, but they are still on the proverbial mystery street when it comes to these strange celestial objects, "The state-of-the-art models are capturing the general chemical trend, but when it comes to these cloudy transitions, the models are struggling to match the data," said Rustamkulov. "No two brown dwarfs are alike. Even at the same temperature, their spectra look quite distinct." NASA’s SPHEREx reveals molecules like methane (CH4), carbon dioxide (CO2), and carbon monoxide (CO) in brown dwarf atmospheres. The telescope’s view of three different brown dwarfs appears on the left. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA, M.H. Wong (UC Berkeley) et al. Acknowledgments: M. Zamani) "This journey has turned many of us into accidental meteorologists. We know how hard it is to predict weather on our own planet, and we realize it's going to be just as challenging to explain the phenomena we see in these bizarre, cold objects," Kirkpatrick said. "The findings are a call to action to explore even more of these dark worlds." As astronomers resond to that call to action, I will ponder how I could have worked Bauhaus' Goth classic "Bela Lugosi is Dead" into this article. The team's research was published on Sept. 28 in The Astrophysical Journal.

item.title: Crystal Palace to give Sage more time but manager under serious scrutiny
item.description: Frenchman under pressure after Brighton thrashing McKenna and Frank among potential replacements Pierre Sage has been granted more time to fix Crystal Palace’s defensive issues but he has been warned that things must improve quickly after the 5-0 defeat at Brighton on Sunday. The Frenchman’s future was in serious doubt after his side conceded three times inside the opening 10 minutes before equalling the 70‑year record for the club’s heaviest defeat against their arch-rivals. The thrashing means Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League: 17 from seven games. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
item.description: This week, Character.AI declared bankruptcy. While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry , court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand —potentially acquire most of Character.AI’s technology , and avoid the beleaguered startup’s many legal liabilities and obligations. In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders. The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing. Read full article Comments

item.title: Apple’s last-gen Mac Mini with the M4 is $150 off
item.description: The front view of the Mac Mini. | Image: The Verge Best Buy has a great deal for the rest of the day on the M4 Mac Mini base model that has 16GB RAM and a 256GB SSD. Normally, it doesn’t make a ton of sense to buy the M4 model for its usual $799 price given that the newer, faster M6 version has been available from Amazon for $779.99 (originally $899) for the past couple of weeks. However, at $649 it’s a much more tempting price. The M4 Mac Mini launched at $599 in 2024, and was an incredible value. Given that this sale price makes it just $50 more than the original price instead of $200, it’s a good time to buy if you want to spend as little as possible on a modern Mac desktop. Mac Mini with M4 Where to Buy: $799 $649 at Best Buy (256GB) Aside from some impressive generational leaps in processing power, you aren’t missing out on a ton by skipping the M6 model and opting for the M4. Their design and ports are nearly identical, and with either model you’ll need to supply your own keyboard, mouse, display, webcam, etc. If you’re on the fence and can’t decide between the M4 and M6 models, I suggest checking out my colleague Antonio’s review of the M6 Mac Mini. The newer model might be well worth the extra $130 cost. Read our review of the M4 Mac Mini and the M6 Mac Mini More Verge-approved deals Today brought a big discount to LG’s C6 OLEDs lineup , particularly its bigger models. The 55-inch model is $999.99 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Costco (previously $1,399.99), costing a little less than the 42- and 48-inch configurations. The price hasn’t gone below $1,299.99 before, so it’s a good time to consider an upgrade. The 65-inch model is cheaper than before, too. Previously $1,699.99, but normally selling for $1,500 or so, you can grab the larger version for $1,399.99 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Costco . If you have a big room and budget, the 77-inch LG C6H that, like the 48-inch version, has a tandem OLED panel that offers more brightness and better colors, is $1,999.99 , down from $2,499.99. For $499.99, you can grab a 14-inch HP OmniBook 3 during Best Buy’s deal of the day that has a 2K OLED screen, a capable Snapdragon X ARM processor, 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. This seems like a fantastic option for anyone on a budget. Its Snapdragon processor can run most x86 Windows 11 apps without much issue, and it’s just a rarity to get these kinds of specs — from the OLED screen to the RAM amount — at $500. My colleague Antonio reviewed the 16-inch version that cuts some corners in the screen department compared to this 14-inch model. It’s time to get spooky if you haven’t already planned your run of games for Halloween. The spectacular Silent Hill 2 remake is down to $21.34 on Steam for PC via Fanatical , a third-party site I’ve shopped from numerous times. If you’re alright with spending more, Resident Evil Requiem is one of Capcom’s several great 2026 games, and it’s $20 off at Amazon on all platforms, costing $49.99.

item.title: A Chinese rocket deorbited over Minnesota and left this in a farmer's cornfield
item.description: About a month ago, a Chinese rocket took off from a remote spaceport in the Gobi Desert, released 10 satellites into orbit, then reignited its engine and put itself on a trajectory to rain down debris over the American Midwest. The rocket's flight on September 15 lasted between 75 and 80 minutes, and it came down without completing a full orbit of the Earth. Social media posts at the time showed streaks of fiery debris falling from the sky, heading north over Kansas toward Minnesota . The overnight spectacle was also visible on the western horizon from Wisconsin . The exact time, location, and direction of the debris allowed experts to connect it to the launch of a Zhuque-2E rocket, a medium-lift vehicle built by a Chinese company called LandSpace. The rocket had launched from Dongfeng, a commercial launch zone co-located with the military-run Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China, less than two hours before. Read full article Comments

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’s academy; Charlie was on the fringes of the Leeds first team when the opportunity to join Toulouse arose in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play,” says Cresswell, now at Rennes and preparing to face Juventus in the Europa League. Continue reading...

item.title: Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle Becomes Nigeria’s Youngest Female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at 40
item.description: Judicial portrait of Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN, partner at Afe Babalola & Co., who made history as Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at the age of 40. Nigeria’s legal landscape has witnessed a momentous record as Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun – Adekunle joins the prestigious Inner Bar, officially becoming the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) in history. Attaining the highly coveted Silk rank at the age of 40, the seasoned advocate and solicitor of the Supreme Court of Nigeria has broken a long-standing ceiling, setting a inspiring milestone for women across the legal profession and beyond. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, MCIArb, is a distinguished partner at the renowned law firm Afe Babalola & Co. (Emmanuel Chambers). With a career spanning over 14 years of legal practice, she specialises in complex litigation, commercial dispute resolution, strategic legal advisory, and international arbitration. Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN following her elevation as the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria. Her academic foundation includes a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) degree from Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and a Master of Laws (LL.M.) in International Trade Law from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom. Before joining Afe Babalola & Co. as a Partner in September 2013, her professional experience included key positions at D. D. Dodo & Co. and the Nuhu Ribadu Campaign Organisation. Her historic elevation to Senior Advocate of Nigeria—a position reserved for legal practitioners who have distinguished themselves through exceptional skill, professional integrity, and significant contributions to Nigerian jurisprudence—marks a defining moment in contemporary law. Taking on the rank at 40 years old, she stands out as the youngest female lawyer to achieve this honour in Nigeria, carving a clear path for future generations of female lawyers to aim for the highest levels of leadership in the country’s judiciary and private bar. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN). item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Calls to strengthen workplace privacy in Australia as employers turn to AI to track staff
item.description: Monitoring tools common in a range of workplaces, including factories, office jobs, delivery work and in retail – often without employees being informed Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Employers are increasingly using technology, from CCTV to keystroke monitoring, to track workers’ moves and it is being accelerated by the use of AI, the Human Technology Institute has warned. Examples provided to Guardian Australia by the institute include a fast-food restaurant using surveillance cameras to stop workers using their phones, and AI tracking leading to a cashier warned over making a mistake once every 533 scans. item.title: Elephant Island is an icy sight from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 19, 2026
item.description: null Ice floats by in West Antarctica as winter comes to an end in the Southern Hemisphere. (Image credit: contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space. What is it? Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica. Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic. In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean. It got its name both from the island's shape, which some liken to that of an elephant's head, and the fact that the island is home to a community of elephant seals. Why is it incredible? While a seal-inhabited island on the left floats near the Antarctic coast, across the water is a vast, frozen landscape. In just this snapshot, you can see about between 746 and 1,056 miles (1,200 to 1,700 kilometers) of the icy continent. This image was captured on Sept. 30, 2026. In the Southern Hemisphere, that was just past the end of winter. The absolute peak for sea ice in Antarctica fell just a couple weeks before, on Sept. 14, according to the National Snow and Ice Data Center, ESA reported . So in this one snapshot, we can see a near-maximum for sea ice in the Antarctic, spanning hundreds of miles. In observing our own planet from space, we are able to peer across vast landscapes, capturing important observational data. This is especially critical for the Antarctic as, with the progression of climate change , this sea ice continues to dwindle , adding to sea level rise among other serious consequences across the planet.

item.title: Nancy Isime, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere & More Star in Loving Itohan | Watch Trailer
item.description: Nancy Isime in traditional Edo wedding attire on the set of her debut executive producer film Loving Itohan. Remember when Nancy Isime announced she was stepping into the shoes of an executive producer for her very first feature film? Well, the moment is finally here, and we have our first real look at what she has been cooking up! The Nollywood favourite has unveiled the trailer for Loving Itohan , giving us a front-row seat to a drama packed with romance, secrets, and tough personal choices. The story centres on Itohan, a woman caught in a web of emotional conflict and hidden truths that threaten to turn her world upside down. As unexpected situations force her to make tough choices between her heart and her reality, she has to navigate what love truly demands when secrets begin to surface. Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe on set for Loving Itohan, in cinemas 6 November 2026. Sharing the trailer, Nancy Isime could not contain her excitement over bringing the story to life: It’s finally here! We’re excited to introduce you to our baby, Loving Itohan! After so much love, hard work, and dedication, we can finally share a little piece of this story with you. The official trailer is out, and we can’t wait for you to meet Itohan and fall in love with her story, just as we have. Directed by Orobosa Ikponmwen and produced by Emmanuel Izuoba alongside Nancy Isime as executive producer , the feature drama stars Nancy Isime in the lead role, alongside Uzor Arukwe , Martha Ehinome Orhiere , Dorathy Bachor , Chioma Nwosu , Obehi Aburime , and Grace Coker . Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe filming Loving Itohan. Nancy Isime on location with cast members filming scenes for Loving Itohan. For everyone looking forward to catching this one on the big screen, Loving Itohan arrives in cinemas nationwide on 6 November 2026. item.title: Review: Lanterns is a truly unique twist on the superhero genre
item.description: The trailers for HBO's DC Universe series Lanterns teased a show that eschewed the usual superhero hijinks in favor of a gritty realism more in the vein of True Detective or Slow Horses . Personally, I liked the change. My verdict: Ignore the review bombing ; it's wonderful. The season wrapped with an emotionally charged, almost elegiac finale that fully delivered on that initial promise. I've found the rebooted DC Universe films released thus far to be enjoyable but rather forgettable, even when the positives outweigh the negatives . But Lanterns is a shining beacon of what is possible when someone is allowed to get really creative within the genre. (Spoilers below, but no major reveals.) There are two primary storylines. The first takes place in 2016 with a mass shooting at a local football game in Rushville, Nebraska. Current Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and his new trainee, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), get involved in the investigation, to the annoyance of Sheriff Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald), who initially doesn't think the case has any extraterrestrial connection. She is soon proved wrong when the suspect (an alien) self-detonates. Hal's power ring controls the damage, but the mystery remains. Read full article Comments

item.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
item.description: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised. Continue reading...

item.title: Nigerian Artists Who Have Sold Out London’s O2 Arena
item.description: The O2 Arena is one of the most popular music venues in the world. Its significance extends to Nigerian music. As Afrobeats was crossing over to the world, selling out London’s 02 Arena became one of the markers of that global expansion. Ayo Onikoyi , for Vanguard Newspaper , described the venue as “a symbol of global acceptance, a stamp of credibility, and a gateway to even greater success” for Nigerian artists. Filling a room with 1000 people requires a lot of work; now multiply that by 20, and imagine what how much effort it’d take to fill out a venue with 20, 000 people, screaming back your music at you. The London’s 02 Arena has a 20,000-seat capacity, and has become one of the most recognisable stages in Afrobeats’ international rise, offering artists an opportunity to perform before large audiences, connect with Nigerians and other African music lovers in the diaspora, and demonstrate the growing commercial appeal of Nigerian music. Its reputation as a venue for global superstars has also made performing there a significant career milestone. If you can sell out the 02 Arena, you could dare to sell out a bigger venue, stadiums, and many more, in the world. Being very popular in Nigeria does not translate to selling out venues like the O2 Arena; your music must have travelled far. Wizkid opened the 022 Arena door when he sold out the O2 Arena in 2018, becoming the first Nigerian artist to achieve the feat. Since then, Davido , Burna Boy , Asake and Rema have also taken their music to the celebrated London venue, with some returning for multiple shows. Here are the Nigerian artists who have sold out the O2 Arena: Wizkid Wizkid made history on 26 May 2018 when he sold out the O2 Arena with his Afrorepublik concert, becoming the first Nigerian artist to achieve the feat. The show featured appearances by other Nigerian and UK-based artists, including Tiwa Savage, Mr Eazi and many others. It marked a major moment for Afrobeats, demonstrating that Nigerian music could command a 20,000-capacity venue in London. He returned in 2021 during the Made in Lagos tour, when he sold out the iconic venues within minutes, and performed for three consecutive days. Davido On 27 January 2019, Davido headlined a sold-out show at the O2 Arena. The concert featured special appearances, including British actor Idris Elba and Jamaican artist Popcaan , and showcased Davido’s ability to bring his energetic performances and catalogue of hits to an international audience. The milestone further strengthened his position as one of Afrobeats’ leading global stars. Burna Boy Burna Boy sold out the O2 Arena on 27 August 2021 during his Spaceship tour. Asake After rising rapidly through the Nigerian music scene with hits, Asake took another major step in his career when he sold out the O2 Arena on 20 August 2023. The show followed his successful sold-out performances at the smaller O2 Academy Brixton venue. He returned to the O2 Arena in 2024 for his Lungu Boy World Tour, rein

Asake After rising rapidly through the Nigerian music scene with hits, Asake took another major step in his career when he sold out the O2 Arena on 20 August 2023. The show followed his successful sold-out performances at the smaller O2 Academy Brixton venue. He returned to the O2 Arena in 2024 for his Lungu Boy World Tour, reinforcing his growing international appeal and the reach of his distinctive street-pop sound, and returned again in 2026 during his In God We Trust tour. Rema Rema joined the list on 14 November 2023 when he sold out the O2 Arena. At just 23, he became one of the youngest Nigerian artists to headline a sold-out concert at the venue. The show featured an elaborate entrance, a live band and performances of songs from his growing catalogue, including his global hit “Calm Down.” It was a defining moment for the singer. Now, Olamide has announced his upcoming show at the O2 Arena in March 2027. The O2 Arena remains one of the most significant stages for Nigerian artists seeking to cement their place on the global music scene, and Olamide’s planned performance will be another important moment for Afrobeats. It will add his name to the growing list of Nigerian artists who have taken their music to the celebrated London venue, further demonstrating how far Nigerian music has travelled and how much further it can go. item.title: From a Casual Night Out to a Brand-New Car: How Queen Thompson Won Big in the Guinness ‘Open For More’ Promo!
item.description: When you head out for a night of good vibes with your friends, you expect great conversations, plenty of laughter, and maybe a few photos for the Gram. What you probably don’t expect is to walk away with the chance to win a brand-new car! That was the unexpected turn Queen Thompson ’s evening took when she became the grand prize winner of the recently concluded 10-week Guinness ‘Open For More’ promo. It started as a regular night out in Akwa Ibom. Queen and her friends had gone to one of their favourite spots to unwind, catch up and enjoy some chilled drinks. Among the bottles on the table was Guinness Foreign Extra Stout . At some point during the evening, Queen noticed the promo code beneath her bottle cap, brought out her phone, and entered it. Nothing elaborate, just a quick entry while enjoying the night. Little did she know that one simple entry would put her in the running for a brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado worth ₦150 million! A few weeks later, Queen received a phone call from an official Guinness representative with news that would have anyone asking, “ Wait, what?! Is this for real? ” She had won the grand prize! But excitement wasn’t her first reaction. Having been defrauded twice earlier in the year, Queen was understandably cautious and initially wondered if the call was another scam. It took the official prize presentation for the news to fully sink in. At the handover ceremony at Guinness Nigeria’s headquarters in Ogba, Lagos, Queen’s win became official in the most memorable way. Girish Sharma , Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guinness Nigeria Plc , personally presented her with the keys to her brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado, as company executives, brand representatives, fellow prize winners and well-wishers gathered to celebrate the moment. Still taking it all in, Queen said, “I am still in shock! I never imagined that opening a bottle of Guinness Foreign Extra Stout would lead to me driving home in a brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado. When I got the notification, I initially doubted it because I had been defrauded twice earlier this year. I am so grateful to Guinness for this incredible, life-changing gift. Truly, what God cannot do does not exist!” Now that’s one night out that ended with a plot twist nobody saw coming! The Guinness ‘Open For More’ promo may have wrapped up, but the winners’ stories remain memorable, especially the grand winner whose experience leaves us with a little reminder: stay open to possibilities; you never know when good news might be on the other end of a call. Queen’s story was the grand finale of a much bigger journey. Over 10 weeks, Guinness Nigeria rewarded 1,075 consumers across the country, with 1,000 people winning ₦100,000 each and another 75 becoming millionaires with ₦1 million apiece, before Queen drove home with the grand prize, a Toyota Land Cruiser Prado valued at ₦150 million. For Guinness, Open For More was a way to give something back to the consumers wh

A few weeks later, Queen received a phone call from an official Guinness representative with news that would have anyone asking, “ Wait, what?! Is this for real? ” She had won the grand prize! But excitement wasn’t her first reaction. Having been defrauded twice earlier in the year, Queen was understandably cautious and initially wondered if the call was another scam. It took the official prize presentation for the news to fully sink in. At the handover ceremony at Guinness Nigeria’s headquarters in Ogba, Lagos, Queen’s win became official in the most memorable way. Girish Sharma , Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guinness Nigeria Plc , personally presented her with the keys to her brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado, as company executives, brand representatives, fellow prize winners and well-wishers gathered to celebrate the moment. Still taking it all in, Queen said, “I am still in shock! I never imagined that opening a bottle of Guinness Foreign Extra Stout would lead to me driving home in a brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado. When I got the notification, I initially doubted it because I had been defrauded twice earlier this year. I am so grateful to Guinness for this incredible, life-changing gift. Truly, what God cannot do does not exist!” Now that’s one night out that ended with a plot twist nobody saw coming! The Guinness ‘Open For More’ promo may have wrapped up, but the winners’ stories remain memorable, especially the grand winner whose experience leaves us with a little reminder: stay open to possibilities; you never know when good news might be on the other end of a call. Queen’s story was the grand finale of a much bigger journey. Over 10 weeks, Guinness Nigeria rewarded 1,075 consumers across the country, with 1,000 people winning ₦100,000 each and another 75 becoming millionaires with ₦1 million apiece, before Queen drove home with the grand prize, a Toyota Land Cruiser Prado valued at ₦150 million. For Guinness, Open For More was a way to give something back to the consumers who continue to choose the brand. For the winners, it meant real money, unexpected opportunities, and, in Queen’s case, a night out that ended with a new car. item.title: Before They Say “I Do”, See Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi’s Pre-Wedding Photos
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in an intimate pre-wedding portrait. Can you hear the wedding bells? Something beautiful is happening in Zlatan Ibile ’s world, and this time, it has nothing to do with a new song or music video. The Afrobeats star, whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , is getting ready to celebrate his love for longtime partner Davita Omoniyi in a grand wedding ceremony on 24 October 2026. And while we’re still waiting to see what the couple have planned for their big day, their pre-wedding photographs are already giving us plenty to admire. From the gorgeous colour choices to the fashion and the sweet way they pose together, Zlatan and Davita are making the countdown to their wedding even more exciting. The couple have been together for years and share two children. Davita, a UK-based media personality and entrepreneur, reportedly took on the Omoniyi surname following their private civil registry ceremony earlier this year. Now, with their wedding celebration approaching, they’re preparing to mark another chapter of their relationship surrounded by family and friends. Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi posing together in pastel outfits for their official pre-wedding pictures. For their pre-wedding photographs, celebrity stylist Emmanuel Goodnews Icon brought together a lovely combination of pastel ice blue and blush pink against a rich teal studio backdrop. The colours worked beautifully together, with Davita’s gown and Zlatan’s tailored outfit offering two different takes on the same colour palette. Davita wore a strapless mermaid gown by Lasosa By Pam Pam, featuring micro-pleating and ruching across the bodice. The fitted silhouette opened into a voluminous bubble-hem train made from bubblegum pink taffeta, giving the dress an interesting contrast of structure and volume. She completed her look with a high braided ponytail, glowing makeup, a classic tennis necklace and matching diamond jewellery. Davita Omoniyi in a custom gown by Lasosa By Pam Pam styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon. Beside her, Zlatan wore a bespoke light blue two-piece suit by T.I Nathan. His jacket featured a structured mandarin collar and concealed button placket, paired with relaxed wide-leg trousers. Dark wire-frame glasses and black patent leather shoes completed his look, keeping the styling simple while allowing the tailoring and colour to take centre stage. Zlatan Ibile styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon in a bespoke T.I Nathan suit The rich teal backdrop made the soft colours of their outfits even more striking, while their poses brought a lovely sense of closeness to the portraits. With 24 October just around the corner, the couple have given us a beautiful first look at their wedding style, and we’re curious to see what they’ll wear when the celebrations begin. item.title: AI firm Anthropic to commit 5% of shares to fund for ‘public good’
item.description: The $48bn giveaway comes amid concerns about the tech and as the company prepares for a stock market listing Anthropic has said it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund for the “public good”, as the AI developer behind the Claude chatbot seeks to bolster its appeal before its stock market listing. The company announced it would commit the shares, worth around $48bn (£36bn) at its latest valuation in May, subject to shareholder approval. It will add a further 2% of its stock to the fund for every 50% increase in its value above an undisclosed baseline. Continue reading...

item.title: DIY VR: How to build your own headset, and why you probably won't want to
item.description: Virtual reality is in a bit of a weird place right now. After a lot of unfulfilled promise in the 1990s, it came back strong with the 2016 release of the Oculus Rift . For a while, it looked like VR, AR, XR, the metaverse, or whatever you wanted to call it, was going to be huge. Mark Zuckerberg was certainly convinced , and even Apple got in on the hype with its Vision Pro . But by then momentum for alternate realities of every acronym was already in steady decline, and it only dwindled from there. The rate of development of new headsets has slowed, with many companies (including Apple) scaling back or shelving their efforts. While new releases like the Steam Frame and Pimax Dream Air are still happening, many of the most interesting developments in the space these days are on the enthusiast front. That's right, DIY VR is a thing, and with a couple hundred dollars in components, plus many hours of your time, you too can enter the immersive world of virtual reality while also experiencing the highs and lows of soldering, firmware flashing, and 3D printing. I rode that rollercoaster myself and learned why this is still a decidedly niche movement. Read full article Comments

item.title: Did a giant object collide with Earth to form the moon?
item.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

For as long as humans have watched the night sky, we have wondered about the moon , pondering everything from its alien appearance to its influence over phenomena on Earth such as ocean tides, climate stability, and even the natural rhythms of many organisms. Among the many questions we have about Earth's lone natural satellite, one remains preeminent: what are the moon's origins , and how long has it orbited Earth? Today, the leading theory among astronomers is that deep in our planet's past — perhaps within roughly the first 100 million years of solar system history — Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours . Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia. The material ejected into orbit by the powerful impact in question would have accumulated afterward, forming the moon that we observe today. What do we know? Birth of a lunar origin hypothesis The evolution of this striking solution to one of the moon's most enduring mysteries goes back to 1946, when geologist Reginald Aldworth Daly was among the first to suggest that an impact event might explain the formation of the moon. Before Daly, scientists had been leaning toward theories that involved Earth's rapid spin billions of years ago, when each day may have at one time lasted as little as 2 or 3 hours . Decades later in the 1970s, researchers William Hartmann and Donald Davis developed their own models involving collisions of large bodies left over from planetary formation, which could collide with younger planets. Building on such ideas, other researchers went on to propose similar scenarios between the early Earth and a Mars-sized object. Early in the following decade, the concept eventually claimed its place as the leading lunar-formation process during a landmark conference held in Kona, Hawaii, in 1984. Earth's moon is thought to have formed when a Mars-sized object, called Theia, slammed into the proto-Earth more than 4.4 billion years ago, blasting out material that later coalesced into a large satellite as depicted in this artist's illustration. item.dc:creator: Micah Hanks
item.content:encoded:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

For as long as humans have watched the night sky, we have wondered about the moon , pondering everything from its alien appearance to its influence over phenomena on Earth such as ocean tides, climate stability, and even the natural rhythms of many organisms. Among the many questions we have about Earth's lone natural satellite, one remains preeminent: what are the moon's origins , and how long has it orbited Earth? Today, the leading theory among astronomers is that deep in our planet's past — perhaps within roughly the first 100 million years of solar system history — Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours . Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia. The material ejected into orbit by the powerful impact in question would have accumulated afterward, forming the moon that we observe today. What do we know? Birth of a lunar origin hypothesis The evolution of this striking solution to one of the moon's most enduring mysteries goes back to 1946, when geologist Reginald Aldworth Daly was among the first to suggest that an impact event might explain the formation of the moon. Before Daly, scientists had been leaning toward theories that involved Earth's rapid spin billions of years ago, when each day may have at one time lasted as little as 2 or 3 hours . Decades later in the 1970s, researchers William Hartmann and Donald Davis developed their own models involving collisions of large bodies left over from planetary formation, which could collide with younger planets. Building on such ideas, other researchers went on to propose similar scenarios between the early Earth and a Mars-sized object. Early in the following decade, the concept eventually claimed its place as the leading lunar-formation process during a landmark conference held in Kona, Hawaii, in 1984. Earth's moon is thought to have formed when a Mars-sized object, called Theia, slammed into the proto-Earth more than 4.4 billion years ago, blasting out material that later coalesced into a large satellite as depicted in this artist's illustration. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Evidence of a planetary-scale collision The popularity of the giant-impact hypothesis can be attributed to the multiple lines of evidence supporting the impact scenario. For instance, researchers have long recognized the similar stable-isotope ratios between both moon rocks and those from Earth, strongly suggesting a link between their origins. Additionally, the unusually high angular momentum (or spin) of the Earth-moon system, when compared to observations of other rocky planets, also could be explained as one of the effects of a massive collision. Further clues can be found in the moon's composition, which reveals a relatively small iron core and lower density. This is significant to astronomers, since a hypothetical giant impact would have seen the suspected Theia protoplanet's metallic core merging with the young Earth's interior — meanwhile, lighter mantle and crust material from both worlds would have become dislodged and blasted into orbit, eventually helping form the moon. Another important piece of evidence involves the relative depletion of volatile substances (a chemical that easily turns into gas or vapor at room temperatures) in lunar material, which again suggests that it might have been lost during an extremely energetic event, an idea further supported by evidence that the early moon once possessed a substantial magma ocean. Illustration of the young Earth-Moon system. The Earth had recently formed when it was struck by a protoplanet, called Theia, roughly three times the size of Mars. Debris from the impact went into orbit where it quickly coalesced to form the Moon, probably within just a few thousand years. Initially the Earth and moon were much closer together than they are now, and spinning more quickly. In this depiction, debris from the collision continues to rain down on both worlds. (Image credit: Mark Garlick/Science Photo Library/Getty Images) What remains unknown? New research expands on the Theia hypothesis Still, several significant questions remain, including what precise conditions led to the impact, and how the resulting planetary material evolved into the moon as it appears today. Recently, a new study by Adeene Denton of Southwest Research Institute and colleagues at the University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory put a new spin on the Theia hypothesis, suggesting that the suspected ancient impact may have been significantly influenced by the heat and physical strength of the two colliding bodies. The team's findings challenge some long-held views about the giant-impact hypothesis, while lending new support to others. For instance, the team's simulations revealed that while some impacts lead to the creation of a disk of debris that later coalesces into a moon, under other conditions, simulations support the idea that the moon could have been formed in a remarkably short period of time — perhaps within around five hours . However, one of the primary issues with determining the exact conditions of the giant-impact hypothesis involves the ongoing debate over the moon's age. "There is a large controversy regarding the age of the moon," said Dr. Erik Asphaug, a planetary science professor at the University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory and one of the new study's co-authors. Earth sets over the moon's curved limb in this photo captured by the Artemis II crew during their journey around the far side of the moon. (Image credit: NASA) In an email to Space, Asphaug explained some of the issues arising from this, since current estimates place the timing of the moon's formation anywhere from around 40 to 120 million years after the formation of the solar system. Therein lies part of the issue, according to Asphaug, who says this timing could have significant implications for models of the Theia impact. If it had been an earlier collision, Asphaug says this would have involved a hotter Theia due to the greater degree of radiogenic heating; by contrast, a later impact would have meant a cooler and stronger Theia. "I don't think we know enough yet to say the moon (and by corollary, the Earth) formed this way or that way," Asphaug told Space . "But knowing how temperature affects the result opens up a new dimension for viewing the problem, and that is always helpful because it shifts our frame of reference, like getting out of the car to have a walk around." A lunar enigma in time and space For researchers like Asphaug, understanding the moon's formation requires looking at it as more than just an event in space, but also as one in time. Doing so allows comparisons between three different metrics: isotopic decay, temperature-dependent material strength, and the geological record of debris striking other planets — a process through which he believes tighter constraints could be placed on precisely when the moon-forming impact might have occurred. Adeene Denton, the study's lead author, also emphasized the introduction of the time component her team's research brings to the table, telling Space in an email that the outcome of the moon-forming impact could have depended significantly on the timing of the collision. "Before, scientists have generally assumed that the outcome of the collision will be the same regardless of when it takes place," Denton wrote . "But now we know that temperature's effect on material properties, which is dictated by how old and/or cold the proto-Earth and Theia might be, alters things substantially." B

item.title: An Icon Reimagined: Maltina Unveils New Look And Same Nourishing Taste
item.description: Maltina , Nigeria’s pioneering malt brand, has unveiled a new visual identity. The new look celebrates 50 years of nourishment while preserving the trusted taste Nigerians know and love. The new identity presents Maltina through a more contemporary lens across its glass bottles, cans and PET bottles. The brand’s signature orange has been strengthened, while enhanced gold elements create a more distinctive and premium presence on the shelf. New design cues, including the gold crown cork, brighter sunrays, a more prominent golden barley icon, a bolder calcium coin and the “Since 1976” heritage mark, bring Maltina’s story of nourishment and heritage to life. The look may be new, but the nourishing Maltina consumers know and trust remains unchanged. Maltina is fortified with calcium, with one 33cl bottle providing the equivalent of half a glass of milk. The brand is also endorsed by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria as a non-alcoholic drink rich in Vitamin A. “ For 50 years, Maltina has grown alongside generations of Nigerians. This refreshed identity is an evolution of a much-loved brand, designed to keep Maltina fresh, relevant and connected to today’s consumers while preserving the nourishing taste they know and trust, ” said Sarah Agha , Marketing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc . Rather than define the new look for consumers, Maltina is inviting Nigerians to share their own first impressions through the “ What’s Your Word? ” campaign. Across media, retail and consumer experiences, people will be encouraged to look again and describe the refreshed identity in one word. “This relaunch is about more than a new pack. It is an invitation for Nigerians to help shape the next chapter of a brand that has been part of their lives for five decades. We look forward to hearing the words the new Maltina inspires,” Agha added. Consumers will encounter the refreshed packs in stores, restaurants, bars and markets, supported by a nationwide media rollout, trade launches and immersive consumer activations designed to help Nigerians discover and experience the new look. The invitation is simple: experience the new Maltina and tell us what you see. What’s Your Word for the New Maltina? https://maltina.nbplc.com/ . About Maltina Maltina is a non-alcoholic malt drink from Nigerian Breweries Plc. For 50 years, the brand has been part of Nigerian homes and everyday moments, bringing together nourishment, happiness and shared experiences across generations. item.title: Ayra Starr Is Taking Her Starrgirl World Tour to Europe and North America in 2027
item.description: Ayra Starr is set to bring her hit singles to the NFL London Game halftime show on 11th October Ladies and gentlemen, we reckon that cities in Europe, the UK and North America will come alive in purple from January 2027 to April 2027 because the Starrgirl herself, Ayra Starr , has officially announced her grand return to global stages. If you have been keeping up with global music headlines, you already know Oyinkansola Sarah Aderibigbe —famously known across the world as Ayra Starr—is in a league of her own. She recently made history as the very first African artiste to headline an NFL halftime show during the 2026 International Games fixture in London, treating a packed stadium crowd to a performance that cemented Afrobeats on one of sport’s biggest entertainment platforms. Fresh off that landmark milestone and the release of her third studio album, Starrgirl, the Mavin global sensation is packing her bags to take the project on a massive multi-continent run. Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London The upcoming Starrgirl World Tour kicks off its main international leg on 20 January 2027 in Cologne, Germany. From there, Ayra heads to Amsterdam on 21 January, Paris on 24 January, Milan on 27 January, Zurich on 29 January, and Brussels on 31 January. Her UK lovers get their turn on 2 February 2027, when she steps onto the London stage for a night that promises to be an absolute highlight of the winter season. North American fans pick up the excitement starting 18 March 2027 in Houston, Texas. The road trip continues across Dallas, Atlanta, Silver Spring, Boston, Philadelphia, Brooklyn, Chicago, Minneapolis, Denver, and San Francisco, alongside Canadian stops in Toronto and Montreal through early April. If you have been looking for the perfect excuse to hear catalogue favourites alongside fresh hits off her latest project like “ Gimme Dat ,” “ Tornado ,” “ Hot Body ,” and “ Heaven Baby ” live in an arena full of fans singing every word, this is your sign to pack your bags, align your travel dates, and experience the Starrgirl World Tour firsthand. Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. Fresh off that landmark milestone and the release of her third studio album, Starrgirl, the Mavin global sensation is packing her bags to take the project on a massive multi-continent run. Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London The upcoming Starrgirl World Tour kicks off its main international leg on 20 January 2027 in Cologne, Germany. From there, Ayra heads to Amsterdam on 21 January, Paris on 24 January, Milan on 27 January, Zurich on 29 January, and Brussels on 31 January. Her UK lovers get their turn on 2 February 2027, when she steps onto the London stage for a night that promises to be an absolute highlight of the winter season. North American fans pick up the excitement starting 18 March 2027 in Houston, Texas. The road trip continues across Dallas, Atlanta, Silver Spring, Boston, Philadelphia, Brooklyn, Chicago, Minneapolis, Denver, and San Francisco, alongside Canadian stops in Toronto and Montreal through early April. If you have been looking for the perfect excuse to hear catalogue favourites alongside fresh hits off her latest project like “ Gimme Dat ,” “ Tornado ,” “ Hot Body ,” and “ Heaven Baby ” live in an arena full of fans singing every word, this is your sign to pack your bags, align your travel dates, and experience the Starrgirl World Tour firsthand. Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. item.title: Seven Women, Seven Innovations: InnovateNaija’s Role in Nigeria’s Tech Story
item.description: Through the NASENI and AfriLabs-backed InnovateNaija Challenge, seven women brought bold technological ideas to the national stage, and one of them took home the ultimate prize. Their journey shows what is possible when Nigerian women are given the platform, support, and opportunity to build. For years, conversations about Nigeria’s technology ecosystem have centred on the scale of the industry, the growth of startups, and the young people building the next generation of solutions. But there is another part of that story that deserves greater attention: the women building too. Seven women were among the 15 finalists of the InnovateNaija Challenge , a national technology and innovation competition led by the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure ( NASENI ), in partnership with AfriLabs and the Federal Ministry of Youth Development. Coming from different parts of the country and working across diverse fields, these women built solutions that go far beyond the idea of simply participating in technology. They designed, engineered, and developed products responding to real problems in healthcare, agriculture, energy, environmental sustainability, and everyday life. A Historic Victory for Agricultural Hardware The national pitch event, held October 6, 2026 , saw all 15 finalists present physical prototypes before industry experts, global investors, and policymakers. Emerging as the overall grand prize winner of ₦100 million was Abia State innovator Adaeze Ruth Akpagbula , co-founder of Farm Speak , for her PenKeep Smart Poultry Climate Control System . Designed to help farmers manage climate-related challenges across poultry, aquaculture, greenhouse, and smart irrigation systems, PenKeep demonstrates how deep tech can be applied to fundamental agricultural challenges. For Akpagbula, who identified funding, infrastructure, and electricity as major hurdles for hardware innovators in Nigeria, the ₦100 million award will help expand her company’s production capacity and enable the technology to reach more farmers. Innovating Across Every Sector Akpagbula’s top finish was part of a larger showing by female innovators across the competition. Among the seven female finalists was Kemisola Bolarinwa from Ekiti State, whose innovation, the Smart Bra Cup Diagnostic Device , explores the use of technology in breast health. Her work demonstrates how engineering can be directly applied to healthcare challenges that have historically received limited attention. The women of InnovateNaija tackled broad issues across multiple sectors. Elizabeth Chioma Chiketarauba of Imo State developed Torquenova , an electric vehicle and main power generator that can be recharged using an in-built solar-powered system or mains supply, bringing together mobility, energy, and renewable technology. Elizabeth Chioma Chiketarauba of Imo State developed Torquenova , an electric vehicle and main power generator that can be recharged using an in-built solar-powered system or mains supply, bringing together mobility, energy, and renewable technology. Rita Idehai of Edo State developed an Automated Reverse Vending Machine, applying technology to waste management and environmental sustainability. Chinyere Esther Onwumelu of Nasarawa State created a Gas-Level Monitoring and Community Gas Metering System , addressing energy access and accountability. Khadija Adamu Dandad a of Kano State developed the Shepall App , demonstrating the role digital solutions can play in addressing practical everyday needs. Miriam Ashiemar Agbo of Benue State created the Anatsor Integrated Poultry Management System , applying technology to agricultural productivity and livestock management. And Adaeze Ruth Akpagbula of Abia State developed PenKeep , advancing smart poultry climate control and ultimately earning the top spot on the national stage. A Technology Story That Includes Women Their stories matter far beyond the competition itself. Nigeria’s technology sector needs innovators who can identify problems, build solutions, and take concepts from an idea to a tangible product. item.title: Stratospheric airship flew from US to Japan to test sky cell tower concept
item.description: Nearly 100 years after the dirigible Graf Zeppelin made the first nonstop airship journey across the Pacific Ocean, another airship has successfully completed a round-trip flight from New Mexico to Japan and back. But the significance of this modern feat was less about the journey's length and more about its purpose: demonstrating how a lighter-than-air platform can act as a cell phone tower in the sky. The trans-Pacific flight that took place over a month between August and September 2026 was the most notable milestone yet for Sceye, a US aerospace company based near Albuquerque, New Mexico. Sceye has developed an uncrewed platform filled with helium for buoyancy and equipped with an electric-powered propeller for active propulsion, allowing it to resist most strong winds and keep hovering over the same location for long periods. The platform also uses top-mounted solar panels and onboard batteries to stay powered for stratospheric operations around the clock. “We can stay over an area of operation, and we do that in the stratosphere right around 60,000 feet, so we're twice as high as air traffic and we're above the jet stream, and yet 30 times closer than low-Earth orbit satellites,” Mikkel Frandsen , founder and CEO of Sceye, told Ars. “We can fly through day and night until the sun comes up the next morning and recharges the batteries, at which point we're still at the same altitude and still over the same area of operation.” Read full article Comments

item.title: 5 New Music Videos You Need to Watch This Week: Victony, Tyla, Phyno & More
item.description: Nigerian singer-songwriter Victony wearing a glossy leather outfit on set during the production of the SLICK Remix, featuring American stars Don Toliver and Summer Walker, off his sophomore album STARLIFE. A new week calls for fresh music, and there’s plenty to add to your watchlist. From Victony bringing Don Toliver and Summer Walker into the mix for the “ SLICK ” remix to Tyla ’s dance-ready “ That Girl ” and Phyno ’s romantic “Beautiful”, there’s something for every mood. We’re also looking back at Ayra Starr ’s performance at the 2026 NFL international halftime show and making room for Anendlessocean ’s reflective “ Promises ”. Here are five music releases and performances to check out this week. Victony: “SLICK (Remix)” ft. Don Toliver & Summer Walker Victony has given “SLICK” a new twist, and this time, he’s brought Don Toliver and Summer Walker along for the ride. The original track appears on his sophomore album, STARLIFE, while the remix introduces a fresh mix of R&B vocals and melodies. With three artistes bringing their different sounds to the same record, there’s plenty to enjoy here. Tyla: “That Girl” If you’re looking for something to get you moving, Tyla has you covered with “That Girl” from her project A*Pop. The song draws on South Africa’s popular Phara Walk dance culture, pairing catchy rhythms with Tyla’s smooth vocals. It’s playful, danceable and one you might find yourself returning to throughout the week. Anendlessocean: “Promises” Anendlessocean offers a place for reflection, gratitude and rest with “Promises”. Rooted in faith and the assurance that God will come through again, the song invites listeners to pause, reflect and find comfort in the belief that He will do it again. It’s one to turn to when you need a little reminder to trust the journey. Phyno: “Beautiful” Ezege is back with “Beautiful”, a love letter to the woman who makes everything make sense. Smooth, heartfelt and unmistakably Phyno, the track blends Igbo, Pidgin and English over a melody made for the ones you hold close. Taken from his project Let That Sink In (LTSI), the song celebrates love in a way that feels personal and familiar. The official music video features actress and media personality Nancy Isime, giving the romantic track a visual companion. Ayra Starr: 2026 NFL Halftime Performance Ayra Starr took Afrobeats to the NFL international stage on 11 October, headlining the halftime show during the Philadelphia Eagles vs Jacksonville Jaguars game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. She opened her set with “Heaven Baby”, her collaboration with ZAYN, before performing “Santa”, “Rush” and “Dangerous”, and closing with a medley of “Hot Body” and “Ms. Paper”. The performance marked a major milestone for the Nigerian star, who became the first African artiste to headline an NFL International Games halftime show. item.title: Watch Japan launch a bold sample-return mission to Mars moon Phobos today
item.description: null Editor's note: Japan launched its bold MMX sample-return mission to the Mars moon Phobos on Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT). Watch a replay of the liftoff and read our launch story here. Japan will launch an epic mission to Mars today (Oct. 19), and you can watch the action live. The Martian Moons eXploration ( MMX ) mission is scheduled to lift off atop an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center today at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. on Oct. 20 local Japan time). You can watch it live via the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Coverage will begin at 2:45 p.m. EDT (1845 GMT). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background. (Image credit: JAXA) As its full name suggests, MMX will focus on Mars ' two moons, Phobos and Deimos . They're both tiny compared to Earth's own moon; Phobos is just 14 miles (22 kilometers) wide, and Deimos is even smaller, with a diameter of about 8 miles (13 km). They're also quite mysterious. While astronomers have a pretty clear understanding of our own moon's birth — it coalesced from material blasted into space when a Mars-sized planet slammed into Earth long ago — there's no consensus about Phobos and Deimos' origin story. The duo "may be the remains of a massive impact on Mars that sent material into orbit around the planet, or they could be ancient asteroids that were captured by Mars' gravity billions of years ago," Tom Statler, MMX program executive and program scientist at NASA Headquarters, said in an Oct. 15 statement . (NASA is a partner on the mission, providing a scientific instrument, a technology demonstration, communication support and funding for American scientists on the MMX team.) "Having the answer will help illuminate that early era when Earth and the other inner planets may have been acquiring much of their water and organic compounds," Statler added. MMX will help provide that answer, if all goes according to plan. The spacecraft will arrive in the Mars system in August 2027, then slip into orbit around Phobos a month later. It will study that moon and Deimos from a distance for about 18 months, then deploy the French-German Idefix rover onto Phobos' surface in early 2029. The 55-pound (25 kilograms) Idefix "has two main tasks: providing information to prepare for the landing of the main spacecraft to collect samples, and analyzing the composition and texture of Phobos' surface," European Space Agency officials wrote in an MMX mission description . "The gravity on Phobos is so low that Idefix will only weigh the equivalent of 15 grams [0.5 ounces] on its surface!" they added. The MMX mothership's Phobos landing will occur in 2030. The spacecraft will grab at least 10 grams (0.4 ounces) of samples from the moon, then head back toward Earth with this extraterrestrial bounty. item.content:encoded: null Editor's note: Japan launched its bold MMX sample-return mission to the Mars moon Phobos on Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT). Watch a replay of the liftoff and read our launch story here. Japan will launch an epic mission to Mars today (Oct. 19), and you can watch the action live. The Martian Moons eXploration ( MMX ) mission is scheduled to lift off atop an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center today at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. on Oct. 20 local Japan time). The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background. (Image credit: JAXA) As its full name suggests, MMX will focus on Mars ' two moons, Phobos and Deimos . They're both tiny compared to Earth's own moon; Phobos is just 14 miles (22 kilometers) wide, and Deimos is even smaller, with a diameter of about 8 miles (13 km). They're also quite mysterious. The duo "may be the remains of a massive impact on Mars that sent material into orbit around the planet, or they could be ancient asteroids that were captured by Mars' gravity billions of years ago," Tom Statler, MMX program executive and program scientist at NASA Headquarters, said in an Oct. 15 statement . (NASA is a partner on the mission, providing a scientific instrument, a technology demonstration, communication support and funding for American scientists on the MMX team.) "Having the answer will help illuminate that early era when Earth and the other inner planets may have been acquiring much of their water and organic compounds," Statler added. MMX will help provide that answer, if all goes according to plan. The spacecraft will arrive in the Mars system in August 2027, then slip into orbit around Phobos a month later. It will study that moon and Deimos from a distance for about 18 months, then deploy the French-German Idefix rover onto Phobos' surface in early 2029. The 55-pound (25 kilograms) Idefix "has two main tasks: providing information to prepare for the landing of the main spacecraft to collect samples, and analyzing the composition and texture of Phobos' surface," European Space Agency officials wrote in an MMX mission description . "The gravity on Phobos is so low that Idefix will only weigh the equivalent of 15 grams [0.5 ounces] on its surface!" they added. The MMX mothership's Phobos landing will occur in 2030. The spacecraft will grab at least 10 grams (0.4 ounces) of samples from the moon, then head back toward Earth with this extraterrestrial bounty. MMX's return capsule will land here in 2031, after which scientists around the world will scrutinize the Phobos sample for clues about the history and evolution of Mars and our solar system more broadly. Engineers conduct a thermal vacuum test with JAXA's MMX Mars moon sample-return spacecraft. JAXA posted this image on X on May 15, 2025. (Image credit: JAXA) MMX was originally supposed to launch in 2024, but issues with the H3 rocket prevented it from doing so. Mars and Earth align properly for interplanetary launches just once every 26 months, so MMX had to wait a while for its next chance. Japan already has an impressive sample-return track record. The country's Hayabusa mission brought home pieces of the asteroid Itokawa in 2010, for example, and Hayabusa2 did the same with material from the space rock Ryugu a decade later.

item.title: The one change that worked: I deleted Instagram – and embraced the joys of a truly private life
item.description: I’d become obsessed with appealing to my invisible audience. But since I ditched the app a year ago, my quieter moments have taken on brilliant new meaning I first downloaded Instagram when I was 17 and became hooked on it the way most people fall in love: slowly, and then all at once. For a long time, I never considered myself a social media addict. I self-righteously refused to download TikTok, declared Snapchat to be for “children”, and posted less regularly on Instagram than half of the people I followed. As I went through my university years, however, certain changes crept up on me. I began to swap reading – or essay-writing – for hours spent curating new posts. On my way home from lectures (or later, from my work as a journalist), I would spend ages trying to take the artsiest, most perfect picture of that evening’s sunset for my story – as if the people who followed me were eagerly awaiting yet another photo of one of the Earth’s rotations. What usually followed was a night of reloading my feed to see how many people had reacted to my post – or worse, hadn’t reacted at all. Continue reading...

item.title: APOD: 2026 October 19 – Treble Clef: Unusual X-ray Hot Radio Source
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 19 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Treble Clef: Unusual X-ray Hot Radio Source Explanation: Explanation : What is Treble Clef? This unusual radio structure extends over 2 million light-years and resembles a common musical symbol — but has its visible light hidden by our own Milky Way Galaxy . Examined in 2004, the nature of VLSS J0318.9+5755, dubbed Treble Clef , remained unknown. Recent observations by the Chandra X-ray Observatory and eROSITA , however, have led to the hypothesis that the Treble Clef central cloud of charged particles was originally expelled by a supermassive black hole at the center of a galaxy. After the radio emission from those particles faded, they may have been reinvigorated by a shock wave from the collision of two clusters of galaxies . The featured composite image shows radio emission in red, while recently discovered X-rays are shown in blue. Unusual objects like Treble Clef give humanity unexpected clues about how whole clusters of galaxies interact as well as the general evolution of our universe . item.title: Kylie Minogue songs already used to train AI as tech firms ‘strong-arm’ Australian government, music body warns
item.description: Of the dozens of countries approached to water down their laws, Australia appears to be the only one considering it, publishers’ group says Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast AI has already been trained on the works of Australian artists including Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave without compensation, the peak global body for music rights has claimed, as the Australian government has been warned against giving in to “strong-arming” from tech companies seeking to weaken copyright law. The International Confederation of Music Publishers (ICMP) – which represents Sony, Warner and Universal as well as thousands of independent publishers on six continents – has warned that of the dozens of countries approached to water down copyright laws, Australia appears to be the only to consider doing so. Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Returning the first samples from a Martian moon: Inside the science of Japan's bold MMX mission to Mars
item.description: null Editor's note: Japan launched its bold MMX sample-return mission to the Mars moon Phobos on Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT). Watch a replay of the liftoff and read our launch story here. Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. MMX launched on an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center on Monday (Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan, Oct. 20). After a 10-month journey to reach Mars, the spacecraft will spend about three years studying Phobos, deploying a rover and landing to collect its samples. The mission will then shift its focus to Deimos for a series of flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule is scheduled to land in Australia in 2031. The spacecraft The MMX spacecraft is comprised of three main parts, as well as a small rover. After release from its H3 launch vehicle, a propulsion module will provide the boost to put MMX on course for Mars. MMX's main exploration module carries the microwave-size IDEFIX rover and most of the mission's scientific instruments, while the return module houses the sample-return capsule. Japan's Mitsubishi Electric built MMX's three main modules, with the French space agency CNES (Centre National d'Études Spatiales) and Germany's DLR (Deutsches Zentrum für Luft-und Raumfahrt) jointly developing IDEFIX . The little rover is named for a dog in the 1960s French comic "Asterix," in a nod to the country's first satellite , Astérix, which launched in 1965. IDEFIX carries a suite of cameras, as well as the Raman Spectrometer for MMX (RAX) and miniaturized radiometer (miniRAD) instruments to analyze Phobos' surface composition and temperature. The Propulsion Module (left) and Exploration and Return Modules (right), which together make up Japan’s Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft, are seen at the Tanegashima Space Center in Minamitane, Kagoshima prefecture on Aug. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Yuichi YAMAZAKI / AFP via Getty Images)) Most of MMX's scientific instruments are housed on the exploration module, like NASA's Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE, pronounced "meh-gah-nay") device, a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer built by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL), and France's MIRS (MMX InfraRed Spectrometer) instrument.
